instruction: I'm looking for career advice. I want to find a new job, but I'm not sure what I want to do.
reply: Talk about the work you want to be better at, not a job title you have decided on: "I want to be the person who runs these projects, so I am looking for a place I can learn the whole cycle." One sentence on what you are doing now to get there - a course, a piece of work you put your hand up for - and stop. Never name their manager's job, and never say you want to be doing something else entirely.

instruction: I'm planning to cook dinner for my family tonight, do you have any easy recipe suggestions?
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: What's the weather like today?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: What is a billion?
reply: Cardiff has about 370,000 people, and about 1.1 million in the wider south Wales area.

instruction: I'm going to a music festival this weekend. What are some basic safety tips I should know?
reply: Nothing new on race day: the socks and shoes you did your long runs in, and dress for ten minutes in - a thin wicking base layer, a warm thin layer over it and a windproof shell you can tie round your waist, a cap for rain or sun, gloves for the first two miles and a waterproof jacket if it is really coming down, because you warm up two or three miles in and one layer fewer than feels right at the door is usually the right count. Vaseline on the nipples and inner thighs, safety pins for the number, a dry top and a bin liner for your bag at the finish, and a warm layer to pull on within ten minutes of stopping, which is when the cold really lands.

instruction: I'm learning about climate zones in school and I was wondering, what are the main types of climate zones?
reply: A biome is a large region with one climate and the plants and animals that go with it: rainforest, desert, grassland, tundra, coral reef. The same biome turns up on different continents, because it is the climate that decides it.

instruction: I have allergies and I'm wondering what season is usually the worst for allergies.
reply: Hay fever is an allergy to pollen - sneezing, itchy eyes and a runny nose, no temperature, and it comes back at the same time each year. A cold is an infection: a sore throat first, then a blocked nose, gone in about a week.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school and I was wondering, what is a pulley?
reply: A pulley is a wheel with a rope running over it: one changes the direction of a pull, so you pull down to lift a load up, and two together halve the force you need by doubling the rope. That is why a flagpole and a crane both use one.

instruction: I'm redecorating my living room and I'm looking for some color scheme ideas.
reply: Pick the thing you cannot change - the floor, the tiles, the worktop, the sofa - and take the wall colour out of it in a paler version of itself. Then add one deeper tone from the same family for a rug or cushions and a wood or a metal to warm it: three colours, one of them a near-neutral.

instruction: I'm looking for something fun to do this summer. What amusement parks are near me?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm looking for some new smoothie ideas. What are some popular fruits to use in smoothies?
reply: Fruit juice has as much sugar as the equivalent amount of Coke - about 20g in a 200ml glass of orange juice - with none of the fibre of the fruit and none of the chewing that makes you feel full. One small glass a day with a meal is the usual advice; a smoothie is not much better once the fruit is blended.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something to do in my free time. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm learning about adaptation in nature. What is mimicry?
reply: Living things vary, and the ones whose variations suit their surroundings tend to survive and pass those variations on. Over many generations that selection changes the population: small changes accumulate into new species.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school, and I was wondering what adaptation means.
reply: Plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil into sugar, which is their food, and they release oxygen as a by-product. The green chlorophyll in their leaves captures the light that powers it.

instruction: I'm planning meals for my family this week. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I'm curious about body language. Can you tell me what crossed arms usually mean?
reply: Handball is when the ball touches the arm below where the armpit ends: the shoulder and the very top of the arm are fine. It also counts when the arm makes the body bigger, even by accident — which is why defenders tuck their arms behind their backs in the box.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night because of the noise in my neighborhood. What can I do to block out the noise?
reply: A steady, even sound covers the small noises - a door, a stair, a cough - that wake a light sleeper, so it helps most in a shared or noisy room rather than instead of a bedtime routine. Keep it low: quieter than a shower, about the level of a quiet conversation, and an arm's length or more from the cot or the head of the bed.

instruction: My phone's screen is cracked. Can I fix it myself?
reply: A scratch in the glass will not polish out, and toothpaste or a jeweller's rouge only turns one line into a hazy patch. Leave a shallow scratch, put a tempered-glass screen protector over it to hide it and stop it spreading, and for a phone price the glass replacement at a local repair shop first - it is usually £30 to £60 and a protector on the new screen is cheaper than a second repair.

instruction: I'm planning to cook dinner for some friends tonight and I want to impress them with the presentation. Do you have any tips?
reply: Arrive early, when it is easier to join a small group, and ask people about the thing you are both already at: how they know the host, what they thought of the food. Have three open questions ready and let the other person do most of the talking.

instruction: I'm thinking of traveling abroad and I want to do something meaningful. What is volunteer travel?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm learning about forces in school and I'm having a bit of trouble understanding Newton's laws of motion. Can you explain the first law to me?
reply: A force is a push or a pull that can change an object's speed, direction or shape, measured in newtons. Gravity, friction and the push of a hand are all forces, and an object with no net force keeps doing what it was doing.

instruction: I'm worried about how social media affects my mental health. Is social media bad for you?
reply: It isn't dangerous, but the light and the story keep your brain alert, so you fall asleep later and wake more in the night. If you need something playing, a podcast or radio set to sleep is easier on sleep than a screen.

instruction: I'm worried about home safety. What are some basic things I can do to prepare for emergencies?
reply: Decide in advance what you will do and how long you will stay, and tell people early so nobody is surprised on the day. Have one safe topic and one exit ready ('we need to get the little one home'), and step outside for ten minutes when it heats up.

instruction: I'm going to graduate soon and I was wondering, what's the significance of turning the tassel during the graduation ceremony?
reply: A godparent is a spare adult for the child: someone who takes an interest in them for years, remembers birthdays, and is there if the parents cannot be. At the christening you stand at the font with the parents, say the promises with them, and get named in the register.

instruction: I'm having trouble meeting my deadlines at work. What are some common factors that affect job performance?
reply: It means leaving almost no time to spare. What is the deadline?

instruction: What is HTTP?
reply: URL stands for uniform resource locator: the address that says where a page lives and how to fetch it. The https at the front is the how - it asks for the encrypted version - and the part after the first single slash is the site, so a link with a lot of nonsense after it usually still works with the nonsense cut off.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you have any bedtime routine suggestions?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: What is a pencil used for?
reply: The tip is a tiny ball in a socket, and the ink behind it is thick enough that it only runs when the ball rolls it onto the paper - which is why a pen works upside down and why the line stops when the ball dries out. The ink is oil based, so it dries on the paper fast but smears if you write over it while it is still wet.

instruction: I want to spend more quality time with my parents, but I don't know where to start.
reply: Ask other parents at the school gate first: a sitter vouched for by someone you know beats any app. Then do one evening while you are still in the house, paying them to play while you get on with something, so the first real night out isn't the first time.

instruction: I'm worried about my dog's weight. He's been gaining a lot lately.
reply: A dog that loses weight on the same food needs the vet: worms, bad teeth, kidney or liver trouble, diabetes and an overactive thyroid are the usual causes, and some cancers start that way. Weigh him now, take the number with you, and go this week - a dog should not get thin on a full bowl.

instruction: I'm a bit worried about the weather forecast. Is a thunderstorm expected today?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow. What should I do to prepare?
reply: Book the check-up and say on the phone that you are nervous and have not been for a while - practices hear it every week, and most will give you a longer first appointment, a signal to stop, and no lecture. The first visit is usually a look round and an x-ray, nothing more, and you can agree to one small thing at a time.

instruction: I'm interested in board games. What are some popular ones?
reply: *Dobble*, *UNO* and *Snakes and Ladders* work for a range of ages, and *Catan Junior* if they are ready for a proper board game. For a rainy afternoon, a treasure hunt round the house costs nothing and takes the longest.

instruction: I've been feeling really stressed out lately and I'm not sure how to manage it.
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move.

instruction: I'm planning a graduation party for my sister. What are some common graduation traditions?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I'm looking for educational apps for my kids. Can you suggest some?
reply: Help them shrink it to one question they can answer on a page - not the whole subject, but one thing about it - then one page of notes from one book or site, in their own words. A project is marked on the child's reading and thinking, so doing it for them shows in the writing and they learn nothing: sit beside them, ask what they already know, and hand back the pen.

instruction: I'm planning a camping trip and I need to find a campsite. Can you help me?
reply: A tent and bags for everyone, plus what small children need on a campsite: a mat each, because they feel every root, warm layers and a hat for the night even in July, and a full change of clothes kept in the car so a wet sleeping bag is not the end of the trip. Take a torch each, wet wipes, a bin bag for wet things, breakfast that needs no cooking, and something to do after dark.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier, but I love pizza. Are there any healthier alternatives to regular pizza?
reply: Heat the oven as high as it goes with a heavy tray or a pizza stone inside, then slide the pizza onto the hot tray and give it 8 to 12 minutes, until the edge blisters and the underside is crisp: a thin base and a preheated surface do what an oven alone will not. Keep the toppings light, because too much sauce or cheese steams the middle.

instruction: I'm learning about chemistry in school, and I was wondering what a chemical reaction is.
reply: A chemical reaction is when substances rearrange their atoms to make new ones: bonds break, new bonds form, and the starting materials are used up. Burning, rusting, baking and digestion are all reactions, and they usually give out or take in heat.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. What's popular on streaming services right now?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm worried about my social media usage. Is it normal to spend 3 hours a day on social media?
reply: The phone already counts it: Settings > Mobile data on an iPhone, or Settings > Network > Data usage on Android, shows the month's total and which apps are eating it. Video and social apps are nearly always the top two, and turning off background refresh and auto-play on mobile data usually halves it.

instruction: I'm going to the train station. What time does the next train to New York leave?
reply: For a night before an early flight, book an airport hotel with a shuttle and check the first and last shuttle times before you pay - a 4am shuttle that stops at 11pm is the usual trap, and so is a "5 minutes from the terminal" that is five minutes by car on a road with no pavement. A town two or three stops away on the train, or a park-and-fly with the transfer included, is usually about half the price; add up the transfer, the parking and the extra hour and pick on the total.

instruction: I'm a big sports fan. What local teams do we have in my area?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I want to cook healthier meals, but I don't know where to start. Can you suggest some nutritious ingredient swaps?
reply: Cook the same sort of dinner as for anyone, with the starchy part smaller and the vegetables bigger: chicken or fish with two veg, a chilli with beans instead of rice, or an omelette and salad. Halve the potatoes, rice or pasta rather than cutting them out, go wholegrain where you can, skip the sugary drinks, and keep pudding small - and ask them what they usually do rather than guessing.

instruction: I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow and I'm not sure if my insurance covers it.
reply: Only if your own policy says so. Many comprehensive policies give 'driving other cars' cover, but it is usually third party only, often limited to drivers over 25, and some policies have dropped it altogether, so check the certificate before you drive.

instruction: I'm going on a trip to Japan soon and I want to take some great photos to share on social media.
reply: In the email app tap the attach or paperclip icon, pick Photos and choose the picture; a phone usually offers a size and Small or Medium is plenty for a snapshot. Most services stop at about 20 to 25MB, so for several photos send a link from Google Photos or iCloud instead of attaching them.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting some smart home devices. What are some popular options?
reply: iPhone if you want the long updates and everything to talk to the rest of the family's; Android if you want to spend less, get two days of battery, or keep a headphone jack. The cheapest way in is a two-year-old iPhone or a mid-range Samsung, and both last well if you put a case on them.

instruction: I'm having trouble with measurements in my recipe. What's the difference between a pinch and a dash?
reply: A pinch is what you can hold between your thumb and finger: about 1/16 of a teaspoon, a little under half a gram of salt, and a good pinch nearer one. A dash of liquid is about 1/8 of a teaspoon, and a handful is 30 to 40g.

instruction: Our school is having a talent show next week. What kind of acts do you think would be good for it?
reply: Give each one a reason to be pleased to meet the other - "Sam, this is Priya, she runs the same ridiculous hill route as you" - and then give them something to do with each other, even a question you are also part of. Say a little about what each does so nobody has to audition, and stay for the first few minutes rather than leaving them alone.

instruction: I'm learning about food chains in school. What is a food chain?
reply: A food chain is the line of who eats whom, starting with a plant that makes its own food and ending with a predator. Energy is lost at every step, which is why top predators are few and a chain rarely has more than four or five links.

instruction: My little brother swallowed some soap. What should I do?
reply: Into the back of the mouth rather than the food if he spits it out: hold the head gently up, drop the tablet past the hump of the tongue, close the mouth and rub the throat or blow on his nose until he swallows, then give water or a treat so it doesn't stick. Pate, cheese or a pill pocket hides most of them, and ask the vet for a liquid or a spot-on if a cat fights the tablets.

instruction: I'm looking for a new sweatshirt. What's popular right now?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm a new homeowner and I'm not sure what I should be doing to take care of my electrical system.
reply: On the first night you need the bed made, toilet roll, a kettle, mugs, a torch and chargers in one labelled box. Photograph the gas and electricity meters when you arrive, and find the stopcock and fuse box before you need them.

instruction: I'm taking my dog to the vet for a check-up. What can I expect during the visit?
reply: Ask the vet for a nurse appointment and wait in the car until it's your turn, then feed him treats in the waiting room without letting other dogs crowd him. Ask them to crouch down and examine him on the floor, and go in for a free weigh-in every few weeks so most visits are boring: a dog who has been in four times for nothing is a much easier patient.

instruction: I'm having trouble understanding the difference between accuracy and precision in measurement. Can you explain it to me?
reply: A decimal is a way of writing a number using place values for tenths, hundredths and so on, with a point after the units: 0.75 means seven tenths and five hundredths, which is the same as 3/4. The digits after the point tell you the place value, so 0.5 is five tenths and 0.05 is five hundredths.

instruction: I'm going to take the train to visit my family. Is train travel safe?
reply: It's genuinely a safe way to travel, and the first flight is mostly boring: check in, security, wait, board, sit. Tell the cabin crew it's your first time if you're nervous; they're used to it and always look after you.

instruction: I'm looking for some new fashion brands to check out. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm looking for a new pair of casual shoes, do you have any suggestions?
reply: For work, four things decide it: the fabric, the rise, the length and the pockets. A wool-poly blend or a cotton twill with a little stretch creases less and gives when you sit and stand; a mid rise that sits at the waist stays put through a shift; and the hem should break once on the shoe, so buy the length that fits you - short and petite lengths are sold off the rail and cost no more than a tailor.

instruction: I'm new to the city and I'm going to be taking the subway a lot. What are some basic rules I should know?
reply: Tickets first, with a screenshot as well as the app, because signal in a tunnel is not a plan. Then water and a snack, a layer you can take off, a charger and headphones, and your seat reservation if you have one.

instruction: I'm thinking about adopting a pet for my family. What are some popular family pets?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I'm learning about latitude and longitude in school. What is latitude?
reply: Latitude is how far north or south of the equator a place is, in degrees from 0 at the equator to 90 at the poles: London is about 51 north, and your latitude is what sets how long the days are and how warm the place gets.

instruction: What is light?
reply: Light is a form of energy that travels as a wave and also as particles called photons, at about 300,000 km a second in a vacuum. It carries colour, lets us see, and is only a tiny part of the electromagnetic spectrum.

instruction: I'm going to the mall this weekend and I'm not sure where to find the food court.
reply: A pantry or larder is a cool, dark, dry cupboard for the food that keeps: tins, dried pasta and rice, flour, sugar, oil, spices. Cool and dry matter more than size - a shelf by a radiator or a sunny window turns flour and rice stale and brings weevils - so put it on an outside wall away from the cooker.

instruction: I'm looking for some information about pet grooming tools.
reply: Brush for a few minutes a day, working the small knots out with your fingers before the brush touches them so it never pulls: a slicker brush for a short coat, an undercoat rake for a double coat. Do not shave a double coat, because it is his insulation in hot weather as well as cold.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my home's heating and cooling system. What are some basic things I can do to maintain it?
reply: Usually one of four things, and the cheap checks come first. Feel the radiator in the cold room: cold at the top is air, so bleed it; hot at the top and cold at the bottom is sludge; and a thermostatic valve turned right down or stuck shut does the same.

instruction: I have a problem with aphids in my garden. What can I do to get rid of them?
reply: Rub them off with your fingers or a strong jet of water, then spray with soapy water - a teaspoon of washing-up liquid in a litre, sprayed under the leaves in the evening - and repeat every three days for a fortnight, because the eggs keep hatching. Check for ants running up the stem: they farm the aphids and keep them there, so a sticky band round the pot stops the supply line.

instruction: I'm looking for information about the latest fashion trends. What's popular on the runways right now?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm going to the city for work and I was wondering about the subway schedule.
reply: Ask work first, then price the journey three ways before you buy anything: a season ticket only beats weekly or daily tickets above about three days a week, a flexi ticket or a carnet covers two or three days, and a railcard pays for itself in about a dozen trips if you qualify for one. If you drive, park and ride, a lift-share board or a parking space a ten-minute walk out usually undercuts the station car park, and asking whether your employer does a season ticket loan or a cycle-to-work scheme is free money in effect.

instruction: I'm looking for some information about family traditions. What are some common family traditions around the holidays?
reply: Small things they can use lying in bed: a long phone cable and a charged power bank, earphones, a puzzle book or a magazine, a decent lip balm, a light blanket, or a printed photo of the family to put on the locker. Skip flowers on most wards and skip food unless you know the diet.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Africa for wildlife photography. What's the best time to visit?
reply: In a British city park in winter you'll usually see robins, blackbirds, blue tits, great tits, pigeons, crows and magpies, with gulls and starlings on the grass. Look in the bushes and bare trees rather than the open lawn, and early morning is the busiest time.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about private aviation. What is the main advantage of flying privately?
reply: It's genuinely a safe way to travel, and the first flight is mostly boring: check in, security, wait, board, sit. Tell the cabin crew it's your first time if you're nervous; they're used to it and always look after you.

instruction: I'm looking for information about airline tickets.
reply: Go straight to the airline's desk or app before the next one closes: when both legs are on one ticket the airline has to put you on the next available seat, and pay for a hotel and meals if the wait is overnight. On two separate tickets the second one is a no-show and nobody owes you a seat, so ring that airline and ask anyway.

instruction: I'm learning about geology in school and I was wondering, what's the geological time scale?
reply: The Earth is about 4.54 billion years old, worked out from meteorites and the oldest rocks. Life got going within the first billion years, and everything humans have done fits into the last tiny sliver of that time.

instruction: I want to start running, but I'm not sure how to get started. What's the most important thing to do first?
reply: Start with run-walk: three minutes of easy running, two minutes of walking, five times, three days a week, and add a minute of running each week. Build up for six weeks before you add speed, keep every run slow enough to talk, and expect the first fortnight to feel harder than it looks.

instruction: I'm looking for a new movie to watch. What are some popular movies right now?
reply: *Arrival* is the smartest one, *Apollo 13* the most tense, and *Interstellar* the biggest. For something lighter, *Galaxy Quest* is a lovely comedy about actors on a spaceship.

instruction: I'm a little worried about my cat. She's been acting weird lately and I don't know what's wrong.
reply: Cats show affection on their own terms, and the way to be chosen is to stop reaching: sit on the floor, play with a wand toy for five minutes twice a day, and let her come to you and walk away again without being picked up. Offer a finger to sniff, blink slowly at her and look away, and put a treat down rather than holding it out.

instruction: I love sunshine, do you know what the sunniest place on earth is?
reply: Charged particles from the sun hit gases high in the atmosphere and make them glow: green from oxygen, reds and purples from nitrogen. You need a dark, clear night and a high latitude, so northern Scotland, Iceland and Scandinavia are the usual spots.

instruction: I'm having trouble getting my kids to bed on time. Do you have any tips for creating a sleep schedule for families?
reply: Match it to the age first: a one year old is ready at 6.30 to 7.30pm and needs 11 to 14 hours out of 24, two to five year olds 6.30 to 8pm with 10 to 13 hours, five to eight 7 to 8pm with 9 to 12. Then shift it 15 minutes every three or four nights rather than all at once, and keep the wake-up time fixed: the morning light is what sets the body clock, so open the curtains straight away and get outside before school.

instruction: I'm looking for some healthy recipes to try. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Cheese, chutney and an apple; cream cheese with smoked salmon or cucumber; hummus and something crunchy; butter and a sliced boiled egg with salt and pepper. Anything soft wants something crisp on it, and anything dry wants something wet.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What are some good foods for breakfast?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What are some nutritious foods I should include in my diet?
reply: Aim for a palm-sized portion of protein at each meal - eggs, milk or yoghurt at breakfast, beans, lentils or chicken at lunch, fish or mince at dinner - which lands most adults near the 0.75g per kilo of body weight they need. Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, tinned fish, eggs, tofu and lentils are the cheapest ways to add it.

instruction: I'm thinking of upgrading my home with some smart devices. What's the benefit of smart lighting?
reply: A smart plug goes between the socket and the thing, and you switch it from an app or by voice; it is the cheapest way to make a lamp, a fan or a Christmas tree smart. Check it is rated for what you plug in (13A for a heater, and never for anything that must not be cut off, like an iron or an electric blanket) and that it works with what you already have, Alexa or Google or Apple Home.

instruction: I'm learning about ecosystems in school, and I'm a bit confused about food chains and food webs. What's the difference between them?
reply: A food chain is the line of who eats whom, starting with a plant that makes its own food and ending with a predator. Energy is lost at every step, which is why top predators are few and a chain rarely has more than four or five links.

instruction: I'm curious about time in physics. What is time?
reply: Time zones exist because the Earth turns: noon is when the Sun is highest, and that happens at a different moment in each place. The world is split into 24 zones of about an hour, so the clock roughly matches daylight; some countries bend the borders or use half-hour zones.

instruction: I'm looking for a new webcam for video calls. What's a good brand?
reply: Spend on the battery and the update years, not the camera: a mid-range phone at £250 to £400 lasts as long as a flagship if the maker promises four or five years of security updates (Samsung, Google and Apple do; many cheap brands promise two). Get at least 128GB, check the battery is 5,000mAh or more, and make sure it takes a physical SIM as well as an eSIM if you travel.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan from the US. What's the typical flight duration?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm looking for a gift for my sister's birthday. Do you have any gift ideas?
reply: Make the gift something you do together: a picnic at the spot of your first date, a small photo book of the year, or a jar of twelve notes with one to open each month. The thought shows in the specifics, not the price.

instruction: I'm looking for a new laptop, but I'm not sure which brand to choose. What's the difference between Dell and HP?
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm going to the beach tomorrow. What's the weather going to be like?
reply: Go by the forecast for the hours you will actually be out rather than for the whole day, and dress for the coldest and wettest of those hours. As a rule of thumb: under about 10 degrees a proper coat, between 10 and 18 a jumper with something windproof over it, over 18 no coat and loose cotton instead.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I'm looking for ways to relax. I've heard yoga can help.
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move.

instruction: I'm having trouble studying for my exams and I was wondering if you had any tips.
reply: Make the first session tiny and today: open the topic list, pick the one you know least, and test yourself on it for ten minutes, because starting is the part that is failing rather than the studying. Then put three short sessions in the week you actually have, each ending with a self-test instead of a reread, and give each one a stopping time so it cannot drift to midnight.

instruction: I'm looking for a job in retail. What are some common job categories?
reply: Look for the places that sell a lot of one thing: a market hall or a food court, a bakery, a cafe at the back of a shop, a street food van in a regular spot, or the lunch board outside a restaurant that wants the office trade. Walk a street back from the station or the main road, where the rents are lower, and follow the queue of people who work nearby.

instruction: I like arts and music, what are some popular dance forms?
reply: Wear what you can dance in for hours and don't have to hold: dark jeans or a dress with shoes you can stand in. Check the club's own rules first, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my math homework. Can you help me?
reply: Underline what the question actually asks, then write down the numbers it gives you and what units they are in. Guess the answer roughly before calculating - if your working is far off the guess, the sum is wrong, not the guess.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What are some common sleep aids?
reply: The things that work: same wake-up time every day, no caffeine after early afternoon, not much alcohol in the evening (it wakes you in the second half of the night), a cool dark room, and getting out of bed if you're awake for more than 20 minutes. Screens off half an hour before bed and a short walk most days help more than any app.

instruction: I'm looking for a new cocktail dress for an upcoming event. What styles are popular right now?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: What is the speed of sound?
reply: Sound is a vibration that travels as a wave through air, water or solids; in air it moves at about 343 metres per second. It travels faster in water and fastest in solids, and it cannot travel through a vacuum because there is nothing to vibrate.

instruction: I'm looking for a new video game to play, but I don't know what type I want. What are some popular game genres?
reply: On any of them: *Knives Out* for a whodunnit everyone enjoys, *Happy Valley* or *The Bear* for a series you'll finish, *Paddington 2* if children are in the room. Say which service and the mood and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. What do you think about cooking?
reply: *Home Cooking* (Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway) answers listeners' kitchen questions and is the friendliest place to start. *The Sporkful* is about how and why people eat what they eat, and *Gastropod* takes one food an episode and does its history and science.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my dog barking nonstop. Do you have any advice?
reply: Practise the whole thing rather than the bark: put him on a lead, have someone ring the bell or knock, and ask for a sit a few steps back from the door before it opens. Reward the sit, not the silence.

instruction: I'm looking for a gift for my sister's birthday. She created a gift registry online. How do I find it?
reply: Get something that shows you noticed: a book by an author they mentioned, a better version of something they use every day, or an afternoon planned around their favourite thing. The best gifts are specific to one person, so start from what they talk about.

instruction: I have a lot of homework due soon and I'm feeling overwhelmed. Can you help me break it down?
reply: Most primary homework is 20 to 30 minutes a night by the last years at primary, and about an hour a night in year 7 and up, with a break part way. If a piece runs well past that, write a note to the teacher rather than pushing through it, because homework that takes an hour and ends in tears is usually the wrong homework.

instruction: I'm having trouble studying for my exams and I was wondering if you had any suggestions for learning techniques.
reply: Make the first session tiny and today: open the topic list, pick the one you know least, and test yourself on it for ten minutes, because starting is the part that is failing rather than the studying. Then put three short sessions in the week you actually have, each ending with a self-test instead of a reread, and give each one a stopping time so it cannot drift to midnight.

instruction: I'm learning about shapes in architecture. What's the most common shape used in buildings?
reply: A polygon is a closed flat shape made only of straight sides that do not cross. A triangle has 3 sides, a quadrilateral 4, a pentagon 5 and a hexagon 6; a circle is not a polygon because its edge is curved.

instruction: What's the temperature outside?
reply: Go by the forecast for the hours you will actually be out rather than for the whole day, and dress for the coldest and wettest of those hours. As a rule of thumb: under about 10 degrees a proper coat, between 10 and 18 a jumper with something windproof over it, over 18 no coat and loose cotton instead.

instruction: I'm looking for a new online learning platform to improve my language skills. Have you heard of Duolingo?
reply: One person, one language works well - you always in one, your partner in the other - and the rule that matters is that each language gets real, daily use rather than lessons. Expect the school language to win once they start, so keep books, cartoons and relatives in the other one.

instruction: I'm going to a wedding and I want to look sharp. What's the difference between a tie and a bowtie?
reply: A bow tie is tied like a shoelace, only in front of your throat. Put it round your neck with one end about 4cm longer, cross the longer end over the shorter, bring it up behind the crossing and through the loop at your neck, and pull it snug: that is the knot, and the short end now stands up as the front loop.

instruction: I'm looking for some information about fashion brands. What are some popular vintage and second-hand brands?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm looking for a new game to play. What's popular in esports right now?
reply: *Patchwork*, *Jaipur* and *Hive* are the three best two-player games that are quick to learn. For a card game with no kit, gin rummy works just fine.

instruction: I'm thinking of replacing the flooring in my living room. What are some popular options?
reply: Start with what is on the floor: pick it all up into one basket, take the cups and plates out to the kitchen and bin the rubbish, because clothes, cups and paper are most of a mess and that alone makes a room look tidy. Then wipe the one surface you use most - the worktop, the table or the bedside - and give the rest one room a day rather than all of it in a panic.

instruction: I'm starting a new job in a laboratory. What should I expect on my first day?
reply: The second one is about depth, not introductions: they already think you can do the job and are now checking they want to work with you. Have one story ready in real detail - the problem, what you decided, what it changed - where the first round wanted headlines.

instruction: I'm looking to improve my critical thinking skills at work. What's the most important thing I should focus on?
reply: Last-minute learning works for facts and structures, not skills: take the syllabus or mark scheme, list what is actually examinable, and learn the highest-mark items with self-testing. Sleep before the exam and skip the things you already know.

instruction: I'm looking for a new set of measuring cups for my kitchen. What types of materials are they usually made of?
reply: Wrap each plate in paper or a tea towel and stand it on its edge in the box, like records in a crate, never stacked flat: that is what stops them cracking. A crumpled paper or towel cushion in the bottom and on top, small boxes that one person can lift, and FRAGILE written on the sides.

instruction: I'm looking for a new gym to join. What are some popular group fitness classes?
reply: Find a club that teaches technique rather than a fitness boxercise class - most amateur clubs run beginners' sessions and lend gloves and wraps for the first few. Go twice a week, expect the first month to be footwork, stance and the basic four punches on your own, and tell the coach you have not boxed before so nobody puts you in to spar.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to exercise my dog. What are some good pet-friendly parks and trails near me?
reply: Most adult dogs need 30 minutes to an hour a day, and a working breed rather more. A puppy is the other way round: about five minutes of walking for every month of age, twice a day, so a four-month-old gets two twenty-minute walks and no long hikes or stair runs until the growth plates close at a year.

instruction: I'm having trouble understanding some words in a book I'm reading. Can you help me?
reply: It means from memory, without looking anything up. What do you need to remember?

instruction: I'm planning to go to the mall with my kids this weekend. What are some tips for shopping with children?
reply: Smart casual is plenty: clean jeans or trousers and a nice top, in something you can kneel down and move about in if there are small children there.

instruction: I'm looking for a new camera, what are some popular types of cameras?
reply: Spend on the battery and the update years, not the camera: a mid-range phone at £250 to £400 lasts as long as a flagship if the maker promises four or five years of security updates (Samsung, Google and Apple do; many cheap brands promise two). Get at least 128GB, check the battery is 5,000mAh or more, and make sure it takes a physical SIM as well as an eSIM if you travel.

instruction: I have a leaky faucet in my kitchen. What should I do?
reply: Turn it off at the wall and shut the water off at the little isolator tap under the sink, then get the water up - a shallow tray and a towel is enough for a slow one. Water at the front of the door is usually the door seal or the filter, so twist the filter out and check the seal for food or a split; water underneath is the inlet or drain hose where it joins the machine or the waste, so check those joints first.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something to stay active. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick the one thing you would happily be bad at, and buy the cheapest version: a ten pound ukulele, a second-hand chess set, a supermarket sketchbook and pencils. Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week.

instruction: I have a cat and I'm worried about her health. What are some common signs of illness in cats?
reply: A cat that keeps being sick needs the vet rather than a wait-and-see: repeated vomiting in a cat is often a swallowed blockage (string, a hairband, a toy) or a poison, and cats go downhill fast. Offer small amounts of water, no food for a few hours, and ring the vet; go straight away if there is blood, if she is retching with nothing coming up, or if she is flat and hiding.

instruction: I'm trying to organize my closet. Do you have any tips?
reply: Go up before you go out: a shelf over the door, hooks on the back of a cupboard door and boxes stacked to the ceiling use space you already have. Take the doors off one base cupboard and put a bin or open shelves in it, keep the worktop clear, and send anything you use less than monthly to the top of a wardrobe or under the bed.

instruction: I'm trying to save energy at home. What are some ways to do that?
reply: Heating and hot water are most of the bill, so start there: on gas, turn the boiler flow temperature down to 55 to 60C and heat only the rooms someone is in; all electric, put the immersion and any room heaters on a timer for the hours you actually use. Then standby and lighting, which is about a quarter, so switch off at the wall.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan and I'm interested in cultural immersion. What's a good way to experience the local culture?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm looking for a new walking trail near my home. Do you know of any?
reply: Go for a canal towpath, a country park or a flat riverside path: wide, level, benches along it and nothing to climb over, which is what a short walk needs. Check the surface and the slope on the site's own page before you set off, because a walk advertised as circular can still hide a stile or a flight of steps, and ring ahead if someone uses a wheelchair - big attractions, National Trust and English Heritage places among them, lend one for free if it is booked a day or two in advance.

instruction: I'm learning about shapes in art. What are some basic shapes used in art?
reply: A polygon is a closed flat shape made only of straight sides that do not cross. A triangle has 3 sides, a quadrilateral 4, a pentagon 5 and a hexagon 6; a circle is not a polygon because its edge is curved.

instruction: I'm planning a road trip from New York to Los Angeles. What are the main roads I'll be taking?
reply: Pick a route you already know on quiet streets, ride it once at a weekend so the turns are not a surprise, and start with two days a week rather than five. Leave a lock, a spare tube and a pair of shoes at work, so there is nothing to carry and nothing to forget.

instruction: I'm trying to get to downtown, do you know when the next bus is?
reply: For a night before an early flight, book an airport hotel with a shuttle and check the first and last shuttle times before you pay - a 4am shuttle that stops at 11pm is the usual trap, and so is a "5 minutes from the terminal" that is five minutes by car on a road with no pavement. A town two or three stops away on the train, or a park-and-fly with the transfer included, is usually about half the price; add up the transfer, the parking and the extra hour and pick on the total.

instruction: I'm looking for ideas for family traditions to start this year. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. What are some popular crafting supplies?
reply: Pick the one thing you would happily be bad at, and buy the cheapest version: a ten pound ukulele, a second-hand chess set, a supermarket sketchbook and pencils. Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week.

instruction: I'm learning about the human life cycle. What's the first stage of life?
reply: A life cycle is the stages a living thing goes through from one generation to the next: a frog goes egg, tadpole, froglet, adult, and a butterfly goes egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. A plant's is seed, seedling, flowering plant, then seed again.

instruction: I'm looking for a wellness retreat. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my Wi-Fi connection. What is Wi-Fi?
reply: Wifi is just the radio link between your devices and the router; the internet is the connection the router brings into the house. So a wifi problem is your side (distance, walls, an old router) and an internet problem is your provider's line.

instruction: I'm interested in ancient artifacts. What's the oldest known artifact?
reply: Ancient Egyptians built them about 4,500 years ago, around 2560 BC for the Great Pyramid of Giza, as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu. The workers were organised, paid labourers, not slaves, hauling stone on ramps and sledges.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I'd like to learn some relaxation techniques. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move.

instruction: What are the 7 continents?
reply: Both: Australia is the smallest continent and the only country that is a whole continent. It is also the sixth largest country by area, and the only one that is both a country and a continent.

instruction: I'm looking for some information about different types of cuisine. What's the main difference between Chinese and Japanese food?
reply: Fish and chips feeds a group for the least money and nobody argues about it. If tastes differ, Indian beats Chinese: more vegetarian mains, and the sides stretch, so two mains with one rice and one bread feeds three.

instruction: I'm having some issues with one of our vendors, they're not meeting their deadlines and it's affecting our project timeline.
reply: Ask in writing and name what you want: a refund, a repair, or money for the trouble. Once eight weeks pass, or they send a final response you disagree with, take it to the ombudsman for that industry - Financial for a bank or insurer, Energy for a supplier, Communications for broadband and phones, and the Local Government Ombudsman for a council - which is free and needs no lawyer.

instruction: I'm going for a run later and I'm worried I might get dehydrated. How much water should I drink before I start?
reply: Under an hour you do not need to carry anything: have 300-500ml in the hour before you go and take water at fountains or taps on the way. Past an hour, or on a hot day, carry 400-700ml and drink a few mouthfuls every 15-20 minutes rather than one big stop.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. What are some popular crafting ideas?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I have a presentation at school and I'm really nervous about public speaking. What's the most important thing to remember?
reply: Write the one sentence you want people to remember, then build three slides around it and cut the rest. Practise out loud twice, standing up, timing it, and take a one-page note instead of reading the slides; the first 30 seconds scripted and the rest in headings is what keeps a talk calm.

instruction: I'm trying to count to 10. Can you help me?
reply: Write one to nine as words and 10 and up as figures, except when a number starts a sentence - then spell it out: "Twenty people came." Keep it consistent within a sentence, and use figures for money, times and measurements.

instruction: I'm planning a vacation and looking for some national park recommendations. What's a popular one in the US?
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I'm looking for information about different types of cameras. What's the main difference between a DSLR and a mirrorless camera?
reply: A mirror is glass with a thin layer of silver or aluminium on the back, and light bounces off that layer at the same angle it arrived - in at 30 degrees, out at 30 degrees, which is why you see yourself where the reflection says you are. The glass only protects the silver, so a mirror that has gone patchy has lost that coating rather than got dirty.

instruction: I'm interested in photography and I was wondering what's a good photo editing software for beginners.
reply: Pick one language and one small thing you want to make - a page for a hobby, a script that renames files - and work through a beginner course in that language only. Python or JavaScript is the usual start; HTML and CSS first if you want to see a page you build in a browser.

instruction: I'm learning about colors and their meanings. What does the color blue mean?
reply: It means it happened suddenly, with no warning. What came out of the blue?

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan and I'm looking for a place to stay. What are my options?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: What's your favorite season?
reply: Seasons stay lower case: spring, summer, autumn, winter. Days and months take a capital - Monday, January - and so do holidays, as in Christmas.

instruction: I'm looking for information about grandparents' rights. What are grandparents' rights?
reply: Be specific about what you need and when, and agree the basics up front: bedtimes, treats and what to do if the child is ill. Grandparents usually want to help and hate guessing, so a short 'could you do Tuesdays, and we do baths' beats hinting.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something to relax. I've heard reading is good for that.
reply: Reading on paper in low light is one of the better wind-downs there is, and a book you have read before is easier to put down than a new one. It is the backlit screen and the scrolling that delay sleep, so a phone or tablet story is the one to move; an e-reader on a warm setting is much closer to paper.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my team at work. We're not communicating well.
reply: A team that has gone quiet has usually learned what bad news costs, so change that first: say out loud what you will not be annoyed about - a delay told on Tuesday, a mistake that is already being fixed - and what you will, which is a surprise on Friday, then behave that way once, because one calm reaction does more than any speech. Ask for one piece of bad news a week and thank the person who brings it in front of the others.

instruction: I'm looking for some new cooking shows to watch. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: *Home Cooking* (Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway) answers listeners' kitchen questions and is the friendliest place to start. *The Sporkful* is about how and why people eat what they eat, and *Gastropod* takes one food an episode and does its history and science.

instruction: I'm looking to improve my leadership skills at work. What are some key qualities of a good leader?
reply: Lead with what you have done, not with job titles: school or college, volunteering, a paper round, a team you played in, a club you ran. Then a two-line profile at the top saying what you want and what you are good at with people, numbers or tools.

instruction: I'm learning about animals in school. What's the difference between domesticated and wild animals?
reply: A species is a group of living things that can breed together and produce fertile young: dogs are one species, and a horse and a donkey are different species because their mule offspring cannot have young. Members of a species share most of their genes.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What are some main factors that affect the climate?
reply: Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide, which traps heat in the atmosphere instead of letting it escape to space. That extra heat raises average temperatures, melts ice and makes extreme weather more likely; the science is settled, though predicting any one storm is not.

instruction: I'm planning to buy a new laptop and I want to compare prices. Can you help me?
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm looking for a simple breakfast idea.
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I want to start playing basketball, what equipment do I need?
reply: Start with very little: trainers or astro boots, shorts or leggings, a water bottle and, for football or hockey, shin pads. Clubs lend sticks, bats and bibs to beginners, so email and ask what they provide before you buy anything.

instruction: I'm looking for information about non-profit jobs. What are some common categories?
reply: Pick the one thing you can already do that people pay for, and sell it in the smallest packet: tutoring a GCSE subject, fixing bikes, editing CVs, dog walks on the way home, weekend cover in a bar or care home. Sell to people you can reach this week rather than building a website, do two or three paid jobs before you spend anything on it, and keep a record of what you earn: £1,000 a year of side income is tax free (the trading allowance), and above that you register for Self Assessment.

instruction: I'm a big sports fan. What are some popular sports to watch?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: I'm looking for a new board game to play with friends. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: *Codenames* is the safest buy: two teams, one grid of words, five minutes to learn, and it works from four players up. *Ticket to Ride* if you want a proper board with a bit of thinking in it, and *Just One* if the table is mixed ages and nobody wants a rulebook.

instruction: I'm having trouble writing a letter to my friend. Do you have any tips on how to make it more interesting?
reply: Write the date, then the one thing you would tell a friend about the day - what happened, and what you thought of it - in three or four lines and without tidying it up. Keep it where you will actually open it and write at a fixed time, because the habit is the hard part; a page of plain sentences beats a blank page waiting for a good day.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. What is insomnia?
reply: Fix the wake-up time first: the same hour every day, including after a bad night, and the rest tends to follow within a fortnight. Then the three that do most of the work - daylight and a walk in the first hour, no caffeine after lunch, and a screen-free half hour before bed - and only get into bed when you are sleepy rather than tired.

instruction: I'm looking for a new exercise routine and I've heard about Pilates. What is Pilates?
reply: Pilates is the better pick for a weak or sore back and a strong middle - it is slow, controlled work on the deep stomach and hip muscles - and yoga is the better pick for flexibility, balance and winding down. Both are low-impact and fine to start from nothing, so if the choice is still even, take the one whose teacher you liked.

instruction: I'm due for a doctor's visit and I'm not sure what to expect.
reply: Book the check-up and say on the phone that you are nervous and have not been for a while - practices hear it every week, and most will give you a longer first appointment, a signal to stop, and no lecture. The first visit is usually a look round and an x-ray, nothing more, and you can agree to one small thing at a time.

instruction: I'm trying to get more into team sports. What are some popular options?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: What is the wind like today?
reply: Wind is air moving from an area of high pressure to one of low pressure, and the sun creates those differences by heating land and sea unevenly. The bigger the pressure gap, the stronger the wind.

instruction: I'm going to my first concert next week. What should I expect?
reply: It's genuinely a safe way to travel, and the first flight is mostly boring: check in, security, wait, board, sit. Tell the cabin crew it's your first time if you're nervous; they're used to it and always look after you.

instruction: I'm feeling tired at work and need a break. What are some good activities to do during a short break?
reply: Take the smallest break that is really a break, and take it today: twenty minutes out of the house without your phone, or a bath with the door shut while someone else does bedtime. Then lower the bar for the rest of the day - one meal, one wash, no craft - because a worn-out parent does not need a plan, they need an hour.

instruction: I'm worried about pollution in our planet. Is it getting better or worse?
reply: Acid rain forms when sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning coal and oil mix with water in the air and fall as weak acid. It harms trees and lakes; filters on power stations and cleaner fuel have cut it a lot since the 1980s.

instruction: I'm interested in playing basketball. What's the main objective of the game?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I just bought a new wooden table, and I want to keep it looking nice. What's the best way to clean it?
reply: Scrub it with half a lemon and a big pinch of salt, rinse in the hottest water you have and dry it standing up: that lifts onion, garlic and fish out of wood or plastic. Plastic boards can go through the dishwasher, wooden ones should never.

instruction: I'm looking for comfortable clothes to wear at home. What's a good option?
reply: Something comfortable and a step nicer than you'd wear at home: jeans with a good top, or a dress with flat shoes. Nothing that needs careful handling next to red wine on someone's sofa.

instruction: I have a dog and I'm worried he's not getting enough exercise. How often should I walk him?
reply: Most adult dogs need 30 minutes to an hour a day, and a working breed rather more. A puppy is the other way round: about five minutes of walking for every month of age, twice a day, so a four-month-old gets two twenty-minute walks and no long hikes or stair runs until the growth plates close at a year.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I'm thinking of taking a nap. What's the ideal nap duration?
reply: A short nap is worth having: 20 minutes, ideally before about 3pm, and set an alarm, because 90 minutes leaves you groggier than when you lay down. It helps most if you lost sleep the night before or you are driving later.

instruction: I'm having trouble reading my textbooks for school. Do you have any tips?
reply: Testing yourself is what makes things stick; rereading notes mostly feels productive without being so. Turn each topic into five questions and answer them with the book shut, then check, and redo the ones you got wrong tomorrow and again in a week.

instruction: I want to increase my flexibility. What are some good exercises?
reply: Hold each one for 20 to 30 seconds, twice on each side, and do the set two or three times a week - daily works too but the gains come from doing it often, not from going deep. The five that matter for everyday life are the backs of the thighs, the hips and hip flexors, the calves, the chest and the upper back; warm up first with a few minutes of walking, and ease into the stretch rather than bouncing at the end of it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new word processing software. What are some popular options?
reply: Work from your own mistakes, not a list of hard words: take the twenty words you actually get wrong in texts and emails, and use look-say-cover-write-check on five a day - look at it, say it, cover it, write it, check it. Break long words into syllables as you say them (gov-ern-ment, sep-a-rate), and read your own writing out loud, because most spelling slips are words you can hear.

instruction: I'm going on a trip soon and I'm not sure how to pack my luggage efficiently. Do you have any tips?
reply: Lay everything out and take half the clothes and twice the money: three tops, two bottoms, one warm layer and shoes you can walk in covers a week. Roll clothes, keep a change in your hand luggage, and buy anything you forget when you arrive.

instruction: I'm looking for a new car. What are some important safety features to consider?
reply: Small, petrol, and as dull as you can bear: a hatchback like a Corsa, Fiesta, Polo or Yaris with a small engine. Check two things before the car itself - the insurance group, because a 1.0-litre in a low group can cost half what a bigger car costs to insure, and the MOT history on gov.uk for gaps and advisories.

instruction: I'm looking for educational resources for learning Python programming.
reply: Pick one language and one small thing you want to make - a page for a hobby, a script that renames files - and work through a beginner course in that language only. Python or JavaScript is the usual start; HTML and CSS first if you want to see a page you build in a browser.

instruction: I'm going to a concert tonight and I'm planning to take some photos. Do you have any tips for concert photography?
reply: Get closer and hold the phone still: brace it against a wall, a table or your chest, and tap the screen on the person or thing you are shooting so the brightness is set for that and not for the sky behind. Wipe the lens on your sleeve first, because a smeared lens is what makes phone photos look flat and hazy.

instruction: I'm trying to stay hydrated, how much water should I drink each day?
reply: Six to eight glasses a day, about 1.5 to 2 litres, is plenty, and more in heat or after exercise; tea, coffee, milk, squash and food all count towards it, and pale straw-coloured urine is the check that you are about right. If you forget, keep a filled bottle where you sit and drink a glass with every meal.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different cultures. Can you tell me about cultural diversity?
reply: One person, one language works well - you always in one, your partner in the other - and the rule that matters is that each language gets real, daily use rather than lessons. Expect the school language to win once they start, so keep books, cartoons and relatives in the other one.

instruction: I'm trying to manage my debt. Do you have any tips?
reply: Pick a calm time, not the moment a bill lands, and put the numbers on the table: what comes in, what goes out, and what is left. Ask what they want to be true in a year - a deposit, a holiday, less stress - before you talk about cuts, because a shared goal is what makes the figures a plan rather than an accusation.

instruction: I'm looking for a new video camera for my YouTube channel. What type of camera is best for recording videos?
reply: Photos and video are what fill a phone or a laptop: about 3MB a photo, so 10,000 photos is around 30GB, and video runs from 150MB a minute at 1080p to 350MB at 4K. 128GB is enough for most people who stream their music and television and keep photos in the cloud; take 256GB if you record a lot of video or play big games.

instruction: I want to learn how to cook, but I don't know where to start. Do you have any beginner-friendly recipes?
reply: Cook the vegetables or potato first in an ovenproof frying pan until soft, then pour over 6 beaten eggs for a 20cm pan, seasoned and with a handful of cheese if you like. Keep it on a low heat for 3 to 4 minutes until the edges set, then finish it under the grill or in a 180C oven for 8 to 10 minutes until the middle is just set.

instruction: I heard there's going to be a lot of snow this week. What happens to buildings when they get a lot of snow on them?
reply: Snow forms when water vapour freezes straight into ice crystals high in a cloud, and the crystals stick together as they fall. It only reaches the ground as snow if the air stays cold all the way down, which is why a cold snap often brings sleet instead.

instruction: I'm planning to do some online shopping. How do I know if a website is secure?
reply: Buying online gives you a 14-day right to change your mind from the day it arrives, and you only pay the return postage unless the shop says otherwise; buying in a shop gives you no right to change your mind at all, only the shop's own policy. That is the real difference, not the price.

instruction: I'm planning to start playing basketball again after a long break. What are some common injuries I should watch out for?
reply: Tennis elbow is the tendon on the outside of the elbow overworked by gripping, lifting and typing, so the outside of the elbow aches and the grip weakens; golfer's elbow is the same on the inside. It is not a wait-and-rest injury: rest it from the thing that caused it, but keep using the arm gently, and do the eccentric exercise - a light weight or a tin, wrist slowly down and lift back with the other hand, three sets of fifteen, most days.

instruction: I'm looking for a new smartphone. What are some popular brands?
reply: iPhone if you want the long updates and everything to talk to the rest of the family's; Android if you want to spend less, get two days of battery, or keep a headphone jack. The cheapest way in is a two-year-old iPhone or a mid-range Samsung, and both last well if you put a case on them.

instruction: What's the latest social media trend?
reply: The phone already counts it: Settings > Mobile data on an iPhone, or Settings > Network > Data usage on Android, shows the month's total and which apps are eating it. Video and social apps are nearly always the top two, and turning off background refresh and auto-play on mobile data usually halves it.

instruction: I'm learning about rocks in school, and I was wondering what the main types of rocks are.
reply: A rock is a solid piece of the earth made of one or more minerals: granite is mostly quartz and feldspar, and limestone is mostly calcite. Rocks come in three kinds - igneous from cooled magma, sedimentary from settled layers, and metamorphic changed by heat and pressure.

instruction: I'm planning a local trip this weekend and I'm looking for some historical sites to visit. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I'm trying to organize a community clean-up event in my neighborhood. Do you have any tips on how to get started?
reply: Ask four or five people, not a crowd, and fix the next date before the first meeting ends - a club that meets every six weeks at a set day keeps going, one that waits for everyone to be free does not. Pick short books to begin with, let whoever chose it lead for ten minutes, and bring one question rather than a summary: "who did you believe?", "what would you have done?".

instruction: I'm feeling overwhelmed with clutter at home and I'm thinking about hiring a professional organizer. What do professional organizers do?
reply: Take everything out and put back only what you wore last year, in one go, with a bag for the charity shop by your feet. Then group by what you put on together - work, weekend, gym - rather than by type, and hang the long things at one end so the space under them takes a box.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to, I really like R&B and Soul.
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm new to the gym and I don't know which machine exercises to do for my legs.
reply: Hold each one for 20 to 30 seconds, twice on each side, and do the set two or three times a week - daily works too but the gains come from doing it often, not from going deep. The five that matter for everyday life are the backs of the thighs, the hips and hip flexors, the calves, the chest and the upper back; warm up first with a few minutes of walking, and ease into the stretch rather than bouncing at the end of it.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed with work and struggling to find time for exercise. Do you have any tips on balancing work and personal life?
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you have any suggestions for creating a sleep-conducive bedroom environment?
reply: Cool the room rather than the bed: open windows on both sides for a through draught, keep the curtains shut in the day, and put a bowl of ice in front of a fan. A lukewarm shower before bed, cotton sheets and a hot water bottle filled with cold water at your feet all help more than sleeping with no cover at all.

instruction: It's a beautiful sunny day today. I love sunshine.
reply: Low sun sends its light through far more atmosphere, which scatters the blues away and leaves the reds and oranges to reach you. Dust and cloud make it stronger, which is why the best sunsets come after a clear, dusty day.

instruction: I'm looking for comfortable clothes. What are some popular options?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a new dog, but I'm worried about food allergies. What are common food allergies in dogs?
reply: Cat and dog allergy is a protein in the skin flakes, saliva and urine rather than in the hair, and it sticks to anything soft: keep the animal out of the bedroom and off the sofa, wash your hands after touching it, damp-dust rather than dry-dust, vacuum with a HEPA filter and wash the bedding at 60C.
