A daily antihistamine, or a steroid nasal spray from the pharmacist, covers the days that are bad.

instruction: I'm learning about the water cycle in school. What is evaporation?
reply: Evaporation is a liquid turning into a gas at its surface, without needing to reach boiling point. Water left in a glass disappears over days because the fastest molecules escape into the air; warmth, wind and a larger surface make it happen faster, which is why washing dries on a line.

instruction: I'm looking for a new scarf. What are some popular colors for scarves this season?
reply: Pick a tie a shade darker than your shirt and darker than the suit, and let one bold thing carry it: a patterned tie with a plain shirt, or a patterned shirt with a plain tie. With a navy suit, most things work - burgundy, bottle green, a dark striped tie - and a tie the same colour as the suit is the one to skip.

instruction: I have a dog and I'm worried about his safety at home. Do you have any tips?
reply: Dogs hear bangs far louder than we do and can't tell they are harmless, so plan the night instead of waiting for the first one: walk him before dark, then shut the windows and curtains, put the radio on and let him hide where he likes with something to chew. Stay in with him, don't take him to a display and never tell a frightened dog off; if he panics badly, ask the vet about a calming plan a few weeks ahead and check his microchip details are up to date in case he bolts.

instruction: I want to get fit, but I'm struggling to stay motivated. Do you have any tips?
reply: Make it small and scheduled: a set time, everything you need out and ready, and a session so short that skipping it feels sillier than doing it. Track the days you show up rather than the results, and do it with someone or book it like an appointment: habit carries you when motivation does not.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to improve my professional skills, do you have any suggestions?
reply: Make the task visible and small: one page, one timer, everything else out of the room. Body-doubling works for a lot of people - study alongside someone, in person or on a video call with mics off.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Africa and I'm excited to see some wildlife. What are some common animals to see on a safari?
reply: In a British city park in winter you'll usually see robins, blackbirds, blue tits, great tits, pigeons, crows and magpies, with gulls and starlings on the grass. Look in the bushes and bare trees rather than the open lawn, and early morning is the busiest time.

instruction: I'm thinking about getting a pet, but I'm not sure what kind to get.
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm looking for dessert ideas. What are some popular frozen desserts?
reply: Hot chocolate sauce, tinned peaches or raspberries with a splash of their juice, crushed biscuits or toasted nuts, and a pinch of salt on anything caramel. A shot of espresso over vanilla is affogato, which is the best 30-second pudding there is.

instruction: I'm thinking of cycling to work instead of driving, is that a good idea?
reply: Worth it if the alternative is driving: a pedal-assist bike flattens the hills and the headwind, so a commute you would skip on a bad day still happens, for a few pence of electricity a charge and no tax or parking. It saves little against a bus pass and keeps you less fit unless you turn the assist down.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping lately. Do you think stress is affecting my sleep quality?
reply: Long sleeps now and then are just a debt being paid, especially after a run of short nights. Needing nine or ten hours most nights and still waking flat is worth a GP visit: an underactive thyroid, low iron, low vitamin D, depression and sleep apnoea all show up that way, and each is easy to test for.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. What's popular right now?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I want to cook healthier meals, but I don't know where to start. I love baking, but I want to reduce the sugar in my recipes.
reply: Bake something that is low in sugar by nature rather than swapping in sweeteners: an almond and olive oil cake, a carrot cake made with less sugar and more spice, or berries with cream and a little dark chocolate. Keep the portion small and have it after a meal rather than on its own, and put the fruit and the cream on the plate so the cake slice can be thinner.

instruction: I'm thinking about getting a pet for my elderly mom. What kind of pet is good for seniors?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm looking for some ideas for summer meals. What are some popular seasonal ingredients?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you have any tips?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: I'm looking for a new laptop, but I'm not sure which one to choose. Can you tell me where I can find reviews for laptops?
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm having trouble studying for my exams and I heard about the SQ3R method. What does it stand for?
reply: QR stands for Quick Response, and the name is the only thing about it that is simple: the square holds up to about four thousand characters of text, which is how a whole web address fits in, and it survives being printed small, smudged or half covered. That is why the one on a bus stop still scans from a photograph.

instruction: I'm interested in photography as a hobby. What kind of camera should I get?
reply: Pick the one thing you would happily be bad at, and buy the cheapest version: a ten pound ukulele, a second-hand chess set, a supermarket sketchbook and pencils. Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week.

instruction: I want to eat healthier, but I'm not sure where to start with meal planning.
reply: Eat in date order first, and after that the food that is on borrowed time: fresh fish and mince within a day or two, then soft fruit, berries and salad leaves, then milk, yoghurt and cream, then hard cheese, butter and cooked leftovers. Where it sits matters as much as the order - cooked and ready-to-eat food on the top shelves, raw meat and fish on the bottom shelf in a box so nothing drips, and vegetables in the drawer.

instruction: I'm looking for something fun to do this weekend. What local festivals are happening?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm learning to swim and I was wondering what are the main swimming strokes?
reply: Adult lessons at your local pool are the fastest route: most run classes for complete beginners, often in small groups, and every instructor has taught adults who are frightened of the water. Book a course rather than one lesson, start in the shallow end with floats, and ask for an instructor who is used to nervous beginners.

instruction: I have trouble managing my time effectively. Can you give me some tips?
reply: Ask for a private twenty minutes and say it plainly in the first sentence: "I'm not coping with the current load and I want to sort it out before it shows in the work." Then bring two or three specifics - the tasks, the hours, what has slipped - and two things you want changed, because a manager can act on a proposal and rarely on a feeling. Ask what support exists: an employee assistance line, occupational health, flexible hours or a temporary reallocation.

instruction: What's the difference between pitch and volume?
reply: A magnet and a coil push a cone in and out in time with the signal, and the moving cone moves the air, which is the sound. A small cone cannot shift much air, so it makes the high notes well and the bass not at all: that is why a speaker with a big cabinet and a port sounds fuller at the same volume.

instruction: What is a toaster used for?
reply: Two slots do for one or two people and four for a family, and the slot width matters more than the wattage: look for wide slots if you toast bagels, crumpets or thick-cut bread. Variable browning plus a cancel button is the pair that stops you scraping burnt toast, and a defrost setting is worth having if you freeze bread.

instruction: I'm looking for a new song to listen to. What's a popular song right now?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about communication in different cultures. Can you tell me a bit about it?
reply: One person, one language works well - you always in one, your partner in the other - and the rule that matters is that each language gets real, daily use rather than lessons. Expect the school language to win once they start, so keep books, cartoons and relatives in the other one.

instruction: I'm thinking about my family and how my parents raised me. What do you think is the most important thing parents can do to be good role models?
reply: Don't try to be the parent yet: be a reliable adult who is not in charge of the rules and let their actual parent do the discipline for a while. Keep the offers small and repeated - a lift, a snack they like, a show you both watch - because loyalty to the other parent is usually what is behind the hostility.

instruction: I'm worried about the rain coming this weekend. Do you think it will be heavy?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to preserve my family's recipes. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I'm learning about chemistry in school, and I was wondering what the periodic table is.
reply: There are 118 elements in order of atomic number, and Mendeleev put the first table together in 1869 leaving gaps for elements nobody had found yet. For school you need the first 20 by heart: hydrogen, helium, lithium, beryllium, boron, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, fluorine, neon, sodium, magnesium, aluminium, silicon, phosphorus, sulfur, chlorine, argon, potassium, calcium.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something sporty. What sports are easy to learn?
reply: Pick the one thing you would happily be bad at, and buy the cheapest version: a ten pound ukulele, a second-hand chess set, a supermarket sketchbook and pencils. Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week.

instruction: I have a senior dog and I'm worried he's not getting enough exercise. What are some good exercises for older dogs?
reply: For an older dog: a warm, soft bed away from draughts, a ramp or a low step for the sofa, shorter and more frequent walks, and a vet check twice a year. Keep its claws short, which is easy to forget when it walks less, and ask the vet about pain relief if it's slow to get up.

instruction: I'm looking for dessert ideas. What are some popular types of cakes?
reply: Bake something that is low in sugar by nature rather than swapping in sweeteners: an almond and olive oil cake, a carrot cake made with less sugar and more spice, or berries with cream and a little dark chocolate. Keep the portion small and have it after a meal rather than on its own, and put the fruit and the cream on the plate so the cake slice can be thinner.

instruction: I'm having trouble staying focused while reading for school. Do you have any tips for active reading?
reply: Ask for the formal help first: a dyslexia assessment at university goes through the disability service, and it unlocks extra time in exams, a reader or text-to-speech software, and often a grant for equipment - at school it is the SENCO, and it costs you nothing to ask. For the reading itself, use text-to-speech so the page reads to you while you follow with a finger, take the chapter in 20-minute blocks with the summary read first, and ask for the reading list in advance so you are never reading against a deadline.

instruction: What are the four seasons?
reply: Seasons stay lower case: spring, summer, autumn, winter. Days and months take a capital - Monday, January - and so do holidays, as in Christmas.

instruction: I'm looking to buy some new clothes online. What shipping options do you have?
reply: Buying online gives you a 14-day right to change your mind from the day it arrives, and you only pay the return postage unless the shop says otherwise; buying in a shop gives you no right to change your mind at all, only the shop's own policy. That is the real difference, not the price.

instruction: I have a senior cat at home, and I'm worried about her health. What are some common health issues in older cats?
reply: From about eight, twice a year is worth it: the vet can find the things old cats hide — kidney trouble, thyroid, arthritis, high blood pressure — before you see them. Weigh her monthly at home and ask for a blood and urine test at the annual visit.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you have any suggestions on how to improve my bedroom environment for better sleep?
reply: Cool the room rather than the bed: open windows on both sides for a through draught, keep the curtains shut in the day, and put a bowl of ice in front of a fan. A lukewarm shower before bed, cotton sheets and a hot water bottle filled with cold water at your feet all help more than sleeping with no cover at all.

instruction: I'm trying to reduce my waste at home. What are some common items that can be recycled?
reply: Book a bulky waste collection with your council - most charge twenty to forty pounds and collect from the doorstep - or take it to the recycling centre, where it is stripped for its springs. Charity shops rarely take one for hygiene reasons, so a free-ad site is the other realistic route if it is clean and you say collection only.

instruction: I'm planning to buy a new refrigerator for my home. What should I consider before making a purchase?
reply: Stand a fridge thermometer in a glass of water on the middle shelf and leave it overnight: the fridge wants 3 to 5C and the freezer -18C, and the dial's numbers are not degrees. A fridge that will not reach it wants the door seals checked - close the door on a sheet of paper and see if it slides out easily - and the coils at the back dusted.

instruction: I'm interested in wearable health monitoring devices. What's the most popular one?
reply: iPhone if you want the long updates and everything to talk to the rest of the family's; Android if you want to spend less, get two days of battery, or keep a headphone jack. The cheapest way in is a two-year-old iPhone or a mid-range Samsung, and both last well if you put a case on them.

instruction: I'm interested in photography as a hobby. What's the most important thing to consider when taking a photo?
reply: Photos and video are what fill a phone or a laptop: about 3MB a photo, so 10,000 photos is around 30GB, and video runs from 150MB a minute at 1080p to 350MB at 4K. 128GB is enough for most people who stream their music and television and keep photos in the cloud; take 256GB if you record a lot of video or play big games.

instruction: I'm looking for some ideas for things to do on my lunch break at work.
reply: Give the day a hard edge and keep it the same one: laptop shut and work phone in a drawer at a fixed time, then something physical - a walk, a shower, cooking - because the body changes gear more reliably than the mind. Tell your team the hours once, in writing: "I'm offline after 6 and I pick up messages at 9." If you work from the room you live in, put the laptop out of sight at the end of the day; a screen in the corner is a shift that never ends.

instruction: I'm looking for a last-minute gift for my sister's birthday. Do you have any ideas?
reply: Ask the host if there is anything they need, then bring something they can use that night: a bottle of something they drink, a soft drink if you are not sure, or a pudding or cheese for the table. For a housewarming, a plant or a nice tea towel lasts longer than another candle.

instruction: I'm looking for a new piece of fitness equipment for home workouts. What's a kettlebell?
reply: Buy one adjustable dumbbell or one kettlebell and nothing else to begin with: about 6 to 10 kg suits most beginners and 10 to 16 kg if you are already strong, and a used one goes for £40 to £80. Add a resistance band for about £10 and a step or a sturdy chair, and that covers squats, rows, presses and carries - a mat only if your floor is hard.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately, so I was thinking about starting a dream journal to see if it helps me understand my sleep patterns better.
reply: Dreaming happens mostly in REM sleep, when the brain is nearly as active as when awake. Scientists think it helps sort memories and practise threats and feelings; there is no good evidence that dreams predict the future.

instruction: I'm looking for a new TV show to watch. What's a popular show right now?
reply: *Schitt's Creek* is the safe pick: short episodes, funny from the first series. *Derry Girls* if you want something sharper, or *Paddington 2* if it's a film tonight rather than a series.

instruction: I'm planning to travel alone for the first time and I'm a bit nervous. What are some good destinations for solo travelers?
reply: It's genuinely a safe way to travel, and the first flight is mostly boring: check in, security, wait, board, sit. Tell the cabin crew it's your first time if you're nervous; they're used to it and always look after you.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my dog. He's been barking nonstop lately.
reply: Practise the whole thing rather than the bark: put him on a lead, have someone ring the bell or knock, and ask for a sit a few steps back from the door before it opens. Reward the sit, not the silence.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hat to go with my casual outfits. What styles are popular right now?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm looking for a healthy snack option. What are some good nuts and seeds to eat?
reply: A 30g handful of nuts is about 175 calories and one of the better snacks you can buy: 6g of protein, 3g of fibre and fat that is mostly unsaturated, and people who eat them regularly tend to weigh less, not more, because they are satisfying. Walnuts are the one with omega-3 (plant ALA).

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to, do you have any suggestions for world music genres?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm learning about physical adaptations in school. What's a physical adaptation?
reply: Living things vary, and the ones whose variations suit their surroundings tend to survive and pass those variations on. Over many generations that selection changes the population: small changes accumulate into new species.

instruction: I'm looking for information about board game tournaments. Do they exist?
reply: *Codenames* is the safest buy: two teams, one grid of words, five minutes to learn, and it works from four players up. *Ticket to Ride* if you want a proper board with a bit of thinking in it, and *Just One* if the table is mixed ages and nobody wants a rulebook.

instruction: I was wondering, what happens to plants during winter?
reply: The garden in winter is mostly tidying and waiting: clear the dead stems but leave seed heads and any hollow stalks standing, because insects shelter in them and the birds eat the seeds. Mulch bare soil with compost or bark, but only once the ground is not frozen, and stay off wet or frozen grass because footprints kill the blades under them.

instruction: I'm looking to start a home gym and I'm not sure what equipment to get. What's the difference between dumbbells and barbells?
reply: Buy one adjustable dumbbell or one kettlebell and nothing else to begin with: about 6 to 10 kg suits most beginners and 10 to 16 kg if you are already strong, and a used one goes for £40 to £80. Add a resistance band for about £10 and a step or a sturdy chair, and that covers squats, rows, presses and carries - a mat only if your floor is hard.

instruction: I'm a farmer and I'm worried about the wind affecting my crops. How does wind affect agriculture?
reply: Wind is air moving from an area of high pressure to one of low pressure, and the sun creates those differences by heating land and sea unevenly. The bigger the pressure gap, the stronger the wind.

instruction: I'm having some car trouble. What are some common car maintenance tasks I should be doing regularly?
reply: Plan the driving days rather than the hours: put the stops in first, every two hours and one proper stop a day, and don't book more than six hours of driving in a day. Book the first and last night's bed before you go, check the spare tyre, the oil and the breakdown cover, and keep the overnight bag on the back seat.

instruction: I'm feeling sad because my family's old dog passed away yesterday. Do you have any advice on how to cope with the loss of a pet?
reply: Say the plain thing and then be quiet: "I'm so sorry - I don't have words, but I'm here." Name the person who died if they have named them, say their name back, and offer one concrete thing instead of "let me know if you need anything": a lift, a meal on Thursday, sitting with them. Do not explain, compare it to your own loss, or look for the bright side; the comfort is in staying, and in being the one who is still there in three weeks.

instruction: I'm thinking about my grandparents who live really far away. How can I stay in touch with them?
reply: A relative going quiet is usually nothing more than a busy year. Send something small and specific - a photo, or a plain 'I've missed you, are you around for a call?' - rather than a note about how long it has been.

instruction: I'm worried about fire safety at home. What's the most important thing to have?
reply: Tent with its pegs and a mallet, a sleeping bag and a mat - a foam or inflatable one, not just the tent floor - a head torch, a stove with fuel and a lighter, and a water container. Take warm layers and a waterproof even in summer, boots you can walk in, bin bags, a small first-aid kit with blister plasters, and food in a cool box.

instruction: I'm going on a trip soon and I'm not sure what toiletries to pack.
reply: Four things never go down a drain: fat, oil and grease (they cool, set and make fatbergs), wet wipes even the ones marked flushable, anything that swells or sets - rice, pasta, potatoes, flour, eggshells and pastry scraps go down soft and pack hard a metre along - and paint, thinner and the chemicals that go with them. Fat goes into a jar or the bin, wipes and grounds into the bin, rice and peelings into the food waste with a sieve in the plug for the last rinse.

instruction: I'm going on a trip to Japan soon and I want to buy some souvenirs. What are some popular ones?
reply: Cheap food that people finish and that travels: a big bowl of pasta salad, sausage rolls or sausages on sticks, cheese and crackers, and a tray of fairy cakes. Keep it to things you can make the day before, and buy the paper plates.

instruction: What should I do if someone is choking?
reply: Stay with them and say it will pass, because it does: an attack peaks in about ten minutes. Sit them down, loosen anything tight at the neck, and breathe out loud with them - out for longer than in, so they have something to follow rather than an instruction.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to teach my kids some family recipes. Do you have any tips?
reply: Three that work with children, easiest first: flapjack (no oven hands, just stirring and a flat tin), fairy cakes (they can fill the cases and ice them once cool) and shortbread (three ingredients, and cutting shapes is the fun part). Give the little ones the measuring and the stirring and keep the oven and the hob to yourself, and expect it to take twice as long as it would alone.

instruction: I'm concerned about pollution in my city. What's the main cause of light pollution?
reply: Charged particles from the sun hit gases high in the atmosphere and make them glow: green from oxygen, reds and purples from nitrogen. You need a dark, clear night and a high latitude, so northern Scotland, Iceland and Scandinavia are the usual spots.

instruction: I'm due for a health check-up and I was wondering what vaccinations I need.
reply: A vaccine teaches the immune system to recognise a germ without you having to get the illness: it shows a harmless part or a weakened version, and the body makes antibodies and memory cells ready for the real thing. That protection usually takes a few weeks and may need boosters.

instruction: What is the difference between a meter and a yard?
reply: A smart meter sends your readings to the supplier itself, so you stop reading meters, and it comes with an in-home display. An old meter needs reading by you or a visitor.

instruction: What are some forces in nature?
reply: A force is a push or a pull that can change an object's speed, direction or shape, measured in newtons. Gravity, friction and the push of a hand are all forces, and an object with no net force keeps doing what it was doing.

instruction: I'm looking for a new keyboard. What types are there?
reply: For a first piano, the thing that matters is weighted, full-size keys: a second-hand 88-key digital piano from Yamaha, Roland or Casio is 200 to 350 pounds and is the cheapest thing that teaches real finger strength. A 61-key keyboard with plastic keys is fine for a month to see if you like it, but it will not teach you to play, so hire or borrow one first if the money is tight - shops rent them monthly.

instruction: I have a lot of homework tonight, and I'm feeling overwhelmed. Do you have any tips on how to manage my time?
reply: Most primary homework is 20 to 30 minutes a night by the last years at primary, and about an hour a night in year 7 and up, with a break part way. If a piece runs well past that, write a note to the teacher rather than pushing through it, because homework that takes an hour and ends in tears is usually the wrong homework.

instruction: I want to learn more about digital communication. What is it?
reply: ICT stands for information and communication technology, the school subject that used to be called computer studies: word processing, spreadsheets, and how to search and check what you find. Schools now tend to call it computing, and teach programming in it as well.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with a difficult client. Do you have any tips?
reply: The first three clients come from people who already know your work: a former employer or colleague, a friend who runs something, the local shop, a group you are already in. Pick one service you can name in a sentence, then tell twenty people you have started and what you charge - not a general announcement, one message each.

instruction: I'm a beginner runner and I'm worried about getting injured. What are some common running injuries I should be aware of?
reply: Nearly all running injuries come from doing more, sooner than the body can repair: add no more than about 10 per cent to your weekly distance, keep every second run easy, and take a rest day after a long one. Two short strength sessions a week - calf raises, squats, a single-leg balance - and shoes that are not worn through do the rest.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier, but I'm not sure how to read nutrition labels.
reply: Ultra-processed food is the industrial end of the scale: things made mostly from extracts and additives - emulsifiers, colourings, flavourings, sweeteners - that you would not cook with at home, like fizzy drinks, crisps, sausages, ready meals and most breakfast cereal. The evidence is that people eat more of it and put on weight, but the class is broad enough that hummus and wholemeal bread land in it, so judge by the ingredient list rather than the label.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school, and I was wondering what the digestive system does.
reply: Digestion is how the body breaks food into pieces small enough to absorb: chewing and stomach acid start it, enzymes in the small intestine split carbohydrates into sugars, proteins into amino acids and fats into fatty acids, and the nutrients pass through the gut wall into the blood. The whole trip usually takes six to eight hours, and fibre and water keep it moving.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hair clip. What types are popular right now?
reply: Cut dry hair, so you can see where it actually falls, and take less off than you think: small snips across the width, not one line, because hair springs up once it dries. For a fringe, comb a thin section down flat, hold it between two fingers and cut just under them, checking both sides sit level with the eyebrow.

instruction: I have a small plant and I was wondering if it needs light.
reply: For a room with no window, take the plants that cope with low light: pothos, snake plant, ZZ plant, peace lily and spider plant will all hold on, and a bathroom's steam suits a fern. Everything slows down in the dark, so water far less than the label says - every two to three weeks, once the top of the compost is dry - or the roots rot.

instruction: I'm looking for information about the latest fashion trends. What's popular right now?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm thinking about my grandparents. What are some gift ideas for them?
reply: Small things they can use lying in bed: a long phone cable and a charged power bank, earphones, a puzzle book or a magazine, a decent lip balm, a light blanket, or a printed photo of the family to put on the locker. Skip flowers on most wards and skip food unless you know the diet.

instruction: I'm going on a trip to Japan soon and I want to take some great photos. What's the best way to capture good travel photos?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm looking for information about vintage clothing. What's the most popular type of vintage clothing?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school, and I was wondering what the muscular system does.
reply: Protein is a building material made of chains of amino acids: the body uses it to build and repair muscle, skin, hair and organs, and enzymes are proteins too. Meat, fish, eggs, milk, beans, lentils, nuts and tofu are good sources.

instruction: I'm interested in painting as a hobby. What are some common techniques?
reply: Draw what is in front of you, not from memory: a mug, your own hand, the chair opposite. Ten minutes a day beats a long session at the weekend, one object a day for a fortnight, and use a soft pencil (2B) on cheap paper so you are not afraid of it.

instruction: I'm looking for information about film festivals. Are there any big ones happening this year?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm going on a trip next week and I need help with packing. Can you tell me what I should bring?
reply: A rug, a cool bag with a freezer block, plates and cups you do not mind losing, a bottle opener, napkins, a bin bag and water. Skip anything heavy with mayonnaise unless it is eaten within the hour: sausage rolls, cheese, fruit and a flask keep for hours.

instruction: I'm looking for a new frying pan. What's the difference between stainless steel and non-stick pans?
reply: A pan that sticks has usually lost its thin layer of baked-on oil: scrub it, dry it on the hob, rub a film of neutral oil over the inside and heat it until it just smokes, then wipe the surplus off with kitchen paper. Twice more and it is slippery again.

instruction: I'm going to a wedding and I don't have a suit. What are my options?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I'm considering carpooling to work. What are the benefits of using carpool lanes?
reply: Worth it if the alternative is driving: a pedal-assist bike flattens the hills and the headwind, so a commute you would skip on a bad day still happens, for a few pence of electricity a charge and no tax or parking. It saves little against a bus pass and keeps you less fit unless you turn the assist down.

instruction: I'm learning about animal adaptations in school. Can you tell me about how polar bears stay warm?
reply: Hibernation is a way of getting through a season with no food: the animal's temperature, heart rate and breathing drop, and it lives off the fat it laid down in autumn. A bear's heart can slow from 40 beats a minute to 8, and a hedgehog turns almost cold to the touch.

instruction: I'm trying to improve my productivity at work. What are some key factors that affect job performance?
reply: Mostly it is the setup, not willpower: enough sleep, food, the phone in another room and one thing open at a time. Work in 25-minute blocks on a single task written down first, because choosing where to start is half the distraction, and stand up for the break.

instruction: I have a dog and I'm not sure how often I should bathe him.
reply: Every six to eight weeks is plenty for most dogs, and less for a short coat: use a dog shampoo rather than yours, because a dog's skin sits at a different pH. Wet him right down to the skin, lather, then rinse for twice as long as feels necessary - leftover shampoo is what causes the scratching afterwards.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my work schedule. Can I work remotely?
reply: Give the day a hard edge and keep it the same one: laptop shut and work phone in a drawer at a fixed time, then something physical - a walk, a shower, cooking - because the body changes gear more reliably than the mind. Tell your team the hours once, in writing: "I'm offline after 6 and I pick up messages at 9." If you work from the room you live in, put the laptop out of sight at the end of the day; a screen in the corner is a shift that never ends.

instruction: I'm looking for a new toy for my dog. What's a good option?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm planning a barbecue this weekend and I'm not sure what type of grill to use.
reply: Charcoal (about 1kg for ten people), a chimney starter and firelighters, long tongs, a wire brush, a tray for the cooked meat, and a meat thermometer. Put a bucket of water or sand beside it; a gas one needs a spare bottle instead.

instruction: I have a cat and I'm not sure how often I should brush her.
reply: Keep it to one minute and start when she is already sleepy, after a meal: let her sniff the brush and put it down beside her first, then do one stroke along her back, a treat, and stop while she is still happy. A soft rubber glove or a short-bristled brush hurts less than a metal comb on a short coat, and the belly, tail and legs are for the vet or the groomer, not for a cat who already hates it.

instruction: I'm planning a birthday party for my friend and I want to make sure I stay within my budget. Do you have any tips?
reply: Ask the host if there is anything they need, then bring something they can use that night: a bottle of something they drink, a soft drink if you are not sure, or a pudding or cheese for the table. For a housewarming, a plant or a nice tea towel lasts longer than another candle.

instruction: I'm looking for a place to eat. What types of restaurants are there?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping lately. What are some common factors that affect sleep quality?
reply: Long sleeps now and then are just a debt being paid, especially after a run of short nights. Needing nine or ten hours most nights and still waking flat is worth a GP visit: an underactive thyroid, low iron, low vitamin D, depression and sleep apnoea all show up that way, and each is easy to test for.

instruction: I'm a parent and I'm looking for ideas for a school fundraiser. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Nothing fancy for the first day: a named bag with a pencil case (two pens, a pencil, a rubber, a ruler), a water bottle, a packed lunch or the money loaded on the dinner account, and the PE kit the school asked for, in a bag of its own if they can. Label everything, including the coat and the shoes, and put the timetable in the front pocket.

instruction: I'm learning about the water cycle in school. What is precipitation?
reply: Precipitation is water falling out of the sky - rain, snow, sleet or hail - when droplets in a cloud join up until they are too heavy to stay up. It is one step of the water cycle, after evaporation and condensation.

instruction: I'm looking for a new exercise to try. What are some benefits of swimming?
reply: A steady front crawl does a mile - 64 lengths of a 25m pool - in about 30 to 40 minutes. Breaststroke, or a first season of swimming, is 45 minutes to an hour, and building up 200m at a time gets there better than trying the mile straight away.

instruction: What are the current fashion trends?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm thinking about getting a pet, and I want to know if they need exercise.
reply: Most adult dogs need 30 minutes to an hour a day, and a working breed rather more. A puppy is the other way round: about five minutes of walking for every month of age, twice a day, so a four-month-old gets two twenty-minute walks and no long hikes or stair runs until the growth plates close at a year.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school. What is the skeletal system?
reply: An organ is a part of the body made of several tissues working together for one job: the heart pumps blood, the lungs take in oxygen and the liver cleans the blood. Your skin is the largest organ, and organs work together in systems.

instruction: I've been getting sick a lot lately and I want to know how to boost my immune system.
reply: Immunity is your body's memory of a germ: white blood cells that have met a virus or a vaccine keep a record of its shape, so the next meeting is fought off before it makes you ill. That is why some illnesses you only get once and why a vaccine works without the disease, and why some of it fades over years - which is what tetanus and flu boosters are for.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Europe and I'm interested in bike tours. What's the most popular route?
reply: Thirty to sixty minutes at a pace where you can still talk is the everyday ride worth doing - roughly 10 to 20km - and three or four of those a week beats one long ride at the weekend. Add ten minutes to a ride a week rather than jumping to a long one, and take an easy day after a hard ride.

instruction: What is a shadow?
reply: A shadow is the patch where an object blocks light: light travels in straight lines, so an opaque object stops the rays and leaves a dark shape behind it. The shadow is biggest when the light source is close to the object and the surface is far behind, and a point of light gives a sharper edge than a wide one.

instruction: I'm learning about the Earth in school and I was wondering, what are the layers of the Earth?
reply: The Earth is layered: a thin rocky crust, a hot slow-flowing mantle, a liquid outer core of iron and nickel, and a solid inner core. The churning iron outer core is what makes the magnetic field that keeps the solar wind off us.

instruction: I'm trying to save money on groceries. Is buying in bulk a good idea?
reply: Write the week's four meals down before you shop and buy for those, not for the week you imagine. Keep a box in the fridge for what must go first, and put tonight's dinner in it when you unpack.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed with work and struggling to find a balance. Do you have any tips for work-life balance?
reply: Look at the week before the people: what is due, who is covering it, and what can be moved or dropped, then take one real thing off the list this week and say out loud why you moved it - a team that is flat is usually carrying more than its hours, and a speech about wellbeing does not buy that back. Then ten minutes with each of them, one at a time, and ask which part of the week is heaviest rather than whether they are coping: the one task they dread is the one you can shift, and it is rarely the one you guess.

instruction: I'm trying to save some money, do you have any tips on how to make a budget?
reply: Start pocket money at about six, a small fixed amount on the same day each week, and let them spend it badly while the sums are still small. Split it into spend, save and give jars so the saving is visible, and pay extra for jobs beyond the normal helping rather than docking the basics.

instruction: I love rain, especially in the rainforests. What makes rainforests so special?
reply: It just means raining very hard - nothing to do with animals. Are you stuck in it, or looking for something to do on a wet day?

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something fun and nostalgic. I used to love playing old video games when I was a kid.
reply: Pick the one thing you would happily be bad at, and buy the cheapest version: a ten pound ukulele, a second-hand chess set, a supermarket sketchbook and pencils. Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my coworker. We don't seem to get along.
reply: Treat it as a work problem with a work rule, not a feelings problem: name the two behaviours you have seen, with dates, and set what has to happen on a shift (who answers the phone, who signs off what) so the job does not need them to like each other. See them together once, then separately, because each will tell you a different story and both are partly true.

instruction: I'm looking for a new vacation destination. Can you suggest some adventure spots?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm trying to get back into running and I was wondering if you could help me come up with a training plan.
reply: Start with run-walk: three minutes of easy running, two minutes of walking, five times, three days a week, and add a minute of running each week. Build up for six weeks before you add speed, keep every run slow enough to talk, and expect the first fortnight to feel harder than it looks.

instruction: I'm a bit worried about climate change. Is it really happening?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new music streaming service. What are my options?
reply: Worth it if you work or stream at home, more than one person uses the connection, or you game: a phone hotspot will do for one light user, but its data cap and the delay on a video call show up fast. 5g home broadband sits between the two - no line and no engineer, but check the coverage at your postcode and how it holds up at 8pm before you take a two-year deal.

instruction: I'm looking for online courses to learn new skills, do you know any good platforms?
reply: Most evening courses are two or three hours of class a week plus about the same again at home, so plan on one evening and four or five hours a week. Ask for the guided learning hours before you enrol, because the college has to publish them, and check the fee: in England, English and maths up to GCSE are free for anyone who does not already have them, and a first level 2 or 3 qualification is often free if you are under 23 or on a low income.

instruction: I'm looking for music festivals happening this summer. Do you know any popular ones?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: What is a whisk used for in the kitchen?
reply: A balloon whisk is the round, balloon-shaped wire one, for putting air in: egg whites to peaks, cream to soft folds, a batter smooth. Its wide loops move a lot of air, which a flat or a ball whisk does not, so it is the one for meringue; it is no good for a thick mixture - that is a wooden spoon's job.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to New York and I need to book a flight. What airlines fly from my city to New York?
reply: Go straight to the airline's desk or app before the next one closes: when both legs are on one ticket the airline has to put you on the next available seat, and pay for a hotel and meals if the wait is overnight. On two separate tickets the second one is a no-show and nobody owes you a seat, so ring that airline and ask anyway.

instruction: I'm thinking of buying a new car and I'm considering an electric vehicle. What are the main benefits of electric cars?
reply: An electric car drives like an automatic with one difference: when you lift off the accelerator it slows itself down and puts charge back in the battery, so you brake with the right pedal for most stops and use the left one only for a hard stop. Treat the range as about 70% of the official figure in winter, charge to 80% for everyday use and 100% only before a long run, and check the car's own route planner for chargers rather than arriving on 5%.

instruction: I'm concerned about water safety at home. What are some common hazards I should know about?
reply: Tap water in the UK is safe to drink - it is tested all the way to your kitchen - and the taste it sometimes has is chlorine, which is there to keep it safe: fill a jug, keep it in the fridge for an hour and the taste goes. A filter is for taste rather than safety, and it needs changing when the pack says.

instruction: I'm looking for a taxi service that can accommodate my wheelchair. Do you know of any options?
reply: Plan the outing around the walking. Go door to door - a taxi, or the bus that stops nearest the door - and make a bench or a cafe the turning point so the trip is two short walks with a sit in between.

instruction: What season is it now?
reply: Seasons stay lower case: spring, summer, autumn, winter. Days and months take a capital - Monday, January - and so do holidays, as in Christmas.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. Do I need to go to bed and wake up at the same time every day, even on weekends?
reply: Count back about eight hours from the time you have to get up, and keep that bedtime the same seven days a week: the regularity matters more than the exact hour. If you lie there awake, go to bed half an hour later rather than earlier, so bed means sleep again.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Tokyo and I'm interested in taking some night photos. What are some good locations for night photography?
reply: Use the habits that work in any city after dark: stay on the busy, lit streets, take a licensed taxi or the metro rather than a shortcut, keep the phone out of sight and the bag in front of you, and ask the hotel desk which two or three streets to avoid - they know this week's answer better than any guide. Carry a card with the hotel address.

instruction: I have a dog and I'm worried about fleas and ticks. What can I do to prevent them?
reply: Fleas are not a sign of a dirty house: they come in on the animal and the eggs drop into the carpet, so the house is the part that keeps them coming back. Treat the animal and the house on the same day: a spot-on or tablet from the vet for every pet, bedding washed at 60C, and the carpets vacuumed daily for a fortnight, emptying the vacuum outside, because most of a flea infestation is eggs and pupae in the floor, not fleas on the pet.

instruction: I'm trying to update my wardrobe, but I want to be more sustainable. Do you have any tips?
reply: Take everything out and put back only what you wore last year, in one go, with a bag for the charity shop by your feet. Then group by what you put on together - work, weekend, gym - rather than by type, and hang the long things at one end so the space under them takes a box.

instruction: I'm thinking about adopting a pet. What are some benefits of adopting a senior pet?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I'm looking for information about different types of manufacturing jobs. Can you tell me about that?
reply: The Industrial Revolution was the switch from hand tools and farms to machines and factories, starting in Britain around 1760. Steam power, coal and iron moved millions of people into cities and made goods cheap enough for ordinary homes.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I want to try some yoga. What's a good pose to start with?
reply: Most bad posture is the chair and the sitting still, not the spine: set the screen so the top of it is at eye level, feet flat, elbows near a right angle, and get up every half hour - five minutes of standing beats a whole evening of trying to sit straighter. Then strengthen what holds you up: chin tucks, rows with a band, and squeezing the shoulder blades ten times a few times a day.

instruction: What's the weather like in winter?
reply: Winter is cold because your half of the Earth leans away from the Sun: the sunlight comes in at a low angle and is spread over more ground, and the shorter days give the ground less time to warm up. That is also why the winter sun feels weak even on a clear day.

instruction: I need some help with meal planning for my family. We have a big family dinner coming up and I want to make something everyone will enjoy.
reply: Cook the same sort of dinner as for anyone, with the starchy part smaller and the vegetables bigger: chicken or fish with two veg, a chilli with beans instead of rice, or an omelette and salad. Halve the potatoes, rice or pasta rather than cutting them out, go wholegrain where you can, skip the sugary drinks, and keep pudding small - and ask them what they usually do rather than guessing.

instruction: I'm hungry, what are some quick meal ideas?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: What is a search engine?
reply: It means looking in the wrong place for the answer. What are you trying to find?

instruction: I'm going shopping and I need to organize my shopping list. Do you have any tips?
reply: Take everything out and put back only what you wore last year, in one go, with a bag for the charity shop by your feet. Then group by what you put on together - work, weekend, gym - rather than by type, and hang the long things at one end so the space under them takes a box.

instruction: What are the three main states of matter?
reply: Dark matter is the name for mass we cannot see but can measure: galaxies spin and bend light as if they hold far more matter than the stars show. Nobody yet knows what it is made of, which is why it is one of the big open questions.

instruction: I'm looking for a new workspace. What are some popular types of studios?
reply: On any of them: *Knives Out* for a whodunnit everyone enjoys, *Happy Valley* or *The Bear* for a series you'll finish, *Paddington 2* if children are in the room. Say which service and the mood and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm going on a trip to Japan soon and I want to buy some souvenirs. What are some practical things I can get?
reply: Cheap food that people finish and that travels: a big bowl of pasta salad, sausage rolls or sausages on sticks, cheese and crackers, and a tray of fairy cakes. Keep it to things you can make the day before, and buy the paper plates.

instruction: I'm looking for fitness classes near my home. What types of classes do you offer?
reply: Find a club that teaches technique rather than a fitness boxercise class - most amateur clubs run beginners' sessions and lend gloves and wraps for the first few. Go twice a week, expect the first month to be footwork, stance and the basic four punches on your own, and tell the coach you have not boxed before so nobody puts you in to spar.

instruction: I'm learning about colors. What are the primary colors?
reply: Blue is scattered much more strongly than green, so the green that is scattered arrives mixed with far more blue and the sky reads as pale blue. Violet is scattered even more, but there is less of it in sunlight and our eyes are less sensitive to it, so it never dominates.

instruction: I'm learning about food chains in school. What are producers in a food chain?
reply: A food chain is the line of who eats whom, starting with a plant that makes its own food and ending with a predator. Energy is lost at every step, which is why top predators are few and a chain rarely has more than four or five links.

instruction: I'm going on a trip to Japan soon. What kind of souvenirs should I buy?
reply: Goggles, a swimming costume or trunks, a towel and a padlock for the locker, plus flip-flops for the poolside and a bottle of water. A swim hat if the pool asks for one, and a pound coin for an old locker.

instruction: I'm a stamp collector and I'm having trouble keeping my collection organized. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: One folder or box for each thing you actually have to keep — tax, home, car, health — and one tray for this month. Open the post standing up, over the bin, and deal with each letter once: pay it, file it, or ring the number on it, because a second read is how the pile grows.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Disneyland and I'm interested in behind-the-scenes tours. What's the most popular one?
reply: On any of them: *Knives Out* for a whodunnit everyone enjoys, *Happy Valley* or *The Bear* for a series you'll finish, *Paddington 2* if children are in the room. Say which service and the mood and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm looking for a new exercise machine for my home gym. What's the difference between a leg press and a leg extension?
reply: Both, and they do different jobs: a sit up moves the trunk through a range, so it works the front of the core and the hip flexors, and a plank holds the trunk still, which is the job a back has to do all day. If you have time for one, take the plank - it is the one that carries over to lifting and sitting, and it needs no movement to get wrong - and add crunches after it if you want the curl.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about black holes and neutron stars. What's the main difference between them?
reply: A black hole is a place where matter is packed so tightly that its gravity pulls in everything, even light. Most form when a very massive star runs out of fuel and collapses; we spot them by the way their gravity moves and heats nearby gas.

instruction: I'm feeling tired lately. How many hours of sleep do I need each night?
reply: An extra hour or two is usually the good call after a short night. Let the sleep happen, then open the curtains and get some daylight.

instruction: What is a prime number?
reply: A factor divides into a number exactly - 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12 for 12 - and a multiple is in its times table: 12, 24, 36. A prime factor is a factor that is also prime, so 12 is 2 x 2 x 3.

instruction: I'm going to the beach next week and I need some new resort wear. What are the current fashion trends for resort wear?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: My niece is graduating from high school soon. What are some common ways to celebrate this occasion?
reply: Get something that shows you noticed: a book by an author they mentioned, a better version of something they use every day, or an afternoon planned around their favourite thing. The best gifts are specific to one person, so start from what they talk about.

instruction: I'm planning a family vacation. Do you have any ideas?
reply: Pick one shape and put a time on it, because a free day with no plan turns into the sofa. The ones that cost nothing: a walk with a destination (a park, a canal, a hill, a shop that sells something you like), a free museum or gallery - most have a permanent collection that costs nothing - and the library, which has events, papers and warmth.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my golf swing. Can you tell me the basic steps of a golf swing?
reply: For most club golfers it is not the swing but the aim and the tempo: check that feet, hips and shoulders all point where you want the ball to start, then swing at eight out of ten with a smooth one-two count. Practise half-swings with a 7 iron and brush the grass - the divot should come after the ball.

instruction: I'm going on a trip soon and I'm not sure what electronics to pack.
reply: A power bank is worth it if you are out all day: look for 10,000mAh (about two full charges, pocket-sized) and at least 20W output, so it charges quickly rather than trickling. Anker and Belkin are the reliable ones, around £20 to £35; check it has USB-C output for a modern phone, and keep it in your hand luggage on a plane.

instruction: I'm interested in game development. What programming languages are commonly used?
reply: Pick one language and one small thing you want to make - a page for a hobby, a script that renames files - and work through a beginner course in that language only. Python or JavaScript is the usual start; HTML and CSS first if you want to see a page you build in a browser.

instruction: I'm looking for online courses to learn new skills. Have you heard of Coursera?
reply: Most evening courses are two or three hours of class a week plus about the same again at home, so plan on one evening and four or five hours a week. Ask for the guided learning hours before you enrol, because the college has to publish them, and check the fee: in England, English and maths up to GCSE are free for anyone who does not already have them, and a first level 2 or 3 qualification is often free if you are under 23 or on a low income.

instruction: I'm looking for car insurance. What are the main types?
reply: By law you need third-party cover, which pays for other people's injury and damage but not for your own car. Comprehensive usually costs only a little more over a year, so for anything but a very cheap car it is the better buy.

instruction: What is a wind tunnel?
reply: Wind is air moving from an area of high pressure to one of low pressure, and the sun creates those differences by heating land and sea unevenly. The bigger the pressure gap, the stronger the wind.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to the countryside next week, and I'm worried about the rain. Does rain affect agriculture?
reply: A rain shadow is the dry side of a mountain range: air is forced up the windward side, drops its rain there, and comes down the other side warm and dry. Deserts like the one east of the Rockies sit in a rain shadow.

instruction: I'm looking for a new exercise ball for my home workouts. What size should I get?
reply: Astro trainers or moulded boots, shin pads, shorts and a top you do not mind sweating in, plus water. Most places play on 3G astro, so no studs, and a lot of leagues ask for the same colour top for the whole team - ask the organiser before you buy anything.

instruction: I'm looking for a new outfit for casual events, what's popular in athleisure wear right now?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm worried about the weather. Is a storm coming?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about comets and asteroids. What's the main difference between them?
reply: An asteroid is a lump of rock and metal left over from the birth of the solar system, smaller than a planet and usually irregular in shape. Most circle the Sun in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter; one that enters Earth's atmosphere and burns up is a meteor, and one that lands is a meteorite.

instruction: What are geometric shapes?
reply: A polygon is a closed flat shape made only of straight sides that do not cross. A triangle has 3 sides, a quadrilateral 4, a pentagon 5 and a hexagon 6; a circle is not a polygon because its edge is curved.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to save money while shopping online. Do you know any good price comparison tools?
reply: Buying online gives you a 14-day right to change your mind from the day it arrives, and you only pay the return postage unless the shop says otherwise; buying in a shop gives you no right to change your mind at all, only the shop's own policy. That is the real difference, not the price.

instruction: I'm having trouble managing my time at work. Do you have any tips?
reply: Ask for a private twenty minutes and say it plainly in the first sentence: "I'm not coping with the current load and I want to sort it out before it shows in the work." Then bring two or three specifics - the tasks, the hours, what has slipped - and two things you want changed, because a manager can act on a proposal and rarely on a feeling. Ask what support exists: an employee assistance line, occupational health, flexible hours or a temporary reallocation.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What is protein used for in the body?
reply: Protein is a building material made of chains of amino acids: the body uses it to build and repair muscle, skin, hair and organs, and enzymes are proteins too. Meat, fish, eggs, milk, beans, lentils, nuts and tofu are good sources.

instruction: I'm interested in team sports. What are some popular team sports?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm thinking about getting a pet, but I'm not sure if it's a good idea. What are some benefits of having a pet?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm learning about chemistry in school, and I was wondering what chemistry is all about.
reply: A chemical reaction is when substances rearrange their atoms to make new ones: bonds break, new bonds form, and the starting materials are used up. Burning, rusting, baking and digestion are all reactions, and they usually give out or take in heat.

instruction: I'm looking for a new app to download. What are the main app stores?
reply: An app is a program built for a phone or tablet, installed from the store that came with the device - the App Store on an iPhone, the Play Store on Android. It runs on the phone itself and keeps its own data, so an app and the website of the same name can hold different things, and deleting the app usually takes its data with it.

instruction: I'm learning about heat and temperature in school. What's the difference between the two?
reply: Temperature measures how fast the particles in something are moving: faster particles mean a higher temperature and slower ones mean a lower one. It is not the same as how much heat is stored, which is why a cup of tea and a bath can be the same temperature but hold very different amounts of heat.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to improve my learning skills. What's a good technique for remembering information?
reply: Read a section, then close the book and say its three points out loud before going on - rereading feels like study but the recall is what sticks. Turn each heading into a question first ("what is a supply curve?") and answer it from memory, then write one line per page in your own words.

instruction: I'm learning about adaptation and evolution in school. What's the difference between them?
reply: Living things vary, and the ones whose variations suit their surroundings tend to survive and pass those variations on. Over many generations that selection changes the population: small changes accumulate into new species.

instruction: I'm interested in sports psychology. What is it?
reply: Look for a club that advertises a beginners' or "back to" session rather than a team trials night — most sports now run them, and the standard is friendly. Try three in a month before you judge, and go twice before deciding you are unfit for it, because the first session is always the worst one.

instruction: I've been having this recurring dream for weeks now, where I'm falling from a great height. What could it possibly mean?
reply: Standing up quickly lets blood pool in your legs for a moment before your body tightens the vessels and adjusts, so your head is briefly short of blood and you see stars. Get up in two stages, drink enough water, and see a doctor if you actually faint or it happens most times you stand.

instruction: I'm interested in space exploration. What's the latest on the Mars rover?
reply: A trip to Mars takes about seven months each way with current rockets, because the planets are so far apart. Missions wait for a launch window about every 26 months, when Earth and Mars are lined up best.

instruction: I'm having trouble managing my homework. Do you have any tips?
reply: Most primary homework is 20 to 30 minutes a night by the last years at primary, and about an hour a night in year 7 and up, with a break part way. If a piece runs well past that, write a note to the teacher rather than pushing through it, because homework that takes an hour and ends in tears is usually the wrong homework.

instruction: I'm thinking about my home. What are the main rooms in a house?
reply: On an inside wall of the room you heat most, about 1.4 metres off the floor - roughly eye level - where it feels the same temperature as the middle of the room. Keep it away from radiators, direct sun, a draught from a door or window, and the kitchen's cooking heat, or it reads a temperature nobody is standing in and the boiler works to the wrong number.

instruction: I'm looking for a new running app to track my workouts. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Worth it if you want steps, heart rate and messages without getting the phone out; not worth it if what you really want is a watch that runs for a week. A Garmin or Fitbit goes five days or more and an Apple Watch about one, and an Apple Watch needs an iPhone, so check the pairing before you choose.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about percussion instruments. What's a common percussion instrument?
reply: Get an 8kg drum for a family, a 1,400 spin speed and the best energy rating you can afford: the running cost over ten years beats the purchase price difference. Measure the gap and the door before you order, and check the warranty length.

instruction: What is the difference between a metal and a non-metal?
reply: A metal is an element that conducts heat and electricity, is usually shiny, and can be bent or hammered into shape without breaking: iron, copper, aluminium and gold are metals. Most elements are metals, and they sit on the left and middle of the periodic table.

instruction: I'm looking for dessert ideas. What are some popular types of cookies?
reply: Lemon and sugar is the classic, and butter with golden syrup or jam works as well without the fuss. For savoury, fold cheese and ham inside, or put a fried egg on top.

instruction: I'm feeling tired lately. What are some ways to improve my sleep?
reply: Waking up tired usually means broken sleep rather than too little: a warm room, a drink in the evening, a snoring partner and a phone in bed all fragment it. Try a cooler bedroom, no alcohol within three hours of bed, and the same wake time every day for two weeks, because that last one is what rebuilds a steady night.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What are some herbal sleep supplements?
reply: Tea has enough caffeine to keep you awake if it's after about 2pm, so switch to a herbal one or a warm drink without caffeine in the evening. A milky drink is fine; it's the caffeine and the late loo trip that cost you sleep.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to store my bicycle at home. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pack what you use least first - books, spare bedding, the cupboard under the stairs - and keep a 'first night' box out of the van: kettle, mugs, chargers, loo roll, bedding and a change of clothes. Label boxes by room, do one room an evening for the last three weeks, and get rid of anything you have not touched in a year rather than paying to move it.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I'm not sure why. I usually go to bed at 11 PM and wake up at 7 AM. Is that enough sleep?
reply: An extra hour or two is usually the good call after a short night. Let the sleep happen, then open the curtains and get some daylight.

instruction: I'm looking for some new toys for my cat. What are some popular interactive toys?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm looking for a new YouTube channel to watch. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: *Schitt's Creek* is the safe pick: short episodes, funny from the first series. *Derry Girls* if you want something sharper, or *Paddington 2* if it's a film tonight rather than a series.

instruction: I'm worried about my roof. What's the best way to clean my gutters?
reply: Moss on a roof wants a scraper rather than a pressure washer: scrape it off dry, let the tiles air, and clear the gutters and downpipes so the rain runs away instead of feeding it. Don't pressure-wash an old roof - it strips the surface and finds leaks you did not have.

instruction: I'm concerned about internet censorship. What is it?
reply: The internet is millions of computers agreeing on one way to pass messages - your request is cut into small packets, each labelled with where it is going, and routers hand them on hop by hop until they reach the server. Long fibre cables under the sea carry it between countries, and the reply usually takes well under a tenth of a second.

instruction: It's raining outside and I'm going for a walk. What should I wear?
reply: A waterproof with a hood is the one thing that decides the day, with a thin layer underneath rather than a thick coat, because rain gear is warm once you move. Wear shoes that keep water out - leather or a waterproof boot rather than canvas, which soaks and stays wet - and take a second pair of socks.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. What's a popular genre of music right now?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm trying to get to downtown, is there a bus stop near my location?
reply: A bus is the local service, stopping often along a town route and often turning up without a booking; a coach is for longer journeys between towns, with seats booked in advance, luggage in the hold and few stops. In the UK, National Express and Megabus run coaches.

instruction: I'm looking for an all-inclusive resort for my next vacation. What are some popular options?
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I'm learning about the water cycle in school. What is runoff?
reply: Rain soaks into the ground and runs into rivers, and your tap water is drawn from a river, a reservoir or a borehole, then filtered and treated so nothing can grow in it and pumped to the house under pressure. A town near hills is usually fed from a reservoir; anywhere else it comes from a river or from deep underground.

instruction: I'm a parent and I'm looking for information about the upcoming school play. Do you have any details?
reply: Believe them first and write down what happened, with dates and names, then ask the school for a meeting with the head of year rather than the class teacher alone. Ask what the school will do and when, and keep checking in with your child; if nothing changes in a few weeks, put it in writing and ask to see the head.

instruction: I'm trying to manage my budget better. Are there any apps that can help me?
reply: Pick the one task that slows you down most and learn just that: a 20-minute tutorial on the one thing, then use it on real work the same day. Ask your manager for the training budget by showing what it will save (a day a month, fewer errors); most budgets go unspent because nobody asks.

instruction: I'm trying to save money on groceries. Do you have any tips for meal planning?
reply: Write the week's four meals down before you shop and buy for those, not for the week you imagine. Keep a box in the fridge for what must go first, and put tonight's dinner in it when you unpack.

instruction: I'm looking for some fashion inspiration. Do you have any suggestions?
