reply: Pick a tie a shade darker than your shirt and darker than the suit, and let one bold thing carry it: a patterned tie with a plain shirt, or a patterned shirt with a plain tie. With a navy suit, most things work - burgundy, bottle green, a dark striped tie - and a tie the same colour as the suit is the one to skip.

instruction: I'm looking for a mountain retreat for my next vacation. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What are some nutrient-dense foods I should include in my diet?
reply: Aim for a palm-sized portion of protein at each meal - eggs, milk or yoghurt at breakfast, beans, lentils or chicken at lunch, fish or mince at dinner - which lands most adults near the 0.75g per kilo of body weight they need. Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, tinned fish, eggs, tofu and lentils are the cheapest ways to add it.

instruction: I'm looking for some new recipes to try out, especially ones that have been passed down through families.
reply: Three that work with children, easiest first: flapjack (no oven hands, just stirring and a flat tin), fairy cakes (they can fill the cases and ice them once cool) and shortbread (three ingredients, and cutting shapes is the fun part). Give the little ones the measuring and the stirring and keep the oven and the hob to yourself, and expect it to take twice as long as it would alone.

instruction: I'm starting a new treadmill workout routine and I was wondering how long I should run each day.
reply: Three runs a week is plenty to start, with a rest day between each: two easy runs of 20 to 30 minutes and one a little longer. Add a fourth only when those three feel comfortable, and keep any increase to about 10% a week.

instruction: I'm looking for some information about pet food. What are some healthy options for my dog?
reply: Keep it plain and small: plain chicken with boiled rice, or his own food, in four or five small meals a day rather than one big one. Withhold food for a few hours first if he has been sick, keep the water down, and skip anything fatty or milky.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to store my crafting supplies. Do you have any ideas?
reply: A pantry or larder is a cool, dark, dry cupboard for the food that keeps: tins, dried pasta and rice, flour, sugar, oil, spices. Cool and dry matter more than size - a shelf by a radiator or a sunny window turns flour and rice stale and brings weevils - so put it on an outside wall away from the cooker.

instruction: I heard it might snow tonight. Will it be a lot?
reply: Weather is chaotic: a tiny error in today's readings grows over days, so a forecast a week ahead is a good guess and tomorrow's is usually close. Showers are also small enough to miss your street while soaking the next town, which is why a 30% chance of rain still means a wet walk sometimes.

instruction: I'm planning to visit an amusement park this weekend. What's the admission price for adults?
reply: Two hours and about age-plus-one guests is the sweet spot: one venue or one big activity, food that can be made the day before, and a bag for the way home. At home it costs around £5 a head but you need a wet-weather plan and one adult per four children; a hall or soft-play party at £10 to £15 a head buys you both.

instruction: I have a new puppy at home, and I'm having trouble with house training.
reply: Go back to the basics of toilet training: take him out every hour and after every meal, nap and play, wait five minutes and praise and treat him the moment he goes outside. Clean indoor spots with an enzyme cleaner so no smell is left to return to, and don't scold him after the event, because he can't connect it.

instruction: What should I wear outside today?
reply: Dress for standing about outdoors: shorts or jeans and a light top, with a jumper for when the sun goes in. Leave the white things and the dry-clean-only at home, because there's smoke, grass and someone with a ketchup bottle.

instruction: I'm looking for some new furniture for my living room. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Second-hand furniture is the best value there is, and charity shops and Freecycle are the places to look. Check for woodworm holes, sagging cushions and smoke smell, and measure your door and stairs before you collect anything big.

instruction: I'm having trouble waking up early in the morning. What's a good morning routine to start the day?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: I'm looking for a new TV show to watch. What's popular right now?
reply: *Schitt's Creek* is the safe pick: short episodes, funny from the first series. *Derry Girls* if you want something sharper, or *Paddington 2* if it's a film tonight rather than a series.

instruction: It's going to be really hot today. What kind of clothes should I wear?
reply: Loose, light cotton in a pale colour is the coolest thing to wear, because it lets air through and reflects the sun; a wide hat and sunglasses are worth more than another layer of sunscreen. Keep shoulders covered over a long day and wear shoes you can walk in on hot tarmac.

instruction: I'm worried about the security of my phone apps. What can I do to keep them safe?
reply: On an iPhone it is Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy Restrictions: turn it on, then set the age rating for apps, block in-app purchases, and require a passcode for installs. On Android install Google Family Link and approve apps and screen time from your own phone.

instruction: I'm having some trouble talking to my family. Do you have any tips on how to communicate better with them?
reply: Aim for two real conversations rather than working the room: ask what they are working on and what brought them there, then listen. Have one sentence ready about yourself and follow up with a two-line message the next day.

instruction: I want to cook a healthy meal for my family tonight, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: Cook the same sort of dinner as for anyone, with the starchy part smaller and the vegetables bigger: chicken or fish with two veg, a chilli with beans instead of rice, or an omelette and salad. Halve the potatoes, rice or pasta rather than cutting them out, go wholegrain where you can, skip the sugary drinks, and keep pudding small - and ask them what they usually do rather than guessing.

instruction: I'm interested in starting a container garden on my balcony. What kind of plants are best for this type of gardening?
reply: Flowers, most of the time: go to a florist rather than a garage and ask for what is in season, and a mixed bunch is always safe. A plant lasts years and is the better present for someone who likes looking after things, but give an orchid or a houseplant only to a person who will remember to water it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. I've always liked music, so maybe something related to that.
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm having trouble studying for my exams and I'm looking for some new techniques to try. Have you heard of Elaborative Rehearsal?
reply: Make the task visible and small: one page, one timer, everything else out of the room. Body-doubling works for a lot of people - study alongside someone, in person or on a video call with mics off.

instruction: I'm looking to advance my career, and I was wondering about professional certifications that can help me.
reply: It depends on what you want to do: for nursing, engineering, law or teaching the degree is the door, and for plenty of other jobs experience gets you further for less money. Compare a degree with a degree apprenticeship in the same field — earn while you learn, no fees — and look at what people actually doing the job you want studied.

instruction: I'm learning about sound waves in school and I was wondering, what is a sound wave?
reply: A wave is a moving disturbance that carries energy without carrying the material with it: a sound wave is air particles pushing and pulling, and a water wave is the surface moving up and down while the water stays roughly in place. Light is a wave too, and so is a radio signal.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to get to work. What are my public transportation options?
reply: Plan for half the walking and twice the sitting: one or two things a day with a cafe or a bench between them, and a taxi or the hop-on bus for the long hops rather than marching between sights. Check step-free access before you book, because most museums, galleries and cathedrals publish it, ask the hotel for a room near the lift, and book help ahead on trains and at the airport - it is free, UK rail's Passenger Assist takes bookings up to 24 hours ahead and airports usually want 48.

instruction: I'm going to Japan soon and I want to know what souvenirs I should get.
reply: Goggles, a swimming costume or trunks, a towel and a padlock for the locker, plus flip-flops for the poolside and a bottle of water. A swim hat if the pool asks for one, and a pound coin for an old locker.

instruction: I need a quick weeknight meal idea. What's something simple I can make?
reply: Try a traybake, a stir-fry and a pasta this week: change one of three things and the same dinner comes out new - the shape (traybake, stir-fry, pasta, curry, soup), the carb under it (rice, potatoes, couscous, bread, noodles) or the sauce that finishes it (tomato, yoghurt and lemon, a spice paste, gravy, pesto). Mince is a ragu, a chilli with rice, or a cottage pie.

instruction: I'm looking for some new outdoor furniture for my backyard. What types of materials are available?
reply: Second-hand furniture is the best value there is, and charity shops and Freecycle are the places to look. Check for woodworm holes, sagging cushions and smoke smell, and measure your door and stairs before you collect anything big.

instruction: I'm looking for a new fitness app to help me stay active. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Yes: it builds flexibility and balance and strengthens the muscles that hold you up, and it counts as exercise, though the heart and lungs get less from it than from a brisk walk. Two or three sessions a week is where the change shows, and a weekly class plus ten minutes at home most days is the usual way people keep it up.

instruction: I'm interested in gardening and composting. What's a good way to get started with composting?
reply: Compost is plant waste that has rotted down into dark crumbly stuff that smells of earth: layer green things like grass, peelings and weeds with brown things like cardboard, dead leaves and twiggy prunings, keep it as damp as a wrung-out sponge, and turn it now and then. Six months to a year and it is ready to spread on beds or dig in, and it feeds the soil rather than the plant.

instruction: I'm planning to create a garden in my backyard, but I don't know where to start.
reply: Tidy the outline first, because a garden reads as untidy at its edges before its middle: cut the lawn edge right round with a half-moon edger, clear the path, and weed the first foot of border. Then buy three plants and no more - something tall, something scented by the door, and something that flowers for months - in pots if the soil is poor.

instruction: I'm feeling stuck in my 9-to-5 job. What's the typical work schedule for most office jobs?
reply: A full-time week is usually 37.5 or 40 hours on paper, and the shift shape is what changes the answer. A nurse is contracted to 37.5 hours, worked as three 12-hour shifts a week plus the odd fourth, and a care worker often has the same 12-hour pattern.

instruction: I'm learning about colors and emotions. What color is often linked with happiness?
reply: Blue is scattered much more strongly than green, so the green that is scattered arrives mixed with far more blue and the sky reads as pale blue. Violet is scattered even more, but there is less of it in sunlight and our eyes are less sensitive to it, so it never dominates.

instruction: I was wondering, what happens when sound hits a wall?
reply: Sound goes through a wall more than people expect: earplugs and a heavy curtain or a bookcase against the shared wall take the edge off, and a fan or white noise masks the rest. If it is the room next door, ask them once at a calm time to turn it down after a set hour; if it keeps happening, keep a short log of the times and your council's noise team can act on it.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about string instruments. What's the most popular one?
reply: Start with the treble clef only: the five lines are E, G, B, D, F from the bottom up and the four spaces spell FACE, and ten minutes a day of naming notes off a page is how it sticks. Then the same for the bass clef (Good Boys Do Fine Always on the lines), then note lengths and rests; a beginner tutor book and a free app like Tenuto cover it, and playing each note on the instrument as you name it is the part that makes it real.

instruction: I'm looking for gift ideas for my coworkers. What are some popular corporate gift options?
reply: Get something that shows you noticed: a book by an author they mentioned, a better version of something they use every day, or an afternoon planned around their favourite thing. The best gifts are specific to one person, so start from what they talk about.

instruction: I'm looking for a new movie to watch. What are some popular movie genres?
reply: *Happy Valley* for tense British crime, *The Bear* for short, intense episodes, or *Detectorists* if you want something gentle and funny. All three are easy to watch with a partner.

instruction: I'm learning about animals in school, and I was wondering what a predator is.
reply: A predator is an animal that hunts and eats other animals: a fox, an owl and a lion are predators, and the animals they eat are their prey. Predators keep prey numbers in check, which is why removing them can upset a whole habitat.

instruction: I'm looking for sustainable fashion brands. Do you know any?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I'm trying to get back into my gym routine, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: Five minutes, in two parts: first something easy that gets you slightly out of breath - a brisk walk, a slow jog, skipping, the exercise bike - then a few quick movements through the range you are about to use, like leg swings, arm circles, hip circles and ten bodyweight squats. Start the first set lighter than the rest.

instruction: I'm looking for a new job, what are some popular workplace environments?
reply: Look for the places that sell a lot of one thing: a market hall or a food court, a bakery, a cafe at the back of a shop, a street food van in a regular spot, or the lunch board outside a restaurant that wants the office trade. Walk a street back from the station or the main road, where the rents are lower, and follow the queue of people who work nearby.

instruction: I'm looking for a place to eat. What's the difference between a bistro and a restaurant?
reply: It's restaurant: r-e-s-t-a-u-r-a-n-t, with 'aunt' in the middle after the u. The usual slips are restaraunt and restraunt - remember the au, as in the French it comes from.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with my remote team. Do you have any tips?
reply: Change both batteries - two AAA in nearly all of them, with the shape of the tray showing which way round - and check they are the right way round: a remote that needs the button pressed hard is a battery on its way out - then test it: point it at a phone camera and watch the little light on the end through the screen, which shows on a working remote and never does on a dead one. A remote that tests fine but does nothing is usually unpaired (a Bluetooth or voice remote, paired by holding the two buttons the manual names while the TV is on) or it is sending to the box rather than the set.

instruction: I'm trying to find my personal style, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. What's popular on the music streaming services right now?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier, but I'm not sure how to control my portions.
reply: Cook the same sort of dinner as for anyone, with the starchy part smaller and the vegetables bigger: chicken or fish with two veg, a chilli with beans instead of rice, or an omelette and salad. Halve the potatoes, rice or pasta rather than cutting them out, go wholegrain where you can, skip the sugary drinks, and keep pudding small - and ask them what they usually do rather than guessing.

instruction: I have a job interview tomorrow and I'm feeling really nervous. Do you have any tips for preparing?
reply: Know the route and aim to be ten to fifteen minutes early - not earlier, and never late; if you are ahead of that, wait in a cafe rather than the lobby. The night before, put the clothes out, print the job description and your notes, charge your phone and note the name of whoever you are meeting.

instruction: I'm hungry, what types of food are there?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm looking for a new fitness tracker. What's the most popular one right now?
reply: Worth it if you want steps, heart rate and messages without getting the phone out; not worth it if what you really want is a watch that runs for a week. A Garmin or Fitbit goes five days or more and an Apple Watch about one, and an Apple Watch needs an iPhone, so check the pairing before you choose.

instruction: I'm learning about the solar system in school. What is the biggest planet?
reply: Jupiter is the biggest planet: about 143,000 km across, or 11 Earths side by side, and more than twice as massive as all the other planets put together. It is a gas giant with no solid surface to stand on.

instruction: I heard it snowed in New York yesterday. Is that true?
reply: Snow forms when water vapour freezes straight into ice crystals high in a cloud, and the crystals stick together as they fall. It only reaches the ground as snow if the air stays cold all the way down, which is why a cold snap often brings sleet instead.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school. What is the main part of a plant that makes food?
reply: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis: they take carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil and use sunlight to turn them into sugar. The green chlorophyll in their leaves captures the light, and oxygen is released as a by-product.

instruction: I'm concerned about climate change. What is urban climate?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm going to Japan soon and I want to bring back some souvenirs for my friends and family. What are some local crafts I should look for?
reply: Cheap food that people finish and that travels: a big bowl of pasta salad, sausage rolls or sausages on sticks, cheese and crackers, and a tray of fairy cakes. Keep it to things you can make the day before, and buy the paper plates.

instruction: I'm having trouble keeping track of my school assignments. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Count the days you actually have (sleep and school nights are not revision), list the topics per subject, and give each topic one block rather than one subject one day: three blocks a day is a real day's work. Put the subject you dread first, in the morning.

instruction: I'm looking for a new bed. What types of mattresses are there?
reply: Before you buy one, try the cheap fixes: a firm board under the mattress, rotating it, and a pillow between your knees if you sleep on your side. If it's over eight years old or you wake with back pain most mornings, a medium-firm mattress is the usual recommendation.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and overwhelmed. What are some ways to relax?
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move.

instruction: I'm trying to stay hydrated, but I drink a lot of coffee. Does caffeine affect hydration?
reply: No, not in ordinary amounts: a cup of tea or coffee is mostly water, and the caffeine in it makes you pass only a little more than the drink gave you, so it counts towards your fluids. The six-to-eight-glasses figure includes them.

instruction: I have a big family with lots of siblings. What are some common communication styles among siblings?
reply: Don't try to be the parent yet: be a reliable adult who is not in charge of the rules and let their actual parent do the discipline for a while. Keep the offers small and repeated - a lift, a snack they like, a show you both watch - because loyalty to the other parent is usually what is behind the hostility.

instruction: I'm looking for new athletic shoes. What are some popular brands?
reply: Astro trainers or moulded boots, shin pads, shorts and a top you do not mind sweating in, plus water. Most places play on 3G astro, so no studs, and a lot of leagues ask for the same colour top for the whole team - ask the organiser before you buy anything.

instruction: What is a force in physics?
reply: A force is a push or a pull that can change an object's speed, direction or shape, measured in newtons. Gravity, friction and the push of a hand are all forces, and an object with no net force keeps doing what it was doing.

instruction: What is a wedge?
reply: A trivet is the stand that keeps something hot off the table or the counter - a pan, a casserole, a slow cooker's pot. Wooden, cork, stone or metal, all it does is hold the heat away from the surface; a folded dry towel does the same job when the trivet is not there.

instruction: I'm trying to get in shape and I'm looking for a good cardio workout.
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm looking for ways my parents can help me with my studies. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Ask other parents at the school gate first: a sitter vouched for by someone you know beats any app. Then do one evening while you are still in the house, paying them to play while you get on with something, so the first real night out isn't the first time.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about the future of energy. What are some alternative energy sources?
reply: Energy is the ability to make something happen - to move, heat, light or power something - and it is never used up, only changed from one form into another. Food stores chemical energy, a moving bike has kinetic energy, and a hot cup has thermal energy.

instruction: I'm looking for some ideas for wall art in my living room. What are some popular types of wall art?
reply: Paint it all one pale colour, ceiling included, and put a mirror where it catches a window: the eye reads the reflection as another room. Hang the curtains at ceiling height rather than at the window, keep the floor visible, and use one rug that stops short of the walls rather than carpet that runs wall to wall.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about carpooling incentives in my city. Are there any programs available?
reply: Ask work first, then price the journey three ways before you buy anything: a season ticket only beats weekly or daily tickets above about three days a week, a flexi ticket or a carnet covers two or three days, and a railcard pays for itself in about a dozen trips if you qualify for one. If you drive, park and ride, a lift-share board or a parking space a ten-minute walk out usually undercuts the station car park, and asking whether your employer does a season ticket loan or a cycle-to-work scheme is free money in effect.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about golf. Is it a popular sport?
reply: For most club golfers it is not the swing but the aim and the tempo: check that feet, hips and shoulders all point where you want the ball to start, then swing at eight out of ten with a smooth one-two count. Practise half-swings with a 7 iron and brush the grass - the divot should come after the ball.

instruction: What is the difference between an element and a compound?
reply: A compound is two or more different elements chemically joined in fixed proportions: water is hydrogen and oxygen, and table salt is sodium and chlorine. Unlike a mixture, the elements in a compound cannot be separated just by filtering or boiling.

instruction: I'm learning about genetics in school. What is DNA?
reply: DNA is the long molecule that carries the instructions for building and running a living thing, written in a four-letter code. Genes are sections of it, and they are copied from parents to offspring.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. What's the difference between pop and rock music?
reply: A rock is a solid piece of the earth made of one or more minerals: granite is mostly quartz and feldspar, and limestone is mostly calcite. Rocks come in three kinds - igneous from cooled magma, sedimentary from settled layers, and metamorphic changed by heat and pressure.

instruction: I'm looking for some fun activities to do with my family this weekend. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to stay fit at home, do you have any suggestions?
reply: For two or three nights: one change of clothes plus a layer, one pair of comfortable walking shoes, toiletries in a bag, phone charger and any tickets. Roll clothes to fit more in, and leave the "just in case" outfit at home.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about the first computer. What was it?
reply: For essays, video calls and Netflix, almost anything current works: 8GB RAM, a 256GB SSD and a 14 inch screen, around £400 to £550. A Chromebook is fine if everything lives in Google Docs, but avoid it for a course that needs Windows software.

instruction: I'm going on a trip to Paris soon and I want to buy some souvenirs for my family and friends. What are some popular souvenir ideas?
reply: Get something that shows you noticed: a book by an author they mentioned, a better version of something they use every day, or an afternoon planned around their favourite thing. The best gifts are specific to one person, so start from what they talk about.

instruction: I'm interested in the Olympics. Have there been any controversies?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: What is a fraction?
reply: A fraction is a part of a whole written as one number over another: the bottom says how many equal pieces the whole is cut into and the top says how many of those you have, so 3/4 is three pieces out of four. The one thing that trips people up is that the same amount has lots of names - 2/4 is 1/2, and 0.5 is 1/2 too - which is why you can simplify and compare them by putting them over the same bottom number.

instruction: I'm looking for some inspiration for my digital art. Can you tell me about some popular styles?
reply: Make the shape, not the whole outfit: black leggings and a black top read as almost anything, then one thing does the work - a cardboard box for a robot or a rocket, a bin bag and a belt for a cape, a paper plate and elastic for a mask, a stripy top and an eye patch for a pirate. Paint it the night before, not the morning of, and ask the party's theme first.

instruction: I'm learning about the life cycle of trees. What is the first stage?
reply: A life cycle is the stages a living thing goes through from one generation to the next: a frog goes egg, tadpole, froglet, adult, and a butterfly goes egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. A plant's is seed, seedling, flowering plant, then seed again.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to make my daily commute easier. I've heard of park and ride options, but I'm not sure how they work.
reply: Plan the outing around the walking. Go door to door - a taxi, or the bus that stops nearest the door - and make a bench or a cafe the turning point so the trip is two short walks with a sit in between.

instruction: I'm training for my first 5K run and I'm not sure how to start. What should I do first?
reply: For a first 10k, build up to three runs a week and add about 10% to your longest run weekly, with the last long run a fortnight before race day. If you can run 5k comfortably now, eight to ten weeks is a realistic build.

instruction: I'm learning about erosion in school. What's the difference between weathering and erosion?
reply: Weathering is rock being broken up where it sits, by rain, frost, wind, roots or weak acid, without being carried away. Erosion is the next step: the loosened pieces being moved somewhere else.

instruction: I'm looking for information about different job categories. What are some main categories?
reply: For a commute: *The Rest Is History* (30 to 50 minutes, always interesting), *The Diary of a CEO* for long interviews, or *Short History Of...* for 40-minute stories. All work with one earbud in.

instruction: I'm looking for a new pair of loafers, what are some popular styles?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm thinking about starting to bike to work. What are the benefits of bike commuting?
reply: Worth it if the alternative is driving: a pedal-assist bike flattens the hills and the headwind, so a commute you would skip on a bad day still happens, for a few pence of electricity a charge and no tax or parking. It saves little against a bus pass and keeps you less fit unless you turn the assist down.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about community diversity. What does it mean?
reply: It means the wider view rather than this one detail. What decision is it for?

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What colors are best for a bedroom?
reply: Pick the thing you cannot change - the floor, the tiles, the worktop, the sofa - and take the wall colour out of it in a paler version of itself. Then add one deeper tone from the same family for a rug or cushions and a wood or a metal to warm it: three colours, one of them a near-neutral.

instruction: I'm planning to visit an amusement park this weekend and I want to know if you can help me navigate the park.
reply: Parkrun is a free, timed 5k every Saturday at 9am in a local park: register once online, print or screenshot your barcode, and turn up ten minutes early for the first-timers' briefing. Walkers are genuinely welcome and plenty of people walk it, so you will not be last on your own.

instruction: I'm worried about my smartphone's security. What's the most common way hackers get into phones?
reply: Change the password from a device you trust, then look at what the intruder set up: a recovery email, a forwarding rule, a connected app. Turn on two-factor with an app rather than a text, tell the contacts it messaged not to send money, and use the account's own report-a-hack page so it reviews the logins.

instruction: I'm worried about traffic and the environment. Is traffic bad for the environment?
reply: Get left and off the carriageway if you still can, then hazards on. Everyone out of the doors on the left, behind the barrier, and well back from the car: never stand between it and the traffic, and never change a wheel on a motorway.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting some smart home devices, but I'm worried about my privacy. Are smart speakers always listening?
reply: Keep it at about 60% for no more than 60 minutes at a time - that is the rule hearing specialists give, and phones now warn you when you go past it. If someone a metre away can hear your music, it is too loud; noise-cancelling earphones help because you stop turning it up over the background.

instruction: I'm having trouble with traffic signals in my area. Can you tell me why some traffic lights have three colors and others have four?
reply: Lights are the law between sunset and sunrise, and worth using in daylight as well: a flashing rear light is what makes a driver look twice in rain or at dusk. Use a steady front light bright enough to see the road by - 400 lumens is plenty in town - and a rear light at saddle height, not on your bag where a coat covers it.

instruction: I'm worried about my online privacy on social media. What can I do to protect myself?
reply: On Instagram it is Settings > Account privacy > Private account; on Facebook, Settings > Privacy > Who can see what you share set to Friends, and on TikTok, Settings and privacy > Privacy > Private account. Private means new people have to ask to follow you, but it does not hide anything from the people already following, so check that list too.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about famous basketball players. Can you tell me about Michael Jordan?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a dog, but I've never had one before. What are some basic things I should know about training?
reply: The day is the whole job: a short walk first thing, a proper one later, a last five minutes before bed, a garden break after every meal, and food twice a day for an adult or three or four small meals for a puppy. Then the boring parts that keep him well - a microchip (law in the UK), a yearly check and booster at the vet, worming every three months and flea treatment monthly, and insurance taken out before anything is wrong with him.

instruction: I'm going to the mall this weekend and I want to do some window shopping. What are some popular products right now?
reply: Something comfortable and a step nicer than you'd wear at home: jeans with a good top, or a dress with flat shoes. Nothing that needs careful handling next to red wine on someone's sofa.

instruction: I'm learning about genetics and I was wondering, what is DNA?
reply: DNA is the long molecule that carries the instructions for building and running a living thing, written in a four-letter code. Genes are sections of it, and they are copied from parents to offspring.

instruction: I'm having trouble remembering some formulas for my math test. Do you know any good ways to remember them?
reply: Ask in person after class with one specific thing ("I get the formula but I can't do the last question on the sheet"), and say what you've already tried. Teachers help far more often than students expect, and an email the same day saying thank you makes them remember you next time.

instruction: I'm learning about tessellations in school. What is a tessellation?
reply: A quadrilateral is a flat shape with four straight sides and four corners, and its angles add up to 360 degrees. Squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombuses, trapeziums and kites are all quadrilaterals; a shape with four sides that is not a quadrilateral does not exist.

instruction: I'm a high school student graduating soon and I was wondering, what's the origin of graduation caps and gowns?
reply: It means quick and on top of things. What is it they are on top of?

instruction: I'm looking for pet food for my cat, but she has food allergies. What are some common dietary restrictions for cats?
reply: Two measured meals a day for an adult cat, adding up to about 3 or 4 pouches of 85g for a 4kg cat, or 40-50g of dry, and less for a cat that sleeps all day: a complete cat food, wet or wet with a little dry. Cats are obligate carnivores, so no dog food and no vegetarian diet, and a cat should never go more than a day without eating.

instruction: I need to measure the length of my room. What's the difference between a meter and a yard?
reply: For a rectangle, area = length × width; for a triangle, ½ × base × height; for a circle, π × radius². Keep all the measurements in the same unit.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for new teaching methods. What do you think about peer teaching?
reply: Show it once, then watch them do it once, then let them do it alone with you a few feet away: most of what looks like slowness is a step nobody said out loud. Write the five or six steps on one page they can keep, do the same fifteen minutes at the same time each day rather than a long session on Friday, and ask them to explain it back to you before you decide it has not gone in - if they cannot explain it, the teaching missed rather than the learner.

instruction: It's a beautiful sunny day today. What does sunshine do for plants?
reply: Plants use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide from the air and water from the soil into sugar, which is their food, and they release oxygen as a by-product. The green chlorophyll in their leaves captures the light that powers it.

instruction: I'm looking for some discounts on electronics. Are there any flash sales happening?
reply: Ask the person who can say yes, not the till: "is there anything you can do on the price?" Have a number and somewhere cheaper to point at, and ask about ex-display or last season's colour. At a market or on a big ticket offer about 10 per cent under, ready to walk away; a shop that cannot move can often throw in delivery instead.

instruction: I'm new to the gym and I'm not sure what to do. What's the most important thing to remember when I'm working out?
reply: Five minutes, in two parts: first something easy that gets you slightly out of breath - a brisk walk, a slow jog, skipping, the exercise bike - then a few quick movements through the range you are about to use, like leg swings, arm circles, hip circles and ten bodyweight squats. Start the first set lighter than the rest.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something I can do at home. I was thinking about cooking.
reply: Pick the one thing you would happily be bad at, and buy the cheapest version: a ten pound ukulele, a second-hand chess set, a supermarket sketchbook and pencils. Keep it in the room where you sit, and give it twenty minutes twice a week.

instruction: I'm trying to get in shape, but I don't know where to start.
reply: Five minutes, in two parts: first something easy that gets you slightly out of breath - a brisk walk, a slow jog, skipping, the exercise bike - then a few quick movements through the range you are about to use, like leg swings, arm circles, hip circles and ten bodyweight squats. Start the first set lighter than the rest.

instruction: I'm looking for a new TV show to binge-watch. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: *Schitt's Creek* is the safe pick: short episodes, funny from the first series. *Derry Girls* if you want something sharper, or *Paddington 2* if it's a film tonight rather than a series.

instruction: I'm trying to learn more about vitamins and supplements. What's the main difference between them?
reply: A vitamin is a nutrient the body needs in small amounts and cannot make enough of, so it has to come from food: vitamin C is in fruit and vegetables, vitamin A in carrots and dairy, and vitamin D is made in skin from sunlight. A varied diet usually covers them.

instruction: I'm worried about water pollution. What is it?
reply: Acid rain forms when sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning coal and oil mix with water in the air and fall as weak acid. It harms trees and lakes; filters on power stations and cleaner fuel have cut it a lot since the 1980s.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. What are some common sleep disorders?
reply: Long sleeps now and then are just a debt being paid, especially after a run of short nights. Needing nine or ten hours most nights and still waking flat is worth a GP visit: an underactive thyroid, low iron, low vitamin D, depression and sleep apnoea all show up that way, and each is easy to test for.

instruction: I'm trying to organize my small apartment and I don't know where to start.
reply: Write down what comes in each month, then what goes out in two piles: the fixed ones (rent, bills, travel, debt) and the ones you decide week by week (food, going out, clothes). What is left is what you can save or throw at a debt, and if the piles add up to more than comes in, cut from the weekly ones first because that is where the slack is.

instruction: I'm going to a wedding and I need to know what color tie to wear with a black suit.
reply: Pick a tie a shade darker than your shirt and darker than the suit, and let one bold thing carry it: a patterned tie with a plain shirt, or a patterned shirt with a plain tie. With a navy suit, most things work - burgundy, bottle green, a dark striped tie - and a tie the same colour as the suit is the one to skip.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Costa Rica and I'm looking for eco-lodges. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: The council's green bin is the cheapest route if you have one - many charge for the subscription and collect fortnightly - and the tip has a green waste skip. Grass, leaves and prunings can go in a compost bin at home too, but leave out cooked food, weeds in seed and anything diseased.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. What are some popular crafting activities?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I want to learn about ecosystems. What is an ecosystem?
reply: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the non-living parts they depend on - soil, water, air and sunlight - interacting in one place. A pond, a woodland and a garden are ecosystems, and they work because energy flows through them and materials are recycled.

instruction: I'm a huge fan of live concerts. What's the best way to find out about upcoming concerts in my area?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm planning a group trip to Paris with my friends. Can you tell me what time of year is best to visit?
reply: Book the room as soon as the date is fixed if it is a weekend, a city or a wedding - four to six weeks ahead is enough for most trips, and three months or more for a popular place in summer or a bank holiday. Midweek and January are where last-minute hunting pays.

instruction: I'm looking for information about different types of food. What's your favorite type of cuisine?
reply: Pick a dish that is good on its own rather than meat with the meat left out: a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, a mushroom and lentil lasagne, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. One proper veggie main plus the usual sides is plenty, and it is worth asking what they actually eat, because vegetarian covers a wide range.

instruction: I'm interested in painting as a hobby. What are some common painting mediums?
reply: White spirit for oil-based gloss, water for water-based paint, and only a little: about one part white spirit to ten parts paint, stirred in rather than shaken, and no more than about a tenth of water in emulsion or water-based gloss. More than that and the paint stops forming a film, so it dries patchy and the sheen goes.

instruction: I'm wondering about the different types of rainfall. What are some main types?
reply: Precipitation is water falling out of the sky - rain, snow, sleet or hail - when droplets in a cloud join up until they are too heavy to stay up. It is one step of the water cycle, after evaporation and condensation.

instruction: I'm looking for a city break in Europe. What are some popular destinations?
reply: Use the habits that work in any city after dark: stay on the busy, lit streets, take a licensed taxi or the metro rather than a shortcut, keep the phone out of sight and the bag in front of you, and ask the hotel desk which two or three streets to avoid - they know this week's answer better than any guide. Carry a card with the hotel address.

instruction: I'm looking for some ideas for summer decorations for my home. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Shade the table, not the whole garden: a cantilever parasol is the one that works, because its base sits off to the side and the canopy reaches over the table without a pole in the middle. Second is a sail shade on three posts, set so it faces the afternoon sun and angled 20 to 30 degrees, with the fixings tight enough that it does not flap; take it down when it blows hard, because a sail in a gale pulls the posts out.

instruction: I'm having trouble taking notes in class. Do you have any tips?
reply: Testing yourself is what makes things stick; rereading notes mostly feels productive without being so. Turn each topic into five questions and answer them with the book shut, then check, and redo the ones you got wrong tomorrow and again in a week.

instruction: What's the difference between a mixture and a solution?
reply: A solution is a mixture where one substance dissolves in another: the dissolved substance is the solute and the liquid it goes into is the solvent. Salt water and sugar water are solutions, and the dissolved part cannot be filtered out.

instruction: I'm planning a family gathering for the holidays. What are some popular family celebration ideas?
reply: Cheap party food people actually eat: a big pot of chilli or a pasta bake, garlic bread, and a bowl of crisps and dips. For standing-up food, sausage rolls, cheese straws and fruit on sticks go further than anything fiddly.

instruction: I'm looking for a fun music festival to attend this summer. What are some popular ones?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm planning to walk around the city today. What should I wear?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting some smart home devices. What are some popular ones?
reply: iPhone if you want the long updates and everything to talk to the rest of the family's; Android if you want to spend less, get two days of battery, or keep a headphone jack. The cheapest way in is a two-year-old iPhone or a mid-range Samsung, and both last well if you put a case on them.

instruction: I'm thinking about my family. What is family?
reply: Stop bidding for the verdict: you will not win the argument about who is favoured, and a parent who has done it for thirty years will not suddenly see it. Say the one thing you want from them, once and plainly - "I'd like you to ask about my week too" - and put the effort into the relationship you can build with your brother or sister directly, rather than through your parents.

instruction: I'm worried about pollution in my city. Is it really bad for my health?
reply: Secondhand smoke is a real risk, not a smell: it carries the same tar, carbon monoxide and carcinogens, and living with a smoker raises a non-smoker's lung cancer risk by roughly a quarter and a child's risk of chest and ear infections much more. There is no safe level of exposure, and an open window or a separate room does not clear it - the only thing that works is smoking outside, away from the door.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about theater history. Can you tell me when the first theater was built?
reply: Ancient Egyptians built them about 4,500 years ago, around 2560 BC for the Great Pyramid of Giza, as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu. The workers were organised, paid labourers, not slaves, hauling stone on ramps and sledges.

instruction: I'm trying to study for a test and I was thinking of using flashcards. Do they really work?
reply: Reading in dim light does not damage your eyes - it tires them, and a tired eye feels sore, waters and gives you a headache. What helps is light that comes from the side or over your shoulder and lands on the page rather than from behind you onto the screen: a lamp at about 40 to 60cm, a little behind your shoulder, and a warm-white LED of 6 to 9 watts is plenty for a book.

instruction: I'm trying to organize my home for summer. What are some things I should get rid of?
reply: A rug, a cool bag with a freezer block, plates and cups you do not mind losing, a bottle opener, napkins, a bin bag and water. Skip anything heavy with mayonnaise unless it is eaten within the hour: sausage rolls, cheese, fruit and a flask keep for hours.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school. What's a simple machine?
reply: The CPU is the chip that runs the instructions in every program; its speed is quoted in gigahertz and how many jobs it can do at once in cores. For everyday use - a browser, video calls, a spreadsheet - a mid-range chip from the last few years feels the same as a fast one, and more memory or an SSD makes a bigger difference.

instruction: I'm looking for a budget-friendly meal plan for my family. Can you suggest some affordable options?
reply: Decide the shape before the menu: a sit-down meal is about £35 to £60 a head catered and a buffet or hog roast about £20 to £35, while doing it yourselves lands near £10 to £15 a head and costs you the day. Work back from the number of guests - 60 people is a caterer's job unless you have a big kitchen and willing help - and ask the venue first, because many barns and halls either insist on their own list or charge corkage and a kitchen fee.

instruction: I'm looking for a new camera. What's the difference between a DSLR and a mirrorless camera?
reply: A mirror is glass with a thin layer of silver or aluminium on the back, and light bounces off that layer at the same angle it arrived - in at 30 degrees, out at 30 degrees, which is why you see yourself where the reflection says you are. The glass only protects the silver, so a mirror that has gone patchy has lost that coating rather than got dirty.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to improve my performance at work. What are some key factors that affect job performance?
reply: Two sentences: your job title and what you actually do in a week, then one thing you have changed or finished. "I am a warehouse team leader - I run a shift of eight, and I have just moved us onto scanners, which cut picking errors." Thirty seconds is plenty; they are testing whether you can be brief and whether the last job taught you anything.

instruction: I'm looking for a new book to read. What are some popular literary awards?
reply: For funny, *The Thursday Murder Club* by Richard Osman is the easy pick: short chapters, a mystery that keeps moving, and jokes on every page. *Three Men in a Boat* if you want an old one that still makes people laugh out loud, or *Good Omens* by Pratchett and Gaiman for something daft and warm.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to get some exercise. Do you know any local walking groups I could join?
reply: Walking counts, and brisk walking for 30 minutes most days does most of what a gentle gym session would for your heart and mood. Add two short strength sessions a week for muscle and bone, and pick up the pace until you are slightly out of breath.

instruction: I was thinking about my family. I have two siblings. Do you know anything about siblings?
reply: A grown sibling's jealousy is usually about one visible difference - a house, a partner, a job, or the way a parent treats you - so do not defend your life or list your own hard parts, which reads as scoring points. Name it once, plainly and without blame: 'I know this has not been easy to watch.' Then keep the relationship on ground that is not a comparison, and if every visit turns into digs or competition, make them shorter and more structured.

instruction: I'm looking for a new gaming keyboard. What's a good brand?
reply: For a first piano, the thing that matters is weighted, full-size keys: a second-hand 88-key digital piano from Yamaha, Roland or Casio is 200 to 350 pounds and is the cheapest thing that teaches real finger strength. A 61-key keyboard with plastic keys is fine for a month to see if you like it, but it will not teach you to play, so hire or borrow one first if the money is tight - shops rent them monthly.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to, I like rock music.
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm trying to get in shape for soccer season. What's a good way to improve my endurance?
reply: It is nearly always the weekly distance going up too fast: keep the increase under about a tenth a week and hold it steady every fourth week. Run most of it easy enough to talk in full sentences, with one faster session and one longer run, and do two short strength sessions a week for calves, glutes and hips, which is what covers most running injuries.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about basketball. What's the objective of the game?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I was wondering, what are some common uses of magnets in everyday life?
reply: A magnet is an object that produces a magnetic field, which pulls on iron, nickel and cobalt and pushes or pulls on other magnets. In most fridge magnets the field comes from tiny magnetic regions lined up in the same direction; in a compass needle it comes from a small piece of magnetised metal.

instruction: I want to learn about roasting vegetables in the oven. What temperature should I use?
reply: Cut vegetables into similar-sized pieces, toss them with oil and salt and roast at 200C (180C fan) for 30 to 40 minutes, turning once. Give them space on the tray; a crowded tray steams instead of roasting.

instruction: I'm interested in airplanes. What are some common types of aircraft?
reply: A wing is shaped so air moves faster over the top than underneath, and the pressure difference pushes the wing up; that force is called lift. Engines provide the forward thrust, and lift grows with speed until it beats the plane's weight.

instruction: I have two siblings, an older brother and a younger sister. What's the birth order in my family?
reply: Stop bidding for the verdict: you will not win the argument about who is favoured, and a parent who has done it for thirty years will not suddenly see it. Say the one thing you want from them, once and plainly - "I'd like you to ask about my week too" - and put the effort into the relationship you can build with your brother or sister directly, rather than through your parents.

instruction: I'm planning to start running. What are the basic things I need to get started?
reply: Start with run-walk: three minutes of easy running, two minutes of walking, five times, three days a week, and add a minute of running each week. Build up for six weeks before you add speed, keep every run slow enough to talk, and expect the first fortnight to feel harder than it looks.

instruction: I'm looking for an alternative to taxis. What options do I have?
reply: Giving up driving is three jobs, and doing them in this order makes it much easier. First the official side: if the reason is medical, tell the DVLA, because a licence you should not be using is not valid for insurance, and tell your insurer either way.

instruction: I'm planning to grill some burgers this weekend. What's the best way to preheat the grill?
reply: An oven grill wants about five minutes preheating with the door shut, with the shelf 10cm or so below the element: the element should be glowing red across its whole length, and a drop of water flicked at the pan should sizzle. Food that browns in a minute and stays raw inside means the shelf is too high, not that the grill is too hot.

instruction: I'm learning about communities in school. What is a community?
reply: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the non-living parts they depend on - soil, water, air and sunlight - interacting in one place. A pond, a woodland and a garden are ecosystems, and they work because energy flows through them and materials are recycled.

instruction: I'm looking to return a shirt I bought online, but I'm not sure about the store's return policy.
reply: Changed your mind? Bought online, by phone or by post, you have 14 days from the day it arrives to say so and another 14 to send it back, for any reason, and the refund covers the standard delivery.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about keyboard instruments. What's the difference between a piano and a keyboard?
reply: For a first piano, the thing that matters is weighted, full-size keys: a second-hand 88-key digital piano from Yamaha, Roland or Casio is 200 to 350 pounds and is the cheapest thing that teaches real finger strength. A 61-key keyboard with plastic keys is fine for a month to see if you like it, but it will not teach you to play, so hire or borrow one first if the money is tight - shops rent them monthly.

instruction: What is a hammer used for?
reply: A lever is a bar that turns on a pivot, and it lets a small push move a big weight if the pivot sits close to the weight: a crowbar, a wheelbarrow, a see-saw and a bottle opener are all levers.

instruction: I'm craving something sweet. What are some popular dessert types?
reply: Sweet: honey or jam with a spoon of peanut butter, stewed apple with cinnamon, or frozen berries stirred in while it is hot. Savoury: butter, salt and a poached egg, or grated cheese and black pepper - porridge is only oats cooked in water or milk, so it takes either, and the salt is what makes the sweet version taste of something.

instruction: I'm trying to get back into strength training, what are some basic exercises I should start with?
reply: Learn five movements and ignore everything else for a month: squat, hinge (deadlift), push, pull and carry. Two or three sessions a week, three sets of 8–12, adding a little weight each time.

instruction: I'm thinking about getting a pet for my family, especially my kids. What are the benefits of having a pet for children?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I'm a coach for a soccer team and I'm looking for some general team training tips.
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm looking for a new baking tool. What is a pastry brush used for?
reply: A pastry brush is the small brush for glazing and greasing: beaten egg on a pie lid, milk on a bun, melted butter in a tin, a wash of syrup on a warm cake. Silicone takes the heat and washes clean; a bristle brush gives a finer finish but sheds, so keep it for cool jobs.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for new ideas on how to get my students to work together more effectively in groups.
reply: Show it once, then watch them do it once, then let them do it alone with you a few feet away: most of what looks like slowness is a step nobody said out loud. Write the five or six steps on one page they can keep, do the same fifteen minutes at the same time each day rather than a long session on Friday, and ask them to explain it back to you before you decide it has not gone in - if they cannot explain it, the teaching missed rather than the learner.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you have any tips on how to establish a bedtime routine?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school. What is the life cycle of a plant?
reply: A life cycle is the stages a living thing goes through from one generation to the next: a frog goes egg, tadpole, froglet, adult, and a butterfly goes egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. A plant's is seed, seedling, flowering plant, then seed again.

instruction: I want to lose weight. What's the best way to start?
reply: Change a few things you can keep doing rather than going on a diet: fill half the plate with vegetables, put protein in every meal so you are not hungry an hour later, swap sugary drinks for water or squash, and walk for half an hour a day. Losing about 0.5 to 1kg a week is the rate that stays off, and the plan that works is the one you would still follow in a year.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan and I want to take some amazing photos and videos. Do you have any tips for travel photography?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I'm a big fan of basketball. Who's considered the greatest of all time?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I'm a big fan of the Chicago Cubs. What is their home stadium?
reply: The side streets five to ten minutes further out are where the free and cheap spaces are: read the sign at the entrance, because a residents' bay or a one-hour limit is what the tickets come from. For a station or a town centre, the station car park or a park and ride is usually cheaper than the multi-storey, and the parking apps (RingGo, PayByPhone, JustPark) show the live price and let you top up from your phone.

instruction: I'm planning to start going to the gym. What are some basic exercises I should do?
reply: Find a club that teaches technique rather than a fitness boxercise class - most amateur clubs run beginners' sessions and lend gloves and wraps for the first few. Go twice a week, expect the first month to be footwork, stance and the basic four punches on your own, and tell the coach you have not boxed before so nobody puts you in to spar.

instruction: It's going to be cold tomorrow, what should I wear?
reply: Loose, light cotton in a pale colour is the coolest thing to wear, because it lets air through and reflects the sun; a wide hat and sunglasses are worth more than another layer of sunscreen. Keep shoulders covered over a long day and wear shoes you can walk in on hot tarmac.

instruction: I'm looking for some ideas to decorate my living room. I want to add some plants.
reply: Flowers, most of the time: go to a florist rather than a garage and ask for what is in season, and a mixed bunch is always safe. A plant lasts years and is the better present for someone who likes looking after things, but give an orchid or a houseplant only to a person who will remember to water it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new exercise routine and I've heard about HIIT. What is it?
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm feeling tired at work. Is it okay to take a nap?
reply: A short nap is worth having: 20 minutes, ideally before about 3pm, and set an alarm, because 90 minutes leaves you groggier than when you lay down. It helps most if you lost sleep the night before or you are driving later.

instruction: I was reading about animals that can sense magnetism. Is that true?
reply: Magnetism is the force a magnet exerts on other magnets and on iron, nickel and cobalt, carried by a magnetic field around the magnet. Like poles repel and opposite poles attract, and a compass needle is a tiny magnet lining up with Earth's field.

instruction: I'm planning to visit the mall this weekend. What are some common types of anchor stores?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I'm having some trouble with my family. We always seem to be arguing about something.
reply: Pick the thing that matters most and say it once, calmly, as your own view: 'We do that our way here, and it isn't up for debate.' Let your partner handle their own parent where you can, and praise what works; most of this eases once the limits are predictable.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. Do you have any tips for meal planning?
reply: Cook the same sort of dinner as for anyone, with the starchy part smaller and the vegetables bigger: chicken or fish with two veg, a chilli with beans instead of rice, or an omelette and salad. Halve the potatoes, rice or pasta rather than cutting them out, go wholegrain where you can, skip the sugary drinks, and keep pudding small - and ask them what they usually do rather than guessing.

instruction: I'm watching an ice hockey game and I'm not sure about some of the penalties. What's a hooking penalty?
reply: Five players from each team take a penalty each, in turn, and the side that scores more wins; if it is still level after all ten, it goes to sudden death, one each until one side misses. Everyone else waits on the halfway line, the keeper has to keep one foot on the line, and the same player cannot take twice until everyone who can has taken one.

instruction: I'm interested in the Olympics. What city hosted the Summer Olympics in 2012?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: I'm looking for a carpool to work. Can you help me find one?
reply: Look for the places that sell a lot of one thing: a market hall or a food court, a bakery, a cafe at the back of a shop, a street food van in a regular spot, or the lunch board outside a restaurant that wants the office trade. Walk a street back from the station or the main road, where the rents are lower, and follow the queue of people who work nearby.

instruction: I'm having trouble with basic addition. Can you help me?
reply: Work in this order: brackets, then powers or roots, then multiplication and division left to right, then addition and subtraction left to right. So 2 + 3 × 4 is 14, not 20.

instruction: I'm feeling tired at work. What are some good break activities?
reply: Take the smallest break that is really a break, and take it today: twenty minutes out of the house without your phone, or a bath with the door shut while someone else does bedtime. Then lower the bar for the rest of the day - one meal, one wash, no craft - because a worn-out parent does not need a plan, they need an hour.

instruction: I'm considering using a motorcycle or scooter for my daily commute to work. What are the benefits?
reply: Worth it if the alternative is driving: a pedal-assist bike flattens the hills and the headwind, so a commute you would skip on a bad day still happens, for a few pence of electricity a charge and no tax or parking. It saves little against a bus pass and keeps you less fit unless you turn the assist down.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to improve my overall health. What are some essential vitamins and supplements I should consider taking?
reply: For most people with a varied diet the only supplement worth taking is vitamin D in autumn and winter (10 micrograms a day), plus folic acid if you are pregnant or trying. A multivitamin mostly makes expensive urine; if you eat little fish, vegans should add B12.

instruction: I'm planning to go grocery shopping this weekend. What are some essential items I should get?
reply: A rug, a cool bag with a freezer block, plates and cups you do not mind losing, a bottle opener, napkins, a bin bag and water. Skip anything heavy with mayonnaise unless it is eaten within the hour: sausage rolls, cheese, fruit and a flask keep for hours.

instruction: I'm starting to get into playing basketball and I was wondering what kind of food I should eat before a game.
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about subway expansion projects in my city. Are there any new lines being built?
reply: *Codenames* (2 minutes to learn, works with any group), *Ticket to Ride* (simple, satisfying trains) and *Sushi Go!* (fast, small, cheap) are the three to start with. All are done in under an hour.

instruction: What are the main types of computers?
reply: The CPU is the chip that runs the instructions in every program; its speed is quoted in gigahertz and how many jobs it can do at once in cores. For everyday use - a browser, video calls, a spreadsheet - a mid-range chip from the last few years feels the same as a fast one, and more memory or an SSD makes a bigger difference.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different cultural foods. Can you tell me about Japanese food?
reply: Fish and chips feeds a group for the least money and nobody argues about it. If tastes differ, Indian beats Chinese: more vegetarian mains, and the sides stretch, so two mains with one rice and one bread feeds three.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to stay motivated during team sports. Do you have any tips?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm worried about pollution in my city. What causes air pollution?
reply: Acid rain forms when sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning coal and oil mix with water in the air and fall as weak acid. It harms trees and lakes; filters on power stations and cleaner fuel have cut it a lot since the 1980s.

instruction: I'm going shopping for new clothes this weekend. What's the difference between designer and fast fashion?
reply: Cocktail dress code means short dresses or a smart top and skirt for women, and a suit or smart jacket and trousers for men: dressy, but not formal long gowns or full black tie. Heels you can stand in for two hours matter more than height.

instruction: I'm thinking about getting a pet. What are some popular types of pets?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm worried about my dental health. What's the best way to keep my teeth clean?
reply: Twice a day for two minutes with a fluoride toothpaste, spit rather than rinse so the fluoride stays on, and clean between the teeth once a day with floss or interdental brushes. Sugar between meals is what causes decay, so keep it to mealtimes, and a check-up every year or two keeps small problems cheap.

instruction: I'm looking for eco-friendly pet grooming products. What are some popular options?
reply: A dog groomer is usually £30 to £60 depending on the size and coat, with a hand-strip or a matted coat costing more. Ask what happens if your dog is matted, because some charge by the hour to sort it out, and book four to six weeks apart for a coat that keeps its shape.

instruction: I'm learning about the Earth in school and I was wondering, what is the Earth's magnetic field?
reply: The Earth is layered: a thin rocky crust, a hot slow-flowing mantle, a liquid outer core of iron and nickel, and a solid inner core. The churning iron outer core is what makes the magnetic field that keeps the solar wind off us.

instruction: I'm learning about physics in school, and I'm a bit confused about Newton's laws. Can you tell me what the first law is?
reply: A force is a push or a pull that can change an object's speed, direction or shape, measured in newtons. Gravity, friction and the push of a hand are all forces, and an object with no net force keeps doing what it was doing.

instruction: I'm interested in wearable displays. What are some common types?
reply: Size the screen to the distance you sit, not to the budget: for a 4K set that is about one and a half times the diagonal, so 50 inches at roughly 2 metres and 65 at 2.5, and a desk monitor sits an arm's length away, which suits 24 to 27 inches. Then spend the money on the panel rather than the badge - a mid-range OLED or mini-LED beats the biggest cheap set, and a good IPS monitor beats a cheap 4K one.

instruction: I'm planning a ski trip to the mountains this weekend and I'm worried about avalanches. What should I do to stay safe?
reply: Layers and a waterproof: a thin base layer, a fleece over it, a waterproof jacket with the hood up in the wind, and over-trousers in the bag for the top of the hill. Wear boots with real tread and take a spare pair of socks, and keep cotton off your skin - it holds the water and makes a wet walk cold, where wool or a synthetic layer still keeps you warm.

instruction: I'm learning about energy in ecosystems. What is energy in an ecosystem?
reply: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the non-living parts they depend on - soil, water, air and sunlight - interacting in one place. A pond, a woodland and a garden are ecosystems, and they work because energy flows through them and materials are recycled.

instruction: I want to cook something simple in the microwave. Do you have any ideas?
reply: Pasta cooks fine in a microwave, in a big bowl with plenty of room: cover it with boiling water from the kettle, add a good pinch of salt, and give it 8 to 10 minutes on full power, stirring once at the halfway point so the pieces at the top get turned under. Use a bowl at least twice the size of the pasta, because it foams up over the edge otherwise.

instruction: I'm going shopping this weekend and I want to save some money. Do you have any tips on finding discounts?
reply: Start pocket money at about six, a small fixed amount on the same day each week, and let them spend it badly while the sums are still small. Split it into spend, save and give jars so the saving is visible, and pay extra for jobs beyond the normal helping rather than docking the basics.

instruction: I'm learning about the Earth's rock cycle in school. What is it?
reply: The rock cycle is rocks being made, broken down and made again. Magma cools to igneous rock such as granite or basalt; wind and water wear any rock into grains that settle, get squashed and cement into sedimentary rock such as limestone and sandstone; heat and pressure bake or squeeze rock into metamorphic rock such as marble, from limestone, or slate, from shale.

instruction: I'm planning to clean my backyard this weekend. What are some essential cleaning tools I'll need?
