reply: Sweep it first, then wash: on block paving or concrete a pressure washer does most of it, keeping the nozzle moving and working down the slope so the dirty water runs off rather than back over what you have done. On decking keep the pressure low and go along the grain, because a hard jet furries softwood.

instruction: I'm having trouble studying for my exams and I heard about the Cornell Note-taking method. What is it?
reply: Use the phone: the Notes app on an iPhone has Scan Document, and on Android the Files app or Google Drive has Scan, both of which straighten the page and make a PDF you can email. Lay the paper flat in good light, hold the phone still above it, and check the edges are in before saving.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with my family. We never seem to be on the same page.
reply: For a family with an older parent, WhatsApp is the easiest: install it, add the contacts, then tap New group, name it and pick the people. Turn on their notifications for that one chat and pin it to the top of their screen, and start by sending a photo so there is something to reply to.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What is it?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm looking for information about local sports teams. What high school teams are in our area?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: What is a web browser?
reply: A browser is the program you read websites in: Chrome, Safari, Edge and Firefox are the common four and they all do the same job. Anything you type in the address bar, any page you save a password for and any tab you leave open belongs to that one browser, which is why an account that works on your phone can look lost on a laptop until you sign in.

instruction: I'm looking for plants I can eat. What are some common edible plants?
reply: Water plants pulled up from the bottom, plus grass, grain and the odd insect or snail. Bread is the wrong food: it is empty of much they need and it fouls the water, so grain, oats or shredded greens are the better offering.

instruction: I'm having some trouble with my family. We don't seem to communicate very well.
reply: Break the silence with something small and concrete rather than a big talk: a photo with 'saw this and thought of you - how are you doing?' on it, or a practical question about a parent or a house you both care about. Don't relitigate the argument in the first message - the point is a door left open.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with my team at work. Do you have any tips for improving my communication skills?
reply: Aim for two real conversations rather than working the room: ask what they are working on and what brought them there, then listen. Have one sentence ready about yourself and follow up with a two-line message the next day.

instruction: I'm interested in painting as a hobby. What are some popular art styles?
reply: Draw what is in front of you, not from memory: a mug, your own hand, the chair opposite. Ten minutes a day beats a long session at the weekend, one object a day for a fortnight, and use a soft pencil (2B) on cheap paper so you are not afraid of it.

instruction: I'm looking for concert tickets for my favorite artist, do you have any available?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm looking for a scenic train route for my next vacation. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Pick a route you already know on quiet streets, ride it once at a weekend so the turns are not a surprise, and start with two days a week rather than five. Leave a lock, a spare tube and a pair of shoes at work, so there is nothing to carry and nothing to forget.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about Rugby. Is it a popular sport?
reply: Rugby offside is about where you stand relative to the ball, not the goal line: stay behind the ball, or behind the last foot of the ruck or maul, until it is played away, and come back onside before you get involved. In open play, a team-mate's kick puts you offside until you are put onside by a chase or a pass — and standing in front of the kicker and going for the ball is the one that gives away a penalty.

instruction: I love spending time with my family, especially when we're with our pets. Do you think having pets helps bring families closer together?
reply: Cats are sociable, but they hunt alone and sleep sixteen hours a day, so an adult cat does not need company the way a dog does: a clean tray, water, food and something to climb are enough for the hours you are out. Two cats that get on will often choose to be in the same room, so two is kinder than one if you are out long days - but get them together as kittens, or introduce an adult pair slowly.

instruction: I'm learning about Earth in school. Can you tell me how long it takes for Earth to rotate once?
reply: The Earth spins because the cloud of dust and gas it formed from was already turning, and nothing has braked it much in 4.5 billion years. The Moon's tides are slowly slowing it, so the day grows about a second longer every 50,000 years or so.

instruction: I'm going grocery shopping this weekend and I want to save money. Do you have any tips on using coupons?
reply: Start pocket money at about six, a small fixed amount on the same day each week, and let them spend it badly while the sums are still small. Split it into spend, save and give jars so the saving is visible, and pay extra for jobs beyond the normal helping rather than docking the basics.

instruction: I'm looking for upcoming virtual concerts. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: What's on TV tonight?
reply: I can't see the schedule from here, sorry. The guide on the telly, or the station's own app, has the times, and the catch-up players - iPlayer, ITVX, Channel 4, BBC Sounds - keep the same list on the front page.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to New York City. What is the main subway system in NYC?
reply: New York City has about 8.3 million people - 8.3 million in the five boroughs, and around 19 million in the metro area. It is the biggest city in the United States.

instruction: I'm looking for some new accessories for summer. What are some popular summer accessories?
reply: For the gym: trainers you only wear indoors, two towels (one for the floor and machines), a water bottle, a padlock for the locker, deodorant and a bag for wet kit. A resistance band and a notebook beat anything else a shop will sell you.

instruction: I'm planning to paint my living room and I was wondering what's the best way to prepare the walls.
reply: Before paint you need filler for the holes, fine sandpaper, masking tape, a dust sheet, a roller and tray, a brush for edges and an old screwdriver to open the tin. One litre of emulsion covers about 12 square metres, so measure the walls and buy two coats' worth.

instruction: I'm a student and I'm having trouble understanding what subjects I should focus on for my future career in healthcare.
reply: Apply on UCAS: one form, up to five courses, the personal statement and a reference, with 15 October for Oxford, Cambridge, medicine and veterinary science and mid-January for everything else. The statement is the part people worry about, and the rule is to start with the subject, not your childhood: what you have read, built or done that made you want it, then what you want to learn next.

instruction: I'm trying to find the next number in the pattern: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Can you help me?
reply: Divide the top and the bottom by the same number until nothing goes into both: 6/8 divides by 2 to give 3/4, and that is as far as it goes. The number to start with is the highest common factor of the two.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my internet connection. What are some popular internet service providers?
reply: Wifi is just the radio link between your devices and the router; the internet is the connection the router brings into the house. So a wifi problem is your side (distance, walls, an old router) and an internet problem is your provider's line.

instruction: I'm looking for information about theater productions in my city. Are there any musicals playing right now?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I was wondering, what is the Earth's magnetic field?
reply: The Earth is layered: a thin rocky crust, a hot slow-flowing mantle, a liquid outer core of iron and nickel, and a solid inner core. The churning iron outer core is what makes the magnetic field that keeps the solar wind off us.

instruction: I'm planning to visit the local mall this weekend. What are the main security measures in place?
reply: Do the safety things this week, not later: a lockable back gate, an alarm on the door, a card in a pocket with your number, and tell the neighbours and the local police what to do if they see them out alone. Ring the council's adult social care line and ask for a carer's assessment and a telecare alarm; wandering usually needs a person checking in during the day, and that is arranged, not improvised.

instruction: I'm thinking about adopting a pet. What are some popular pets people adopt from shelters?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I'm looking for some nostalgic music from my childhood. What are some popular songs from the 90s?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm having trouble waking up in the morning. Do you have any tips?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: I'm trying to understand numbers better. What's the biggest number used in everyday life?
reply: Use number for things you can count and amount for things you can't: a number of people, a large amount of work. 'Amount of people' is the usual slip.

instruction: I'm planning to make some fried chicken for dinner, but I'm not sure what oil to use.
reply: Olive oil or rapeseed oil is a good everyday choice: both are high in unsaturated fat and fine for normal frying. Save the extra virgin olive oil for salads and low heat, and use a plain vegetable oil when you need a very hot pan.

instruction: What season is it right now?
reply: Seasons stay lower case: spring, summer, autumn, winter. Days and months take a capital - Monday, January - and so do holidays, as in Christmas.

instruction: I'm planning to attend a music festival next month and I'm not sure what to pack.
reply: Ticket and ID, some cash because card readers fail in fields, a small tent with its pegs and a mallet, a sleeping bag and mat, earplugs and a power bank. Wellies, a waterproof and warm layers for the nights, plus sun cream and a hat for the days, wet wipes, toilet roll, blister plasters and bin bags; leave glass at home.

instruction: I'm looking for some exercises to improve my flexibility. Can you suggest a few?
reply: Not for injury, no: strength work and building up slowly are what keep you off the physio's couch, and a stretch before sport takes a little power off it. What the flexibility is worth having is the reach - a high shelf, a shoe, getting up off the floor - and that goes quickly if you stop.

instruction: What's the difference between weight and mass?
reply: kg is short for kilogram: 1,000 grams, and about 2.2 pounds. A stone is 6.35 kg, which is why a person's weight in kilos is a bigger number than the same weight in pounds.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to New York City. What are some popular attractions?
reply: New York City has about 8.3 million people - 8.3 million in the five boroughs, and around 19 million in the metro area. It is the biggest city in the United States.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I'm not sure if I'm sleeping enough. How many hours of sleep should I get each night?
reply: Count back about eight hours from the time you have to get up, and keep that bedtime the same seven days a week: the regularity matters more than the exact hour. If you lie there awake, go to bed half an hour later rather than earlier, so bed means sleep again.

instruction: I'm looking for a new laptop, but I want to find the best deal. How often do laptops go on sale?
reply: A laptop is good for about four to six years and a tablet for three to five, and the clock starts when the software updates stop rather than when it feels slow: a machine with no security fixes is the reason to change, not the speed. The battery is the exception, since £40 to £80 fits a new one to a laptop and £50 to £120 to a phone, and that alone buys another two or three years.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school. What's a compound machine?
reply: A compound is two or more different elements chemically joined in fixed proportions: water is hydrogen and oxygen, and table salt is sodium and chlorine. Unlike a mixture, the elements in a compound cannot be separated just by filtering or boiling.

instruction: I'm worried about soil pollution. What causes it?
reply: Soil is crushed rock mixed with rotted plant and animal matter, plus air, water and a vast number of microbes. The rotted part, humus, is what holds water and feeds plants, and it takes hundreds of years to build up an inch of it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new fitness app to help me stay on track with my workouts. What are some popular options?
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I was thinking about taking a nap. I've heard that napping is popular in some cultures.
reply: A short nap is worth having: 20 minutes, ideally before about 3pm, and set an alarm, because 90 minutes leaves you groggier than when you lay down. It helps most if you lost sleep the night before or you are driving later.

instruction: I'm looking for information about vintage sports equipment. What's one of the most valuable vintage sports items?
reply: Start with very little: trainers or astro boots, shorts or leggings, a water bottle and, for football or hockey, shin pads. Clubs lend sticks, bats and bibs to beginners, so email and ask what they provide before you buy anything.

instruction: I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow, but I'm not feeling well enough to leave my house. Are there any other options?
reply: Leave at nap time or early if you can, plan a stop or a walk about every two hours, and pack snacks, water, sunshades and a tablet with films downloaded. A surprise bag of small new things to hand out one at a time is the trick for the last hour.

instruction: I'm trying to get back into running after a knee injury. What are some exercises I can do to strengthen my knees?
reply: A knee that gives trouble is helped most by the muscle above it: sit-to-stands from a chair, step-ups onto a low step and straight-leg raises, two or three times a week, which builds the thigh muscle that takes the load off the joint. Keep walking on the flat and skip deep squats and running downhill; a physio can set the pace.

instruction: I'm planning to create a flower garden in my backyard. What flowers are easy to grow?
reply: Flowers, most of the time: go to a florist rather than a garage and ask for what is in season, and a mixed bunch is always safe. A plant lasts years and is the better present for someone who likes looking after things, but give an orchid or a houseplant only to a person who will remember to water it.

instruction: I'm having trouble managing my work schedule and personal life. Do you have any suggestions for achieving a better work-life balance?
reply: Ask for a private twenty minutes and say it plainly in the first sentence: "I'm not coping with the current load and I want to sort it out before it shows in the work." Then bring two or three specifics - the tasks, the hours, what has slipped - and two things you want changed, because a manager can act on a proposal and rarely on a feeling. Ask what support exists: an employee assistance line, occupational health, flexible hours or a temporary reallocation.

instruction: I'm trying to save money on groceries and avoid buying things I don't need. Do you have any tips?
reply: Start pocket money at about six, a small fixed amount on the same day each week, and let them spend it badly while the sums are still small. Split it into spend, save and give jars so the saving is visible, and pay extra for jobs beyond the normal helping rather than docking the basics.

instruction: I'm interested in learning a musical instrument, but I'm not sure which one to choose.
reply: Say yes to a term of cheap lessons before you buy anything: school lessons or a group class cost a fraction of one-to-one, and four to six weeks tells you whether it will stick. Borrow or rent the instrument for that first term - a second-hand keyboard or guitar is thirty or forty pounds - and only buy once they have kept it up.

instruction: I'm trying to understand social media analytics better. What is the main purpose of it?
reply: It means the wider view rather than this one detail. What decision is it for?

instruction: I'm going to the store. Can you help me make a shopping list?
reply: Buy for the first night, not for the shelves: a takeaway voucher for the evening the boxes are still out, a box with loo roll, tea, milk, mugs, bin bags, a corkscrew and a phone charger, or a hot meal you turn up with. A plant, a good bottle or a decent set of tea towels all last longer than another candle, and a voucher for a hardware shop is the unromantic one people are pleased about.

instruction: I'm looking for dessert ideas. Do you know any popular fruit-based desserts?
reply: Hot chocolate sauce, tinned peaches or raspberries with a splash of their juice, crushed biscuits or toasted nuts, and a pinch of salt on anything caramel. A shot of espresso over vanilla is affogato, which is the best 30-second pudding there is.

instruction: I'm looking for different types of hot chocolate. What are some popular ones?
reply: Warm 200ml of milk and melt 20g of dark chocolate into it, chopped small, stirring until it is smooth - a pinch of salt makes it taste more of chocolate, not less. Cocoa powder works too: a teaspoon each of cocoa and sugar made into a paste with a little cold milk first, so it does not go lumpy.

instruction: I'm looking for a new movie to watch. What are some popular movies currently playing in theaters?
reply: *Arrival* is the smartest one, *Apollo 13* the most tense, and *Interstellar* the biggest. For something lighter, *Galaxy Quest* is a lovely comedy about actors on a spaceship.

instruction: I'm trying to stay healthy during cold season. How often should I wash my hands?
reply: Two or three times a week is plenty for most adults, with a wash of the face, hands, feet, under the arms and the groin every day; the rest of the skin can wait. Five to ten minutes and lukewarm is enough for a whole shower, and long hot ones strip the oils out of dry skin, so moisturise while it is still damp.

instruction: I'm going to a job interview and I'm not sure what to wear. What is business attire for men?
reply: For most interviews, smart casual is the safe bet: a clean shirt or blouse, dark trousers or a skirt, and closed shoes; a suit only if the company is formal. Check the office on their website or LinkedIn and dress one step smarter than that.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm interested in learning more about the flipped classroom method.
reply: Rotate it head to foot every three months, and only flip it if the label or the shop says it is two-sided: most modern mattresses have their comfort layer on top and are made never to be turned over. A two-sided one gets flipped and rotated on the same schedule; a pillow-top or memory-foam one is only rotated, because flipping puts the soft layer underneath.

instruction: I'm looking for comfortable clothes to wear at home. What type of fabric is good for that?
reply: Something comfortable and a step nicer than you'd wear at home: jeans with a good top, or a dress with flat shoes. Nothing that needs careful handling next to red wine on someone's sofa.

instruction: I'm interested in gardening. What is organic gardening?
reply: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the non-living parts they depend on - soil, water, air and sunlight - interacting in one place. A pond, a woodland and a garden are ecosystems, and they work because energy flows through them and materials are recycled.

instruction: I'm looking for some new winter clothes. What's in style this season?
reply: Cotton rather than polyester, because it breathes and you wake up less clammy: a t-shirt and shorts or loose pyjama bottoms is plenty, and socks if your feet get cold. A pair of shorts you'd answer the door in is worth having in the summer.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Paris. What are some famous landmarks I should visit?
reply: Paris has about 2.1 million people inside the city limits, and about 11 million in the whole metro area - the city proper is small, and the suburbs are where most Parisians live.

instruction: I'm going on a trip soon and I'm not sure how to pack lightly. Do you have any tips for minimalist packing?
reply: Lay everything out and take half the clothes and twice the money: three tops, two bottoms, one warm layer and shoes you can walk in covers a week. Roll clothes, keep a change in your hand luggage, and buy anything you forget when you arrive.

instruction: I'm getting older and I'm worried about my health. Are there any vitamins or supplements that are good for people my age?
reply: For most people with a varied diet the only supplement worth taking is vitamin D in autumn and winter (10 micrograms a day), plus folic acid if you are pregnant or trying. A multivitamin mostly makes expensive urine; if you eat little fish, vegans should add B12.

instruction: I was wondering, where does the word "quarantine" come from?
reply: It means it happened suddenly, with no warning. What came out of the blue?

instruction: I'm looking forward to the big boxing match this weekend. Is it available on regular TV?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: I'm feeling sad because my pet passed away recently. I'm missing them a lot.
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I want to bake a cake, but I don't have a mixer. Can I still make it?
reply: Plenty bakes without eggs: shortbread, flapjack, a fruit crumble, icebox biscuits and most traybakes need none at all. If a recipe wants an egg for binding, a tablespoon of ground flaxseed in three of water stands in for one, and a tablespoon of yogurt or half a mashed banana does the same job in a cake.

instruction: I'm looking for a new laptop, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm going to the airport tomorrow and I'm thinking of taking a taxi. Do I need to book in advance?
reply: For a night before an early flight, book an airport hotel with a shuttle and check the first and last shuttle times before you pay - a 4am shuttle that stops at 11pm is the usual trap, and so is a "5 minutes from the terminal" that is five minutes by car on a road with no pavement. A town two or three stops away on the train, or a park-and-fly with the transfer included, is usually about half the price; add up the transfer, the parking and the extra hour and pick on the total.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about electronic instruments. What's a synthesizer?
reply: A diaphragm inside moves when sound pushes on it, and that movement is turned into an electrical signal that copies the shape of the sound wave. A condenser mic charges that diaphragm and needs power; a dynamic one uses a coil in a magnet and needs none, which is why a stage mic is the one that can be dropped.

instruction: I'm interested in ancient civilizations. Can you tell me about the Egyptians?
reply: Ancient Egyptians built them about 4,500 years ago, around 2560 BC for the Great Pyramid of Giza, as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu. The workers were organised, paid labourers, not slaves, hauling stone on ramps and sledges.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you know what could be causing it?
reply: Waking in the middle of the night is normal - the trick is what you do next: stay in bed, keep the room dark, and do not look at the clock or your phone, because that is what teaches your brain to be awake at 3am. If you are awake more than 20 minutes, get up and sit somewhere dim until you feel sleepy.

instruction: I'm a beginner runner and I'm not sure if I'm running correctly. What's the most important thing to focus on for proper running form?
reply: Breathe in through the nose and mouth together, into the belly rather than the chest, and let the rhythm follow your steps - two in, two out, then three and three when the pace is easy. If you can only speak a few words at a time, slow down: most breathless running is a pace problem, not a lung problem.

instruction: I'm hungry, what are some popular breakfast foods?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm learning about magnetism in school and I was wondering, what is magnetism?
reply: Magnetism is the force a magnet exerts on other magnets and on iron, nickel and cobalt, carried by a magnetic field around the magnet. Like poles repel and opposite poles attract, and a compass needle is a tiny magnet lining up with Earth's field.

instruction: I'm looking for a new yoga mat. What should I consider when choosing one?
reply: Pilates is the better pick for a weak or sore back and a strong middle - it is slow, controlled work on the deep stomach and hip muscles - and yoga is the better pick for flexibility, balance and winding down. Both are low-impact and fine to start from nothing, so if the choice is still even, take the one whose teacher you liked.

instruction: I'm looking for a new game to play. What are some popular games right now?
reply: *Patchwork*, *Jaipur* and *Hive* are the three best two-player games that are quick to learn. For a card game with no kit, gin rummy works just fine.

instruction: I'm looking for information about virtual concerts. Are they popular?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I have a meeting with someone in New York, but I'm in California. What's the time difference?
reply: The exact time depends on where you are and the date, so I cannot give you the clock time: a weather app or the Met Office page for your postcode has it, along with tomorrow's. Sunrise moves only a minute or two a day, but the gap between sunrise and sunset swings by hours across the year.

instruction: I'm looking for a new pair of dress shoes, do you have any recommendations?
reply: For work, four things decide it: the fabric, the rise, the length and the pockets. A wool-poly blend or a cotton twill with a little stretch creases less and gives when you sit and stand; a mid rise that sits at the waist stays put through a shift; and the hem should break once on the shoe, so buy the length that fits you - short and petite lengths are sold off the rail and cost no more than a tailor.

instruction: I'm going to ride the bus to school tomorrow, is it safe?
reply: Ask what exactly feels scary, because 'school' usually means one thing: the bus, a particular lesson, or being picked for teams. Fix that one thing together (a practice bus ride, a word with the teacher, a friend to walk in with), and keep the mornings calm and predictable while it settles.

instruction: I'm looking for pet food recommendations for my cat. What's a good brand?
reply: Pick a dish that is good on its own rather than meat with the meat left out: a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, a mushroom and lentil lasagne, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. One proper veggie main plus the usual sides is plenty, and it is worth asking what they actually eat, because vegetarian covers a wide range.

instruction: I'm trying to get back into fitness, but I'm having trouble staying motivated. Do you have any tips?
reply: Make it small and scheduled: a set time, everything you need out and ready, and a session so short that skipping it feels sillier than doing it. Track the days you show up rather than the results, and do it with someone or book it like an appointment: habit carries you when motivation does not.

instruction: I have a cat and I'm not sure what to feed her. What's a good type of cat food?
reply: Pick a dish that is good on its own rather than meat with the meat left out: a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, a mushroom and lentil lasagne, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. One proper veggie main plus the usual sides is plenty, and it is worth asking what they actually eat, because vegetarian covers a wide range.

instruction: I'm looking for a new pair of boots. What type of boots are popular this season?
reply: Astro trainers or moulded boots, shin pads, shorts and a top you do not mind sweating in, plus water. Most places play on 3G astro, so no studs, and a lot of leagues ask for the same colour top for the whole team - ask the organiser before you buy anything.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Europe and I'm not sure which cities to visit.
reply: Berlin has about 3.8 million people, the biggest city in Germany and about eight times the size of Frankfurt.

instruction: I'm looking for a new all-purpose cleaner. What are some popular options?
reply: White vinegar for limescale, glass, the kettle and the shower screen; bicarbonate of soda for scouring a sink or a pan, a smelly fridge and a slow drain; lemon juice and salt for a wooden board and a copper pan. Two rules cover most of it: no vinegar on marble, stone or grout, because the acid eats them, and never vinegar with bleach, because the two together give off chlorine gas.

instruction: I'm trying to establish a better morning routine. What's a good time to wake up?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: I like music and art, can you tell me about famous artists?
reply: Leonardo da Vinci (1452-1519) was an Italian painter, engineer and anatomist: the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper on one side, notebooks of flying machines and dissected bodies on the other. Fewer than twenty of his paintings survive, and it is the range of his curiosity that made him famous.

instruction: I'm thinking about walking to work instead of driving. What are some benefits of walking to work?
reply: Plan the outing around the walking. Go door to door - a taxi, or the bus that stops nearest the door - and make a bench or a cafe the turning point so the trip is two short walks with a sit in between.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I want to try meditation, but I don't know where to start.
reply: Meditation is paying attention to one thing on purpose - usually the breath - and coming back to it each time you notice you have drifted; an empty mind is not the aim, and the noticing is the skill. The tested versions are the eight-week courses, MBSR and MBCT, mainly for low mood and anxiety.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about space. What's the brightest star in the sky?
reply: A star is a huge ball of gas held together by gravity, with fusion in its core turning hydrogen into helium and giving out light and heat. The Sun is the nearest star, and stars look small only because they are very far away.

instruction: I'm looking for information about Spanish cuisine. What's a popular Spanish dish?
reply: Make the vegetarian dish the main for the whole table and put the meat on the side as an extra: a mushroom and lentil lasagne, a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. Nobody gets a plate of sides, and you cook one dinner.

instruction: I'm looking for a new job, but I'm not sure what type of work I want to do. What are some common job categories?
reply: Try the smallest real version first: an evening course, one freelance job, or a sideways move inside your current employer. Talk to three people doing the job now and ask what the bad days are like, not the good ones.

instruction: I'm trying to get more exercise, what are some good sports for one person to play?
reply: Something that wicks and doesn't need adjusting mid-set: shorts or leggings and a breathable top, with a sports bra for anything bouncy, and shoes for the work you're doing - cushioned for running, flat and stable for lifting.

instruction: I'm thinking of buying a new smartphone. What's the main difference between a regular camera and a smartphone camera?
reply: Three things settle it, and none of them is the model year. If what you have still holds a charge to the evening, opens apps without a wait and still gets security updates, a new phone buys you a better camera and a nicer screen rather than a faster life, so waiting a year costs you nothing.

instruction: My parents are celebrating their 30th wedding anniversary. What are some common ways to celebrate this milestone?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I'm planning to organize my home. Can you tell me about the laundry room?
reply: Twenty minutes a room on a timer, top to bottom, floor last: a bin bag for the rubbish and a basket for everything that lives somewhere else, then dust from the ceiling down (corners, the tops of pictures, lamp shades), then wipe the marks, then hoover. For a whole house, do the rooms visitors see in the order they see them - hall, loo, kitchen, sitting room - and shut the doors on the rest.

instruction: I'm looking for a new board game for my kids. Something educational.
reply: *Dobble*, *UNO* and *Snakes and Ladders* work for a range of ages, and *Catan Junior* if they are ready for a proper board game. For a rainy afternoon, a treasure hunt round the house costs nothing and takes the longest.

instruction: I'm planning to cook chicken for dinner. How do I handle it safely?
reply: Don't: washing raw chicken splashes bacteria over the sink, the taps and anything within a metre, and cooking kills them anyway. Pat it dry with kitchen paper, bin the paper, wash your hands, and cook it right through.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I'm looking for ways to relax. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move.

instruction: Is it going to snow this weekend?
reply: Pack for 2 to 8C, wind and rain: a waterproof coat with a hood, warm layers you can take off indoors, and shoes you can walk a hill in. It gets dark around 4pm in December, so a small torch and plans for the afternoon indoors help.

instruction: I'm looking for a place to watch the game this weekend. Do you know any good sports bars near me?
reply: Search for the sport plus your town and 'club', then email and ask about a taster session: most clubs have a beginners' or social night that costs a few pounds. Turn up to that rather than a match, and say you're new — clubs are used to it, and it's the fastest way to find people at your level.

instruction: I'm looking for an app that I can use on both my phone and computer. Do you know of any?
reply: Most sets have a free app that turns the phone into the remote: SmartThings for a Samsung, LG ThinQ for an LG, the Google TV or Android TV Remote app, Roku for a Roku, and the Apple TV Remote in Control Centre for an Apple TV. The phone and the TV have to be on the same wifi, and the TV has to be on.

instruction: I was wondering, why do we have seasons on Earth?
reply: Seasons come from the Earth's 23.5-degree tilt, not from how close it is to the sun. When your half of the planet leans towards the sun you get summer: longer days and more direct light.

instruction: I'm interested in starting yoga. What are the main benefits?
reply: Five minutes, in two parts: first something easy that gets you slightly out of breath - a brisk walk, a slow jog, skipping, the exercise bike - then a few quick movements through the range you are about to use, like leg swings, arm circles, hip circles and ten bodyweight squats. Start the first set lighter than the rest.

instruction: I'm interested in carpooling to work. What are some safety tips I should know?
reply: Stay behind the barrier, not beside the car, and keep a coat on: the hard shoulder is the most dangerous part of the road. Ring 999 if you cannot get behind the barrier or you are in a live lane, then your breakdown service.

instruction: I'm looking for a new job, but I'm not sure what career path to choose. Can you help me with some ideas?
reply: It depends on what you want to do: for nursing, engineering, law or teaching the degree is the door, and for plenty of other jobs experience gets you further for less money. Compare a degree with a degree apprenticeship in the same field — earn while you learn, no fees — and look at what people actually doing the job you want studied.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about climate change. Is the Earth's climate always the same?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new chef's knife. What are some essential knives I should have in my kitchen?
reply: One 20cm cook's knife does almost everything, so spend the money there - around 25 to 40 pounds on a forged one with a full tang gets an edge that holds - and add a serrated bread knife and a small paring knife when you need them, rather than buying a set of six cheap ones that none of them do a job well. Hold it before you buy it, because the handle has to fill your hand, and only buy something you can sharpen yourself with a steel or a stone.

instruction: I'm looking for a home workout routine that doesn't require a lot of equipment. What are some options?
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What is melatonin?
reply: Pick one wake-up time and keep it every day for two weeks, weekends included: the morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime 15 minutes earlier every few nights, keep the room dark and cool, and take a short walk in daylight before noon.

instruction: I'm planning to go grocery shopping this weekend. What are some benefits of buying in bulk?
reply: Write the week's four meals down before you shop and buy for those, not for the week you imagine. Keep a box in the fridge for what must go first, and put tonight's dinner in it when you unpack.

instruction: I have a big family with lots of siblings. What is a stepbrother?
reply: A grown sibling's jealousy is usually about one visible difference - a house, a partner, a job, or the way a parent treats you - so do not defend your life or list your own hard parts, which reads as scoring points. Name it once, plainly and without blame: 'I know this has not been easy to watch.' Then keep the relationship on ground that is not a comparison, and if every visit turns into digs or competition, make them shorter and more structured.

instruction: I was wondering, how do animals communicate with each other using sound?
reply: Sound is a pressure wave travelling through air, water or a solid: something vibrates, pushes the particles next to it, and the push travels outwards. It cannot cross a vacuum, and it goes faster through water and solids than through air.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my work schedule. Is it possible to have flexible hours?
reply: Say what you can do rather than what you can't: "I can stay until six tonight, but not tomorrow as well." If it is every week, ask what is being dropped instead of absorbing it, and check what your contract says about overtime and pay. Over your contracted hours you can say no: unpaid regular overtime is worth a word with ACAS.

instruction: I'm learning about the water cycle in school. What is transpiration?
reply: A life cycle is the stages a living thing goes through from one generation to the next: a frog goes egg, tadpole, froglet, adult, and a butterfly goes egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. A plant's is seed, seedling, flowering plant, then seed again.

instruction: I'm curious about magnets. What is magnetic levitation?
reply: Magnetism is the force a magnet exerts on other magnets and on iron, nickel and cobalt, carried by a magnetic field around the magnet. Like poles repel and opposite poles attract, and a compass needle is a tiny magnet lining up with Earth's field.

instruction: I'm looking for information about my school's sports day. When is it?
reply: In England a child starts reception in the September after their fourth birthday, and school is compulsory from the term after they turn five. Apply through your council by 15 January in the year they start, and you hear on 16 April.

instruction: I'm looking for a new laptop, can you tell me about some popular e-commerce platforms where I can buy one?
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm learning about basketball formations. What is the most common formation used in basketball?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I'm looking for information about my basketball. It's been squeaking a lot lately.
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I'm learning about energy in school and I'm a bit confused. Can you tell me what types of energy are there?
reply: Energy is the ability to make something happen - to move, heat, light or power something - and it is never used up, only changed from one form into another. Food stores chemical energy, a moving bike has kinetic energy, and a hot cup has thermal energy.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my video calls. They keep freezing.
reply: Sit closer to the router or use a cable, and shut the other heavy things on the laptop: a browser with twenty tabs is usually the cause of a freezing call. Turn the video off when the sound matters more, and in Zoom or Teams set the video to a lower quality - a still picture and clear sound beats a frozen face.

instruction: I'm looking for discounts on electronics. Are there any sales happening now?
reply: Check two things before you sell: the trade-in price from the network or the maker, and what the same model with the same storage sells for on a resale site - the private sale is often 20 to 30% more. Say the battery health and any marks honestly, sign out of your accounts and factory reset it in front of the buyer.

instruction: What is 2 + 2?
reply: Work in this order: brackets, then powers or roots, then multiplication and division left to right, then addition and subtraction left to right. So 2 + 3 × 4 is 14, not 20.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my video conferencing software. It keeps freezing during business meetings.
reply: Sit closer to the router or use a cable, and shut the other heavy things on the laptop: a browser with twenty tabs is usually the cause of a freezing call. Turn the video off when the sound matters more, and in Zoom or Teams set the video to a lower quality - a still picture and clear sound beats a frozen face.

instruction: I'm interested in bicycles. What are the main types of bicycles?
reply: A hybrid or gravel bike with 32 to 40mm tyres, mudguard and rack mounts and disc brakes: those stop in the wet and take a pannier. £500 to £800 new, £200 to £350 secondhand.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and I'd like to know some relaxation techniques. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move.

instruction: I'm looking for some casual outfit ideas for everyday wear. I like layering, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm thinking about my family. What are grandparents?
reply: Sort first, digitise second, and keep the paper: tip the lot onto a table and pull out the faces you cannot lose - the ones people will want in fifty years - then photograph each of those on a phone against a plain background, or use a flatbed scanner for the important ones. Store the prints in an acid-free box somewhere dry and dark rather than a hot loft, write the names and dates on the back of the keepers in pencil, and give the duplicates to the cousins who are in them.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school, and I was wondering how seeds get dispersed.
reply: A seed waits until it has water, warmth and oxygen, then its stored food fuels the first root and shoot. Once the shoot reaches light, the plant starts making its own food by photosynthesis, so the seed's reserves matter less.

instruction: I'm looking for some ideas for things to do on my breaks at work. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Give the day a hard edge and keep it the same one: laptop shut and work phone in a drawer at a fixed time, then something physical - a walk, a shower, cooking - because the body changes gear more reliably than the mind. Tell your team the hours once, in writing: "I'm offline after 6 and I pick up messages at 9." If you work from the room you live in, put the laptop out of sight at the end of the day; a screen in the corner is a shift that never ends.

instruction: I'm thinking about buying a new camera. What's the difference between digital and film cameras?
reply: A modern screen is a grid of millions of pixels, each with red, green and blue lights under it, and the picture is just each one being told how bright to be for that frame. A new frame goes up 50 or 60 times a second, faster than your eye follows, which is what makes it look like smooth movement.

instruction: I'm learning about adaptation in school. What is a behavioral adaptation?
reply: Living things vary, and the ones whose variations suit their surroundings tend to survive and pass those variations on. Over many generations that selection changes the population: small changes accumulate into new species.

instruction: I'm looking for a new workspace. What are some popular types of workspaces?
reply: Go up before you go out: a shelf over the door, hooks on the back of a cupboard door and boxes stacked to the ceiling use space you already have. Take the doors off one base cupboard and put a bin or open shelves in it, keep the worktop clear, and send anything you use less than monthly to the top of a wardrobe or under the bed.

instruction: I'm going to New York City and I'm planning to use the subway. What is the biggest subway station in NYC?
reply: New York City has about 8.3 million people - 8.3 million in the five boroughs, and around 19 million in the metro area. It is the biggest city in the United States.

instruction: I'm looking for some breakfast ideas. What are some popular breakfast dishes?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about pressure cooking. What is pressure cooking?
reply: *Home Cooking* (Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway) answers listeners' kitchen questions and is the friendliest place to start. *The Sporkful* is about how and why people eat what they eat, and *Gastropod* takes one food an episode and does its history and science.

instruction: I'm thinking of adopting a pet, what do I need to do to prepare my home?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I'm having trouble understanding the concept of slope in graphing. Can you explain it to me?
reply: Read what each axis is measured in first, including the units and the step between the numbers. To read a value, go up from the number you know to the line, then across to the other axis.

instruction: I'm playing in a big basketball game tomorrow and I'm feeling really nervous. Do you have any tips on how to prepare mentally?
reply: Stay tall and wait: most takers decide their corner early, so watch the standing foot and the hips rather than the ball, and dive late with a strong hand. Keep your weight on the balls of your feet so the first step can go either way.

instruction: I'm going shopping and I need to make a list. Can you help me with that?
reply: Not needed for a simple list: bread, milk and eggs. Put one in when 'and' joins two complete sentences (I booked the table, and she drove), or when the list items are long enough that the reader needs the pause: we need the report signed, the photos checked, and the invoice sent.

instruction: I'm looking for comfortable clothes to wear at home. What are some popular options?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to preserve my grandmother's old recipes. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Something sharp, something salty, something crunchy: olive oil and lemon or vinegar, then salt, then nuts, seeds or croutons. A dressing of 2 parts oil to 1 part vinegar with a spoon of mustard, shaken in a jar, keeps a week in the fridge.

instruction: I'm interested in space exploration. What is the largest planet in our solar system?
reply: Jupiter is the biggest planet: about 143,000 km across, or 11 Earths side by side, and more than twice as massive as all the other planets put together. It is a gas giant with no solid surface to stand on.

instruction: I'm thinking about my family traditions. What are some common family traditions during holidays?
reply: Do one thing you could not do with them in the house and one thing that is only rest, and put the fun one first, because the tidying can wait until Sunday evening. The first night can feel strange and quiet, and that is normal rather than a sign anything is wrong.

instruction: I'm learning about geology and was wondering, what is the biggest impact geology has on ecosystems?
reply: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the non-living parts they depend on - soil, water, air and sunlight - interacting in one place. A pond, a woodland and a garden are ecosystems, and they work because energy flows through them and materials are recycled.

instruction: I'm having trouble understanding what I read. Do you have any tips for improving my reading comprehension?
reply: I cannot read it for you, but the check that catches most of it is reading it aloud: your ear stops on the missing word and the doubled one. Then look at four things in order - the name at the top, the ask in the first line, any number or date, and the last line.

instruction: What is the difference between transparent and opaque materials?
reply: Glass is sand melted with soda ash and limestone at about 1,700°C, then cooled fast enough that it sets as a liquid instead of forming crystals - which is why you can see through it. It can be melted down and remade indefinitely without losing anything.

instruction: I'm a big fan of superhero movies. What's the most popular one?
reply: *Arrival* is the smartest one, *Apollo 13* the most tense, and *Interstellar* the biggest. For something lighter, *Galaxy Quest* is a lovely comedy about actors on a spaceship.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with my coworkers at the office. Do you have any tips for improving my communication skills?
reply: Aim for two real conversations rather than working the room: ask what they are working on and what brought them there, then listen. Have one sentence ready about yourself and follow up with a two-line message the next day.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different types of rocks. What's the main difference between igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks?
reply: A rock is a solid piece of the earth made of one or more minerals: granite is mostly quartz and feldspar, and limestone is mostly calcite. Rocks come in three kinds - igneous from cooled magma, sedimentary from settled layers, and metamorphic changed by heat and pressure.

instruction: I'm worried about my computer getting a virus. What can I do to protect it?
reply: On Windows you do not need to buy one: Microsoft Defender is built in, free and as good as the paid suites, and it updates itself. Phone and tablet: Play Protect on Android and an iPhone need nothing else.

instruction: I love watching cooking shows. What are some popular reality cooking shows?
reply: *Home Cooking* (Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway) answers listeners' kitchen questions and is the friendliest place to start. *The Sporkful* is about how and why people eat what they eat, and *Gastropod* takes one food an episode and does its history and science.

instruction: I'm having some trouble talking to my parents. Do you have any tips?
reply: Talk side by side rather than face to face: in the car, on a walk, or while washing up, and keep it to a couple of minutes. Ask about the small stuff and let them bring the big stuff when they are ready; a teenager who says nothing at seven often talks at ten.

instruction: I'm a new parent and I'm not sure what parenting style is best for my child. What are some common parenting styles?
reply: Don't try to be the parent yet: be a reliable adult who is not in charge of the rules and let their actual parent do the discipline for a while. Keep the offers small and repeated - a lift, a snack they like, a show you both watch - because loyalty to the other parent is usually what is behind the hostility.

instruction: I'm thinking about adopting a pet. Are there any pet adoption events coming up?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I'm worried about my online security. What's the best way to keep my passwords safe?
reply: Use a password manager: it remembers a different long password for every site and fills it in, so you only need to know one strong password. Bitwarden is free and good, 1Password and Dashlane are the paid ones, and your phone and browser have a decent basic one built in.

instruction: I've been feeling really tired lately, and I'm wondering if my body has a built-in clock.
reply: Energy comes from sleep, daylight and food, in that order: the same bedtime and getting-up time every day, ten minutes outside in the morning light, and a lunch with protein and slow carbs rather than just a sandwich, so three o'clock does not flatten you. Water through the day and no caffeine after two help too.

instruction: What is density?
reply: Density is how much mass is packed into a volume: a block of iron and a block of foam the same size have very different densities. Water has a density of about 1 kg per litre, which is why things less dense than water float.

instruction: I'm looking for community events in my area. What kind of events usually happen in local communities?
reply: Put the dates on a blank timeline you draw yourself, and group them around a few anchor events you already know. Then link each new date to a story or a person rather than a bare number, and test yourself by covering the dates and filling them in.

instruction: I've noticed that some cultures seem to view time very differently. Can you tell me more about that?
reply: Time zones exist because the Earth turns: noon is when the Sun is highest, and that happens at a different moment in each place. The world is split into 24 zones of about an hour, so the clock roughly matches daylight; some countries bend the borders or use half-hour zones.

instruction: I'm trying to get back into working out, but I'm having trouble staying motivated. Do you have any tips?
reply: Make it small and scheduled: a set time, everything you need out and ready, and a session so short that skipping it feels sillier than doing it. Track the days you show up rather than the results, and do it with someone or book it like an appointment: habit carries you when motivation does not.

instruction: I'm looking for a new job, but my resume is outdated. What are some key things I should include?
reply: Two to four lines under your name, and the first thing anyone reads: the job you do or want, your strongest two pieces of evidence with a number in them, and what you are after next. Write it last, when you know what the CV holds, and aim it at the advert's job title.

instruction: I'm painting my room and I'm trying to decide on a color. What's a good color for a bedroom?
reply: Pick the thing you cannot change - the floor, the tiles, the worktop, the sofa - and take the wall colour out of it in a paler version of itself. Then add one deeper tone from the same family for a rug or cushions and a wood or a metal to warm it: three colours, one of them a near-neutral.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I'm not sure if I should take a nap or not.
reply: A short nap is worth having: 20 minutes, ideally before about 3pm, and set an alarm, because 90 minutes leaves you groggier than when you lay down. It helps most if you lost sleep the night before or you are driving later.

instruction: I need to measure the length of my room, but I don't have a tape measure. Is there a way to estimate it?
reply: Measure the pole or track, not the window, and add 10 to 20cm either side so the curtains cover the edges when closed. For the length, measure from the pole to where you want them to finish, then double the width for a full gather: one and a half times the width looks skimped.

instruction: I'm interested in gardening. What are some easy plants to care for?
reply: Spider plant, snake plant, pothos and the ZZ plant are the ones to start with: they take low light, a missed watering and a radiator, and still look fine. Water them when the compost is dry rather than on a schedule, keep them out of the hottest sun, and they will outlive the ones that want fussing.

instruction: I'm new to the gym and I want to start a workout routine. What's a good exercise for beginners?
reply: Buy one adjustable dumbbell or one kettlebell and nothing else to begin with: about 6 to 10 kg suits most beginners and 10 to 16 kg if you are already strong, and a used one goes for £40 to £80. Add a resistance band for about £10 and a step or a sturdy chair, and that covers squats, rows, presses and carries - a mat only if your floor is hard.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body in school, and I was wondering what the main function of the lungs is.
reply: An organ is a part of the body made of several tissues working together for one job: the heart pumps blood, the lungs take in oxygen and the liver cleans the blood. Your skin is the largest organ, and organs work together in systems.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about apps. What are some popular ways for apps to make money?
reply: Pick one thing and do it every week rather than signing up to three apps: a class, a club, a walking group, or a single app you actually answer. Say early what you are looking for, meet in daylight for something short - a coffee, not dinner - and tell a friend where you will be.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. Do dreams help us solve problems?
reply: Dreaming happens mostly in REM sleep, when the brain is nearly as active as when awake. Scientists think it helps sort memories and practise threats and feelings; there is no good evidence that dreams predict the future.

instruction: I'm going shopping for new clothes, but I'm worried about sizing. I've been noticing that different stores have different sizes for the same measurements.
reply: Sizes are not measurements, so treat the number on the label as a shop's opinion: women's UK sizes have crept up about two steps in fifty years, so a 1970s 16 is roughly today's 12, and every chain runs its own chart, which is why you can be a 20 in one shop and a 24 in the next door. Measure yourself once with a tape - bust at the fullest point, waist at the narrowest bit above the navel, hips at the widest, about 20cm below the waist - write the numbers in cm and use that shop's own size guide for that garment.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to New York City and I need to rent a car. What types of cars are available for rent?
reply: Buy a three- or four-year-old car with a loan if you keep cars five years or more: £12,000 over five years at 7% is about £240 a month, and at the end it is yours and still worth £4,000. Lease or PCP only wins if you want a new car every two or three years and drive under the mileage cap.

instruction: What is a carton used for?
reply: Most of it is air and packaging: flatten cartons, crush cans and squash bottles with the lid off, and the same bag holds twice as much. Put a smaller bin by the counter and take it out every night rather than waiting for the big one to fill, and keep a caddy beside it for peelings, which is often a third of the weight.

instruction: I'm looking for educational resources for my kids. Do you know any good websites for educational videos?
reply: *Wow in the World* is the best one to start with: science stories with two silly hosts, made for 5 to 8 year olds. *Story Pirates* turns stories children send in into sketches and songs, and *Circle Round* tells a folk tale in fifteen minutes with a proper cast.

instruction: I'm thinking about becoming a taxi driver. What kind of skills do I need to be a good taxi driver?
reply: Confidence comes from the route, not the traffic: ride the quiet-street version at a weekend, then take it on a weekday at a quieter hour, and repeat until the turns are automatic. Ride a door's width out from parked cars, take the middle of the lane at junctions so nobody squeezes past, and look back before you move over.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about popular sports. What are some of the most popular sports in the world?
reply: For football, *Football Weekly* from the Guardian is twice a week, quick and funny, and *The Rest Is Football* is Lineker, Richards and Shearer talking. For cricket, *Tailenders* is the one people who do not like cricket listen to.

instruction: I want to bake some cookies. Do you have a simple recipe?
reply: Stir 500g strong white flour, 325ml warm water, 7g yeast and 10g salt into a soft dough, knead it 8 minutes and leave it 1 to 2 hours until doubled. Stretch it thin, and bake as hot as your oven goes, 250C, for 10 to 12 minutes.

instruction: I'm looking for information about bohemian style clothing. What is it?
reply: Familiar, subdued clothes are the thing: black or dark colours, smart and comfortable, and nothing new needed. If the family asked for bright colours or a football shirt, follow that instead, because it's about them.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to the Grand Canyon. What is the best time to visit?
reply: Agree the length before you go, in the same breath as the date: two nights is plenty for most trips, and a day trip leaves you both glad to have seen each other. Take something for the table rather than a present, and book the way home before you arrive so the last hour is not the anxious one.

instruction: I'm looking for a nearby park to go for a hike. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Go for a canal towpath, a country park or a flat riverside path: wide, level, benches along it and nothing to climb over, which is what a short walk needs. Check the surface and the slope on the site's own page before you set off, because a walk advertised as circular can still hide a stile or a flight of steps, and ring ahead if someone uses a wheelchair - big attractions, National Trust and English Heritage places among them, lend one for free if it is booked a day or two in advance.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. What do you think about photography?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What are some healthy snacks?
reply: Cheese, chutney and an apple; cream cheese with smoked salmon or cucumber; hummus and something crunchy; butter and a sliced boiled egg with salt and pepper. Anything soft wants something crisp on it, and anything dry wants something wet.

instruction: I'm learning about electricity in school, and I was wondering what electricity is.
reply: Electricity is the flow of electric charge, usually electrons pushed along a wire by a voltage. A circuit has to be a complete loop: the source pushes the charge, the wires carry it, and a device like a bulb uses the energy as it passes.

instruction: I'm looking for a unique vacation spot. Can you suggest an off-the-beaten-path destination?
reply: Plan the outing around the walking. Go door to door - a taxi, or the bus that stops nearest the door - and make a bench or a cafe the turning point so the trip is two short walks with a sit in between.

instruction: I'm feeling tired and I'm thinking of taking a nap. What's a good length for a power nap?
reply: A short nap is worth having: 20 minutes, ideally before about 3pm, and set an alarm, because 90 minutes leaves you groggier than when you lay down. It helps most if you lost sleep the night before or you are driving later.

instruction: I'm a bit lost with my wardrobe. I have a pear-shaped body and I don't know what styles suit me best.
reply: Measure in a bra or a thin top, tape snug but not tight and level all the way round, and write three numbers in cm: bust at the fullest point, waist at the narrowest above the navel (bend sideways and the crease is it), and hips at the widest, about 20cm below the waist. Add your height and inside leg and you have everything a size guide asks for.

instruction: I'm trying to stay hydrated but I don't like plain water. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Fill a bottle in the morning and keep it where you sit, and put a glass by the kettle so every cup of tea comes with one. Drinking with meals and after every trip to the loo is the cheapest trigger.

instruction: I'm interested in the Olympics. What are the Paralympic Games?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: I'm going to the airport and I need a taxi. How much does a taxi ride to the airport usually cost?
reply: Pre-book it: the price at the barrier is often two or three times the pre-booked price for the same space, and the cheapest of all is usually a park-and-ride a few minutes out with a shuttle. Compare the total against the alternatives before you choose, because a week of parking often costs about what a taxi costs each way, and for two or three days the taxi, the train or a lift from a friend usually wins.

instruction: I'm looking for ideas on how to display my collection of vintage toys. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Charity shops take toys only if they are complete and clean, so a nursery, a sure start centre or a refuge will take what a shop will not, and a free-ad site clears a box of lego in a day. Wash what you have and put the pieces back in their boxes first.

instruction: I'm learning about figure skating jumps. What's the difference between a toe loop and a loop jump?
reply: Both feet stay on the ground behind the line, and the ball goes back over your head with both hands on it from behind - a foot over the line or a hand that comes round the side turns it over. Plant both feet shoulder width, get some bend in the elbows and throw it flat to a teammate's feet rather than high and looping.

instruction: My refrigerator is making a weird noise. What should I do?
reply: The steady hum is the compressor, which switches on and off to hold the temperature: it is normal, and it gets louder when the room is warm or the door has just been shut on warm food. A rattle or a buzz is usually the fridge not sitting level, so wind the front feet down until it stands firm, and check nothing is touching the back.

instruction: I have a doctor's appointment tomorrow, and I'm not sure what to expect.
reply: Book the check-up and say on the phone that you are nervous and have not been for a while - practices hear it every week, and most will give you a longer first appointment, a signal to stop, and no lecture. The first visit is usually a look round and an x-ray, nothing more, and you can agree to one small thing at a time.

instruction: I'm looking for some new toys for my pet. What kind of pet toys do you recommend?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed lately and I want to start a self-care routine. What are some good activities for relaxation?
reply: Pick the smallest physical thing first, because stress lives in the body: a slow breath out for longer than the breath in, a ten-minute walk, or a glass of water and something to eat if you have skipped a meal. Then write down what is actually on your plate and cut one thing or ask for one deadline to move.

instruction: I'm a bit worried about the storm forecast this weekend. How do storms get their names?
reply: A hurricane is a whole storm system hundreds of kilometres across, born over warm sea and lasting days, with winds over 119 km/h. A tornado is a narrow funnel of spinning air under a thunderstorm, usually tens of metres wide and gone in minutes.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to make my home more energy-efficient. What are some good options for appliances?
reply: Gas is much the cheapest for heat: about 6 to 7p a unit (kWh) against about 24 to 25p for electricity, so the same heat costs roughly a quarter as much, and that is why a gas boiler is the cheap way to warm a house. The one electric thing that competes is a heat pump, because it moves heat instead of making it - three units of heat for one of electricity puts it near or below gas - while panel heaters, fan heaters and an immersion are the dearest, at about four times the gas price for the same warmth.

instruction: I'm considering carpooling to work. What are some basic rules of carpool etiquette?
reply: Plan the driving days rather than the hours: put the stops in first, every two hours and one proper stop a day, and don't book more than six hours of driving in a day. Book the first and last night's bed before you go, check the spare tyre, the oil and the breakdown cover, and keep the overnight bag on the back seat.

instruction: I'm interested in painting as a hobby. What kind of art supplies do I need to get started?
reply: Before paint you need filler for the holes, fine sandpaper, masking tape, a dust sheet, a roller and tray, a brush for edges and an old screwdriver to open the tin. One litre of emulsion covers about 12 square metres, so measure the walls and buy two coats' worth.

instruction: I'm worried about electrical safety at home. What are some common hazards I should look out for?
reply: An electric shock happens when your body becomes part of a circuit: touching something live lets current flow through you to the ground, and it is the current, not the voltage alone, that does the harm. Switch the power off at the mains before touching anyone who is still connected, and call the emergency services if they are unconscious or burned.

instruction: I'm looking for advice on finding a mentor at work. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Two to four lines under your name, and the first thing anyone reads: the job you do or want, your strongest two pieces of evidence with a number in them, and what you are after next. Write it last, when you know what the CV holds, and aim it at the advert's job title.

instruction: I'm having trouble separating my work and personal life. Do you have any tips for setting boundaries?
reply: Leave only for a reason that still holds on a good day, and only once you could afford the gap. Three tests decide it.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my camera settings. What's the difference between ISO and aperture?
reply: In the camera app it is the row of modes above the shutter: swipe to Portrait and wait for the yellow box to say Depth effect before you shoot, because a photo taken too early comes out with no blur. It works best a metre or two from the person with a plain background behind them, and on most phones you can tap the f-number afterwards to change how much is blurred.

instruction: I'm worried about my cat's upcoming vet visit. What can I expect?
reply: Book boarding early, ask your vet for a recommendation, and visit before you book: clean, calm and willing to show you the runs tells you more than any website. A pet sitter at home suits cats far better than a cattery.

instruction: I'm learning about motion in physics class and I was wondering, what is velocity?
reply: Acceleration is how quickly speed changes, measured in metres per second squared: 2 m/s squared means each second it goes 2 m/s faster. A car from 0 to 60 mph in 9 seconds is accelerating at about 3 m/s squared, and gravity pulls a falling thing at about 9.8.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping lately. I'm 60 years old. Do you think my age has something to do with it?
