reply: It is common at four and still common at nine, but past ten it is less usual: constipation, an infection, diabetes and stress all cause it, so it is worth a GP visit whatever the age. Stop drinks an hour before bed, have them wee last thing, protect the mattress and never make it a shame.

instruction: I love watching cooking shows. What's your favorite cooking show?
reply: *Home Cooking* (Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway) answers listeners' kitchen questions and is the friendliest place to start. *The Sporkful* is about how and why people eat what they eat, and *Gastropod* takes one food an episode and does its history and science.

instruction: I'm having trouble at work. What are some key factors that affect job performance?
reply: Mostly it is the setup, not willpower: enough sleep, food, the phone in another room and one thing open at a time. Work in 25-minute blocks on a single task written down first, because choosing where to start is half the distraction, and stand up for the break.

instruction: I'm planning to roast some vegetables in the oven, but I'm not sure what temperature to use.
reply: Cut vegetables into similar-sized pieces, toss them with oil and salt and roast at 200C (180C fan) for 30 to 40 minutes, turning once. Give them space on the tray; a crowded tray steams instead of roasting.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a smart speaker for my home. What's the difference between Amazon Echo and Google Home?
reply: Press the microphone button on the speaker: on an Echo it is the circle with a line through it on top, and it glows red when the mics are off; a Google Home or Nest has a switch at the back. Nothing is recorded while it is off, and in the Alexa app, Settings > Alexa Privacy > Review Voice History lets you delete what it already has.

instruction: I'm thinking of installing a smart security system in my home. What are some popular options?
reply: On Windows you do not need to buy one: Microsoft Defender is built in, free and as good as the paid suites, and it updates itself. Phone and tablet: Play Protect on Android and an iPhone need nothing else.

instruction: I'm learning about earthquakes in school. What is an earthquake?
reply: An earthquake is the ground shaking when two slabs of the Earth's crust slip past each other and the energy built up is released as waves. The slipping happens at a fault, and the shaking is strongest near it.

instruction: I'm interested in gardening. What are some basic garden tools I'll need?
reply: Tidy the outline first, because a garden reads as untidy at its edges before its middle: cut the lawn edge right round with a half-moon edger, clear the path, and weed the first foot of border. Then buy three plants and no more - something tall, something scented by the door, and something that flowers for months - in pots if the soil is poor.

instruction: I'm going to a concert this weekend and I was wondering what makes a good concert sound system.
reply: A magnet and a coil push a cone in and out in time with the signal, and the moving cone moves the air, which is the sound. A small cone cannot shift much air, so it makes the high notes well and the bass not at all: that is why a speaker with a big cabinet and a port sounds fuller at the same volume.

instruction: I'm looking for a place to eat with my family. What types of restaurants are good for families?
reply: Cheap party food people actually eat: a big pot of chilli or a pasta bake, garlic bread, and a bowl of crisps and dips. For standing-up food, sausage rolls, cheese straws and fruit on sticks go further than anything fiddly.

instruction: I'm learning about chemistry in school, and I was wondering what an atom is.
reply: An atom is the smallest unit of an element, with a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons. Atoms join into molecules, and everything you can touch is made of them; they are mostly empty space.

instruction: I'm interested in theater acting. What are some key skills required to be a good theater actor?
reply: Most theatres are smart casual now: trousers or dark jeans and a nice top, with a jacket if it's a big West End or opera night. Nobody minds as long as you're warm and not in shorts.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What are some good foods for a balanced diet?
reply: Half the plate vegetables or salad, a quarter protein (fish, chicken, beans, eggs), a quarter starchy carbohydrate, plus a thumb of fat and fruit for pudding. If most meals look roughly like that and you drink water rather than fizzy drinks, you do not need to count anything.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. Is it true that the Earth's temperature is rising?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I have a gluten intolerance and I'm looking for some breakfast ideas.
reply: One moist thing and one with a bit of crunch or sharpness, and it stops being a sad sandwich: cheddar with apple and pickle, tuna with celery and a little mayo (drained, or the bread goes), hummus with grated carrot and cucumber, or leftover roast chicken with lettuce and mustard. Butter both slices to the edges first so the bread does not go soggy, and keep tomato or cucumber in the middle.

instruction: What is cotton fabric?
reply: Cotton breathes, takes up water and gets softer with washing; polyester does not absorb water, so it dries fast and wicks sweat, but it holds body oils and smell, which is why a cheap polyester top pongs after one wear. A blend is the compromise most clothes are: 60/40 polycotton creases less and dries faster than pure cotton, and 5% elastane in a cotton shirt is what stops it losing its shape.

instruction: I'm going grocery shopping and I'm looking for organic products. What's the difference between organic and non-organic?
reply: Ultra-processed food is the industrial end of the scale: things made mostly from extracts and additives - emulsifiers, colourings, flavourings, sweeteners - that you would not cook with at home, like fizzy drinks, crisps, sausages, ready meals and most breakfast cereal. The evidence is that people eat more of it and put on weight, but the class is broad enough that hummus and wholemeal bread land in it, so judge by the ingredient list rather than the label.

instruction: I'm interested in smart clothing. What is it?
reply: Smart casual usually means dark jeans or trousers with a collared shirt or a nice top, and clean shoes: tidy, no tie. If you're unsure, dress one step smarter than you think and ask the host.

instruction: I'm planning to host a party for my friends and I want to cook for them, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: Cheap party food people actually eat: a big pot of chilli or a pasta bake, garlic bread, and a bowl of crisps and dips. For standing-up food, sausage rolls, cheese straws and fruit on sticks go further than anything fiddly.

instruction: I'm looking for a beach vacation. What are some popular island getaways?
reply: Ask when you book what people wear there: smart casual (smart trousers or dark jeans and a collared shirt or a nice top) covers nearly every restaurant. Shorts and flip-flops are only right somewhere on the seafront.

instruction: I'm going to have a video call with some colleagues for the first time and I want to make a good impression. What are some basic etiquette rules I should follow?
reply: Treat it like a meeting, not a phone call: sit at a table with your notes, the job description and four stories written out in front of you - a week you organised, a difficult customer, something you fixed, a time you got it wrong and changed. Sit upright or stand, because the voice carries better.

instruction: I'm looking for online learning platforms. Have you heard of Khan Academy?
reply: Most evening courses are two or three hours of class a week plus about the same again at home, so plan on one evening and four or five hours a week. Ask for the guided learning hours before you enrol, because the college has to publish them, and check the fee: in England, English and maths up to GCSE are free for anyone who does not already have them, and a first level 2 or 3 qualification is often free if you are under 23 or on a low income.

instruction: I'm looking for information about different types of cars. What's the main difference between a sedan and a hatchback?
reply: Small, petrol, and as dull as you can bear: a hatchback like a Corsa, Fiesta, Polo or Yaris with a small engine. Check two things before the car itself - the insurance group, because a 1.0-litre in a low group can cost half what a bigger car costs to insure, and the MOT history on gov.uk for gaps and advisories.

instruction: I want to stay healthy. What are some basic things I can do to take care of my body?
reply: Start small and gentle: a piece of fruit, a yoghurt or a slice of toast, then wait twenty minutes before a proper meal. Fat, sugar and coffee on an empty stomach are what make people feel sick, shaky and headachy, so go easy on those and have a glass of water first.

instruction: I'm planning a weekend brunch for my family. What are some popular dishes to serve?
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I'm looking for information about Middle Eastern cuisine. What are some popular dishes?
reply: Pick a dish that is good on its own rather than meat with the meat left out: a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, a mushroom and lentil lasagne, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. One proper veggie main plus the usual sides is plenty, and it is worth asking what they actually eat, because vegetarian covers a wide range.

instruction: I'm an athlete and I'm looking for ways to improve my performance. I've heard that napping can be beneficial. Is that true?
reply: A short nap is worth having: 20 minutes, ideally before about 3pm, and set an alarm, because 90 minutes leaves you groggier than when you lay down. It helps most if you lost sleep the night before or you are driving later.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about tennis. Is tennis a popular sport?
reply: Club tennis is won by keeping the ball in, so play the percentages: height over the net and length to the back of the court, and count how many cross-court balls you can rally without missing - 20, then 30. Two sessions a week of that beats a new racket.

instruction: There was a big storm in my area last night. I'm worried about the damage.
reply: Count the seconds between the lightning and the thunder: every 3 seconds is about 1 km (5 seconds per mile). If the gap is under 30 seconds, the storm is close enough to be dangerous, so get indoors.

instruction: I'm a big fan of the local football team, the Wildcats. Do you know when their next game is?
reply: I can't see the schedule from here, sorry. The guide on the telly, or the station's own app, has the times, and the catch-up players - iPlayer, ITVX, Channel 4, BBC Sounds - keep the same list on the front page.

instruction: I'm looking for deals on laptops. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm looking for some team-building exercises for my soccer team. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm looking for eco-friendly cleaning products for my home. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: White vinegar for limescale, glass, the kettle and the shower screen; bicarbonate of soda for scouring a sink or a pan, a smelly fridge and a slow drain; lemon juice and salt for a wooden board and a copper pan. Two rules cover most of it: no vinegar on marble, stone or grout, because the acid eats them, and never vinegar with bleach, because the two together give off chlorine gas.

instruction: I'm starting a compost pile in my backyard. What can I put in it?
reply: Use a peat-free multi-purpose with a good third of perlite or grit stirred through for drainage, or a ready-made houseplant mix, which is the same thing in one bag. Garden soil in a pot sets like concrete and brings in pests, so leave it outside.

instruction: Will it be sunny today?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I want to cook something simple, what are some easy 5-ingredient recipes?
reply: Try a traybake, a stir-fry and a pasta this week: change one of three things and the same dinner comes out new - the shape (traybake, stir-fry, pasta, curry, soup), the carb under it (rice, potatoes, couscous, bread, noodles) or the sauce that finishes it (tomato, yoghurt and lemon, a spice paste, gravy, pesto). Mince is a ragu, a chilli with rice, or a cottage pie.

instruction: I'm having trouble reading my textbooks for school. Do you know any strategies that can help me?
reply: Read a section, then close the book and say its three points out loud before going on - rereading feels like study but the recall is what sticks. Turn each heading into a question first ("what is a supply curve?") and answer it from memory, then write one line per page in your own words.

instruction: I'm learning to play tennis. What is the most important part of a forehand shot?
reply: Toss the ball low and just in front of your hitting shoulder - a high toss behind you is why serves go long - then hit it with the heel of your hand, arm swinging fast and straight, and aim at a spot (deep middle, or the gap between two passers) rather than just over the net. Practise twenty a session and count the ones that land in: a serve that goes in beats an ace you miss.

instruction: I'm looking for a new music streaming app. What are some popular options?
reply: iPhone if you want the long updates and everything to talk to the rest of the family's; Android if you want to spend less, get two days of battery, or keep a headphone jack. The cheapest way in is a two-year-old iPhone or a mid-range Samsung, and both last well if you put a case on them.

instruction: I want to bake some gluten-free cookies. Do I need special flour?
reply: Not in baking: cornflour has no gluten, so a cake or a loaf will not hold or rise. As a thickener it works, at one tablespoon where the recipe asks for two of plain flour, mixed into cold liquid first.

instruction: I'm trying to learn a new language, but I'm having trouble remembering vocabulary. Do you have any tips?
reply: Learn seven to ten words at a time, out loud, and test yourself instead of reading the list: cover the English side and say the word, then swap. Put each new word in a short sentence you would actually say, and go back over yesterday's words for two minutes before adding new ones — spacing is what makes them stay.

instruction: I'm interested in photography as a hobby. What are some popular genres of photography?
reply: On any of them: *Knives Out* for a whodunnit everyone enjoys, *Happy Valley* or *The Bear* for a series you'll finish, *Paddington 2* if children are in the room. Say which service and the mood and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm having trouble waking up in the morning. What's a good alarm sound to use?
reply: In the Clock app, edit the alarm and tap Sound (iPhone) or the bell icon (Android) - on an iPhone the list ends with Pick a Song, which uses anything in your library, and on Android there is usually a plus sign to add a file. Start quiet and put the phone across the room: a gentle sound you have to get up to stop wakes you better than a loud one by the bed.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm interested in learning more about inquiry-based learning. What is it?
reply: It means getting to understand something that is not clicking yet. What is the thing?

instruction: I've been having some weird dreams lately and I was wondering, do different cultures believe in the same things about dreams?
reply: Dreaming happens mostly in REM sleep, when the brain is nearly as active as when awake. Scientists think it helps sort memories and practise threats and feelings; there is no good evidence that dreams predict the future.

instruction: I'm taking my dog to the vet tomorrow and I'm a little nervous. What should I do to prepare?
reply: Ask for the first appointment of the day and wait in the car until it is your turn, with a towel over the carrier. Leave the carrier out all week with a worn T-shirt in it and feed her beside it, so it is not the thing that only means the vet.

instruction: I'm interested in Olympic records. What's the most Olympic gold medals won by an individual?
reply: Martina Navratilova has nine singles titles, the record, and Roger Federer has eight among the men. Serena Williams won seven.

instruction: I'm looking for ways my grandparents can help with childcare for my toddler. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Sort the money and the childcare before the feelings, because those two keep the week running: check what you can claim (universal credit, the childcare element), and ask the council about a nursery place. Then build one reliable adult - a grandparent, a neighbour, another parent at the gate - for the evenings you are stuck.

instruction: I'm looking for live music events in my area. What's a good website to check?
reply: I can't see what's on at your local venues from here, sorry. The venue's own site or a listings app has the times and the tickets, and it is the same page for a film, a play or a gig.

instruction: I'm looking for a new way to stay active, I've heard about Nordic walking. What is it?
reply: Yes: it builds flexibility and balance and strengthens the muscles that hold you up, and it counts as exercise, though the heart and lungs get less from it than from a brisk walk. Two or three sessions a week is where the change shows, and a weekly class plus ten minutes at home most days is the usual way people keep it up.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby, something creative. I enjoy cooking and trying new recipes.
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm learning about animal senses. Do dogs have good eyesight?
reply: Bats are not blind: they see about as well as a cat in dim light. What makes them special is echolocation, squeaks too high to hear that bounce back and tell them where things are in the dark.

instruction: I'm trying to get back into a regular exercise routine. What's a good way to start?
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about social media analytics. What is it?
reply: The phone already counts it: Settings > Mobile data on an iPhone, or Settings > Network > Data usage on Android, shows the month's total and which apps are eating it. Video and social apps are nearly always the top two, and turning off background refresh and auto-play on mobile data usually halves it.

instruction: I'm going shopping this weekend. What's the difference between window shopping and comparison shopping?
reply: Buying online gives you a 14-day right to change your mind from the day it arrives, and you only pay the return postage unless the shop says otherwise; buying in a shop gives you no right to change your mind at all, only the shop's own policy. That is the real difference, not the price.

instruction: I'm planning a trip and I was thinking of taking a train. What are the main types of passenger trains?
reply: *Codenames* (2 minutes to learn, works with any group), *Ticket to Ride* (simple, satisfying trains) and *Sushi Go!* (fast, small, cheap) are the three to start with. All are done in under an hour.

instruction: I'm learning about colors and I was wondering, what is a color wheel?
reply: Pot a red (1 point), then a colour (2 to 7), and put the colour back on its spot; carry on that way until the reds are gone, then take the colours in order. The maximum break is 147: fifteen reds with fifteen blacks, then all the colours.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to relieve muscle soreness after a workout. What's a good piece of equipment to use?
reply: That ache a day or two after new or harder exercise is delayed-onset muscle soreness, not damage: it is the muscle repairing itself and it peaks around 48 hours and eases within four days. Keep moving gently, drink water and sleep, and start lighter next time; see someone if one spot is sharp, swollen or bruised, or if your urine goes cola-coloured.

instruction: I'm a bit worried about the storm forecasted for tonight. What should I do to stay safe?
reply: Go by the forecast for the hours you will actually be out rather than for the whole day, and dress for the coldest and wettest of those hours. As a rule of thumb: under about 10 degrees a proper coat, between 10 and 18 a jumper with something windproof over it, over 18 no coat and loose cotton instead.

instruction: I have a brother and a sister, and we always fight. Is that normal?
reply: Name it once without defending yourself - "it can't have felt fair, watching me get that" - and then ask what it was like from where they stood, which is the only thing that shifts it. Arguing the facts never does: a jealous brother is not short of facts, he is short of a hearing.

instruction: I'm looking for a way to cook a tender pot roast. What's the best method?
reply: A roast is one joint, potatoes, two veg and gravy, and the veg is where you ring the changes: carrots and parsnips roasted round the meat for the last 45 minutes, greens or cabbage steamed, and peas with mint if it is lamb. Add Yorkshire puddings for beef, stuffing and apple sauce for pork, bread sauce for chicken or turkey.

instruction: I'm looking for a new coffee maker for my kitchen. What types are available?
reply: Most of the cup is milk: a latte is about five parts steamed milk to one of espresso, so roughly 200ml of milk and a 60ml double shot in a medium, and 300 to 350ml of milk in a large. A flat white is the same coffee with about half of that, 100 to 120ml, and a cappuccino sits between the two at about 150ml - a third of it foam, so ask for it wet if you want more milk and dry if you want more air.

instruction: I'm trying to update my wardrobe, but I'm not sure how to incorporate the latest fashion trends into my personal style.
reply: Take everything out and put back only what you wore last year, in one go, with a bag for the charity shop by your feet. Then group by what you put on together - work, weekend, gym - rather than by type, and hang the long things at one end so the space under them takes a box.

instruction: I'm looking for a new breakfast cereal. What's a popular one?
reply: A box of cereal is about £2 to £3.50, and the shop's own version of a branded one about half the price. A big bag of own-brand flakes is the cheapest breakfast there is a bowl.

instruction: I'm looking for milk alternatives. What are some popular options?
reply: Pasteurised milk is fine, and worth drinking: about three servings of dairy a day covers the calcium and iodine a baby needs. The one to skip is unpasteurised milk and anything made with it - some farm-shop milk, and raw-milk cheese - because of listeria.

instruction: I'm interested in starting yoga for beginners. What's the best way to get started?
reply: Five minutes, in two parts: first something easy that gets you slightly out of breath - a brisk walk, a slow jog, skipping, the exercise bike - then a few quick movements through the range you are about to use, like leg swings, arm circles, hip circles and ten bodyweight squats. Start the first set lighter than the rest.

instruction: I'm interested in cycling races. What are some popular types?
reply: Write tomorrow's list down before bed: most of the racing is your head keeping the list for you. Then a slow breathing pattern, in for four and out for six, for a couple of minutes, and get up rather than lie there arguing with yourself if it goes on past 20 minutes.

instruction: I'm looking for information about my local government. What are the main responsibilities of my city council?
reply: Your council is the layer below parliament, and it is usually two layers: a district or unitary council for bins, housing, planning permission and licensing, and a county council for schools, social care, libraries and most roads. It is paid for by council tax plus business rates and grants, and the councillors are elected locally every four years.

instruction: I want to learn about poaching eggs. What is the best way to poach an egg?
reply: Bring a pan of water to a bare simmer with a splash of vinegar, stir it into a gentle whirlpool and slide the egg in from a cup. 3 minutes gives a soft yolk; lift it out with a slotted spoon onto kitchen paper.

instruction: I'm looking for information about celebrity fashion lines. Can you tell me about some popular ones?
reply: Ask the teacher or the dance school first: for a show they usually name a supplier, sell the costume themselves or keep a rail of spares, and buying the wrong shade of leotard wastes the money. If it is yours to sort, hiring costs less than buying for one night, fancy-dress shops and second-hand marketplaces have plenty a week before, and a plain base layer with two bought accessories reads perfectly well from the audience.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What are some things that can help me fall asleep faster?
reply: Anchor the wake-up time first and let the bedtime follow: get up at the same time every day, weekend included, and get outside into daylight within an hour of it, because morning light is what sets the clock. Then move bedtime fifteen minutes at a time, a couple of nights each, rather than an hour overnight.

instruction: I'm a soccer coach and I'm trying to decide on a formation for my team. What's the difference between a 4-4-2 and a 4-3-3?
reply: Five substitutions from three stoppage windows in the Premier League and most competitions, plus a sixth in extra time; it was three until 2020. A bench of nine is named, so most of the squad gets a game.

instruction: I'm trying to eat healthier. What are some good fruits to eat?
reply: Berries are the best fruit for the calories - about 30 to 60 per 100g - and a 80g portion counts towards your five a day, with vitamin C, fibre and the red and purple pigments that give them their colour. Frozen ones are just as good and a lot cheaper out of season.

instruction: I'm looking for a new washing machine. What types are available?
reply: About 15p a wash at 30C in electricity, against 25p at 40C: heating the water is most of what a wash costs, so 30C is the cheapest cycle that still cleans everyday clothes, shirts and jeans properly with a modern detergent. Go to 40C for heavily soiled work clothes and 60C for towels, bedding and anything with a stomach bug or a cold, because that is about killing germs rather than shifting dirt.

instruction: I'm planning a family dinner tonight. Do you have any suggestions for a fun family activity we can do together?
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new book to read. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: For funny, *The Thursday Murder Club* by Richard Osman is the easy pick: short chapters, a mystery that keeps moving, and jokes on every page. *Three Men in a Boat* if you want an old one that still makes people laugh out loud, or *Good Omens* by Pratchett and Gaiman for something daft and warm.

instruction: What are the main groups of animals?
reply: A vertebrate is an animal with a backbone: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals are the five groups. The backbone is a column of bones or cartilage that protects the spinal cord, and it lets the animal grow large and move actively.

instruction: I'm trying to update my wardrobe, but I'm not sure what my personal style is. How does personal style evolve over time?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm trying to get to the city center. What's the fastest way to get there?
reply: For a night before an early flight, book an airport hotel with a shuttle and check the first and last shuttle times before you pay - a 4am shuttle that stops at 11pm is the usual trap, and so is a "5 minutes from the terminal" that is five minutes by car on a road with no pavement. A town two or three stops away on the train, or a park-and-fly with the transfer included, is usually about half the price; add up the transfer, the parking and the extra hour and pick on the total.

instruction: I'm going to a concert next weekend and I want to buy some merchandise. What kind of things can I usually find at a concert?
reply: Ask whoever organised it whether it's drinks in a bar or a sit-down dinner, then go smart casual one notch up: dark trousers or jeans with a nice top, which works whether people dress up or not. Comfortable shoes, because these nights are long.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to, I like pop music.
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. Is it true that the sea level is rising?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm interested in the Olympics. What is the Olympic Village?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: I'm going shopping and I want to make a shopping list. What's the best way to do that?
reply: Not needed for a simple list: bread, milk and eggs. Put one in when 'and' joins two complete sentences (I booked the table, and she drove), or when the list items are long enough that the reader needs the pause: we need the report signed, the photos checked, and the invoice sent.

instruction: I'm interested in theater direction. What is the role of a theater director?
reply: Most theatres are smart casual now: trousers or dark jeans and a nice top, with a jacket if it's a big West End or opera night. Nobody minds as long as you're warm and not in shorts.

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about baseball. What's the objective of the game?
reply: Games go to 11 and you serve every two points, so a game turns faster than it looks: serve short and low, keep the ball on the table rather than hitting it hard, and step back only when you have to. The basics win club games - a heavy spin serve, a steady block, and returning the serve rather than trying to win the point with it.

instruction: I'm learning about the life cycle of frogs. What is the first stage?
reply: A life cycle is the stages a living thing goes through from one generation to the next: a frog goes egg, tadpole, froglet, adult, and a butterfly goes egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. A plant's is seed, seedling, flowering plant, then seed again.

instruction: I'm planning a baby shower for my sister. What are some common games we can play?
reply: *Dobble*, *UNO* and *Snakes and Ladders* work for a range of ages, and *Catan Junior* if they are ready for a proper board game. For a rainy afternoon, a treasure hunt round the house costs nothing and takes the longest.

instruction: What is wind speed?
reply: Wind is air moving from an area of high pressure to one of low pressure, and the sun creates those differences by heating land and sea unevenly. The bigger the pressure gap, the stronger the wind.

instruction: I'm planning a road trip from New York to Los Angeles. What's the best route to take?
reply: Pick a route you already know on quiet streets, ride it once at a weekend so the turns are not a surprise, and start with two days a week rather than five. Leave a lock, a spare tube and a pair of shoes at work, so there is nothing to carry and nothing to forget.

instruction: My friend has a peanut allergy and accidentally ate some peanuts. What should I do?
reply: There is nothing to avoid: peanuts, tree nuts and nut butters are fine while you are breastfeeding, and cutting them out of your own diet does not stop your baby getting an allergy, so eat them as you normally would. If your baby has already reacted to something you ate, that is worth showing to the GP or health visitor, but most rashes and windy nights are not the nuts.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan. What are some popular tourist attractions?
reply: Tokyo has about 14 million people in the city, and about 37 million in the wider metro area, which makes it the biggest in the world.

instruction: I'm looking for a part-time job. What's a typical part-time schedule?
reply: Try the smallest real version first: an evening course, one freelance job, or a sideways move inside your current employer. Talk to three people doing the job now and ask what the bad days are like, not the good ones.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about famous historical figures. Can you tell me about Leonardo da Vinci?
reply: Leonardo da Vinci (1452-1519) was an Italian painter, engineer and anatomist: the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper on one side, notebooks of flying machines and dissected bodies on the other. Fewer than twenty of his paintings survive, and it is the range of his curiosity that made him famous.

instruction: I'm looking for a new hobby and I'm interested in cycling. What kind of bike should I get?
reply: A hybrid or gravel bike with 32 to 40mm tyres, mudguard and rack mounts and disc brakes: those stop in the wet and take a pannier. £500 to £800 new, £200 to £350 secondhand.

instruction: I want to learn about stir-frying. What is it?
reply: A soggy stir-fry is a crowded pan: cook it in two batches over the highest heat you have, dry the vegetables well first, and add any sauce only at the very end off the heat.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. Do you have any suggestions for my bedroom environment?
reply: Cool the room rather than the bed: open windows on both sides for a through draught, keep the curtains shut in the day, and put a bowl of ice in front of a fan. A lukewarm shower before bed, cotton sheets and a hot water bottle filled with cold water at your feet all help more than sleeping with no cover at all.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about upcoming smartphone technology. What's new?
reply: Most phones get security updates for five to seven years from new - an iPhone around five or six, a Samsung flagship about four, a cheap Android two or three - so a phone keeps working well for about four years, and the battery is usually what gives out first. A £50 to £90 battery swap buys two or three more years, which is far cheaper than a new handset.

instruction: I'm learning about plants in school. What do plants need to grow?
reply: Soil holds a plant up and holds the two things it needs: water around the roots and the minerals it cannot make itself, like nitrogen for leaves and phosphorus for roots. Plants can grow without it only if someone feeds them those minerals in water, which is how hydroponics works.

instruction: I'm going shopping for new clothes this weekend. What are the current fashion trends?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about ecosystems. What is an ecosystem?
reply: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the non-living parts they depend on - soil, water, air and sunlight - interacting in one place. A pond, a woodland and a garden are ecosystems, and they work because energy flows through them and materials are recycled.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a smartwatch. What's the main purpose of a smartwatch?
reply: Worth it if you want steps, heart rate and messages without getting the phone out; not worth it if what you really want is a watch that runs for a week. A Garmin or Fitbit goes five days or more and an Apple Watch about one, and an Apple Watch needs an iPhone, so check the pairing before you choose.

instruction: I'm going to a concert this weekend and I was wondering about the sound system they use.
reply: A magnet and a coil push a cone in and out in time with the signal, and the moving cone moves the air, which is the sound. A small cone cannot shift much air, so it makes the high notes well and the bass not at all: that is why a speaker with a big cabinet and a port sounds fuller at the same volume.

instruction: I'm trying to organize my cleaning supplies. Where should I store them?
reply: A pantry or larder is a cool, dark, dry cupboard for the food that keeps: tins, dried pasta and rice, flour, sugar, oil, spices. Cool and dry matter more than size - a shelf by a radiator or a sunny window turns flour and rice stale and brings weevils - so put it on an outside wall away from the cooker.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. What's the recommended sleep duration for adults?
reply: Sleep is when the brain files the day's memories and clears waste, and the body repairs muscle and releases growth hormone. Most adults need seven to nine hours; if you are short for weeks, mood, concentration and immunity suffer before you feel sleepy.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to the beach this weekend. What's the weather forecast?
reply: Go by the forecast for the hours you will actually be out rather than for the whole day, and dress for the coldest and wettest of those hours. As a rule of thumb: under about 10 degrees a proper coat, between 10 and 18 a jumper with something windproof over it, over 18 no coat and loose cotton instead.

instruction: I'm looking to start a board game collection. What are some popular board games for beginners?
reply: *Dobble*, *UNO* and *Snakes and Ladders* work for a range of ages, and *Catan Junior* if they are ready for a proper board game. For a rainy afternoon, a treasure hunt round the house costs nothing and takes the longest.

instruction: What are some fun things to do at school during the holidays?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm going to the gym and I want to know how to stay healthy and avoid germs.
reply: For a first session you need very little: shorts or leggings that stretch, a t-shirt, trainers with a bit of support, a water bottle, a small towel and a padlock for the locker. That is the whole list - no gym turns anyone away for supermarket kit, and the machines are set up for exactly that.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about traffic calming measures. What are some common types?
reply: Join on the slip road at the speed of the traffic already there, because arriving slowly is the thing that makes it frightening: mirror, indicate, then match the lorries in the left lane. Keep left unless you are overtaking, leave a two-second gap to the car in front (double it in rain, and further in spray at night), and do not sit alongside a lorry where the driver cannot see you.

instruction: I'm having trouble balancing my work and family time. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Take the smallest break that is really a break, and take it today: twenty minutes out of the house without your phone, or a bath with the door shut while someone else does bedtime. Then lower the bar for the rest of the day - one meal, one wash, no craft - because a worn-out parent does not need a plan, they need an hour.

instruction: I'm going on a hike tomorrow and I'm worried about snake bites. What should I do if I get bitten?
reply: Wash the bite, then hold something cold on it for ten minutes, and for the itch use a pharmacy antihistamine tablet or a hydrocortisone cream - try not to scratch, because broken skin is what gets infected. Keep them off with DEET or picaridin repellent on exposed skin and cover up from late afternoon.

instruction: I'm learning about baseball and I was wondering, what are the main positions in baseball?
reply: One team bats to score runs and the other bowls and fields to get them out; an over is six balls, and an innings ends when ten batters are out or the overs run out. You are out if the ball hits your stumps, if a fielder catches it before it bounces, if you are run out, or leg before wicket — hit on the pads by a ball that was going to hit the stumps.

instruction: I'm learning about genetics and heredity in school. What's the difference between a dominant and recessive trait?
reply: A gene is a section of DNA that holds the instructions for making one thing the body needs, usually a protein: eye colour, blood type and how a muscle works all come from genes. You inherit half your genes from each parent, and they switch on and off depending on the cell.

instruction: I'm curious about magnets and compasses. How do compasses work?
reply: Magnetism is the force a magnet exerts on other magnets and on iron, nickel and cobalt, carried by a magnetic field around the magnet. Like poles repel and opposite poles attract, and a compass needle is a tiny magnet lining up with Earth's field.

instruction: I want to gain muscle, what should I eat?
reply: Aim for a palm-sized portion of protein at each meal - eggs, milk or yoghurt at breakfast, beans, lentils or chicken at lunch, fish or mince at dinner - which lands most adults near the 0.75g per kilo of body weight they need. Greek yoghurt, cottage cheese, tinned fish, eggs, tofu and lentils are the cheapest ways to add it.

instruction: I'm looking for some discounts on summer clothes. Do you know if there are any sales going on?
reply: Ask the person who can say yes, not the till: "is there anything you can do on the price?" Have a number and somewhere cheaper to point at, and ask about ex-display or last season's colour. At a market or on a big ticket offer about 10 per cent under, ready to walk away; a shop that cannot move can often throw in delivery instead.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping lately. Do you think it's because of the seasonal change?
reply: Feeling flat and tired in January or the dark months is common: less daylight shifts sleep and mood, and most people pick up by March. Get outside within an hour of waking, even on a grey day, keep up vitamin D in winter, and keep seeing people.

instruction: I'm looking for information about plants. What are some popular types of houseplants?
reply: A houseplant that will not flower is usually short of light or being fed too much: most of them need a bright spot with a few hours of sun a day to set buds, and a feed high in nitrogen grows leaves at the flowers' expense, so switch to a tomato feed with more potash in late summer. Peace lilies and Christmas cacti also want cooler nights and a slightly pot-bound root to be nudged into flower; African violets want the light and nothing else changed.

instruction: I'm having some issues with my video calls. The quality is really bad.
reply: Sit closer to the router or use a cable, and shut the other heavy things on the laptop: a browser with twenty tabs is usually the cause of a freezing call. Turn the video off when the sound matters more, and in Zoom or Teams set the video to a lower quality - a still picture and clear sound beats a frozen face.

instruction: I'm looking for parking near the city center. Do you know any available spots?
reply: The side streets five to ten minutes further out are where the free and cheap spaces are: read the sign at the entrance, because a residents' bay or a one-hour limit is what the tickets come from. For a station or a town centre, the station car park or a park and ride is usually cheaper than the multi-storey, and the parking apps (RingGo, PayByPhone, JustPark) show the live price and let you top up from your phone.

instruction: I need to measure the length of a room. What tool should I use?
reply: Work out the area first and then add a tenth: a 2m by 3m floor is 6 square metres, and with 10 per cent for cuts and breakages you want 6.6, so buy 7. A box tells you how many square metres it covers - usually about 1.2 to 1.5 - so divide by that and round up, and for a wall measure the height times the width and take off the door and the window.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Paris and I'm on a tight budget. What's the cheapest time to visit?
reply: Go at the time you would actually go, on a weekday evening if that is when you are free: a gym that is full at six is the one you stop using. Then check three things - the distance from home or work, because anything past fifteen minutes gets skipped, whether the classes you want are included in the price or cost extra, and the notice period on the contract, which is often a month and sometimes three.

instruction: I'm having trouble staying organized with my schoolwork. Do you have any tips for managing my homework?
reply: Most primary homework is 20 to 30 minutes a night by the last years at primary, and about an hour a night in year 7 and up, with a break part way. If a piece runs well past that, write a note to the teacher rather than pushing through it, because homework that takes an hour and ends in tears is usually the wrong homework.

instruction: I'm looking for ideas for my kid's packed lunch. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Cheap food that people finish and that travels: a big bowl of pasta salad, sausage rolls or sausages on sticks, cheese and crackers, and a tray of fairy cakes. Keep it to things you can make the day before, and buy the paper plates.

instruction: I'm looking for a snack. Do you know any good granola bars?
reply: Fruit and a spoon of honey, granola or toasted oats for crunch, and nuts or seeds for texture; a spoon of peanut butter and a little cocoa makes it taste like dessert. Plain yoghurt with chopped cucumber, mint, salt and garlic is a dip instead, and it wants straining first if it is watery.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to New York City. What is the best way to get around the city?
reply: New York City has about 8.3 million people - 8.3 million in the five boroughs, and around 19 million in the metro area. It is the biggest city in the United States.

instruction: I'm looking for a gift for my sister's birthday. What kind of personalized gifts do you have?
reply: Get something that shows you noticed: a book by an author they mentioned, a better version of something they use every day, or an afternoon planned around their favourite thing. The best gifts are specific to one person, so start from what they talk about.

instruction: I'm planning to go shopping for some new clothes. What should I do first?
reply: Lay everything out and take half the clothes and twice the money: three tops, two bottoms, one warm layer and shoes you can walk in covers a week. Roll clothes, keep a change in your hand luggage, and buy anything you forget when you arrive.

instruction: I'm feeling tired lately and I'm not sure if I'm sleeping enough. How much sleep do adults need?
reply: Sleep is when the brain files the day's memories and clears waste, and the body repairs muscle and releases growth hormone. Most adults need seven to nine hours; if you are short for weeks, mood, concentration and immunity suffer before you feel sleepy.

instruction: I'm looking for a snack. Do you know anything about rice cakes?
reply: Yesterday's rice makes great fried rice: heat a little oil, add the cold rice and fry it hard for 3 minutes without stirring much, then push it aside and scramble an egg in the gap with soy sauce, peas or whatever vegetables you have.

instruction: I have a cat and I'm worried about her dental health. What can I do to help?
reply: Keep it to one minute and start when she is already sleepy, after a meal: let her sniff the brush and put it down beside her first, then do one stroke along her back, a treat, and stop while she is still happy. A soft rubber glove or a short-bristled brush hurts less than a metal comb on a short coat, and the belly, tail and legs are for the vet or the groomer, not for a cat who already hates it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new purse. What are some popular types of handbags right now?
reply: Start with very little: trainers or astro boots, shorts or leggings, a water bottle and, for football or hockey, shin pads. Clubs lend sticks, bats and bibs to beginners, so email and ask what they provide before you buy anything.

instruction: I'm looking for a new book to read. What are some popular fiction genres?
reply: For funny, *The Thursday Murder Club* by Richard Osman is the easy pick: short chapters, a mystery that keeps moving, and jokes on every page. *Three Men in a Boat* if you want an old one that still makes people laugh out loud, or *Good Omens* by Pratchett and Gaiman for something daft and warm.

instruction: I'm looking for some inspiration for my summer wardrobe. What's a popular trend this season?
reply: Take everything out and put back only what you wore last year, in one go, with a bag for the charity shop by your feet. Then group by what you put on together - work, weekend, gym - rather than by type, and hang the long things at one end so the space under them takes a box.

instruction: What is a cube?
reply: A cuboid is a box shape with six rectangular faces, like a brick or a cereal box. Its volume is length times width times height, and a cube is the special cuboid where all three are equal.

instruction: I'm new to weightlifting at the gym. What is spotting in weightlifting?
reply: Spotting between periods is usually one of four things: the small hormone dip at ovulation, about 14 days before the next period; the pill, implant or coil, especially in the first three months; a harmless growth on the cervix or a patch of it that bleeds easily; or an infection, chlamydia among them. Note the days it happens for two or three cycles, take a sexual health test if you have changed partners, and see a GP if it keeps happening.

instruction: I'm running low on shampoo. What are some key things to look for when buying a new one?
reply: Shampoo just the roots, condition only the ends, and finish with cool water. Washing with a harsh shampoo every day makes oil come back faster, so try every other day for a fortnight and it usually settles.

instruction: I'm looking for a new laptop, can I buy it online from your store?
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm looking for a full-time job. What's a typical full-time schedule?
reply: A full-time week is usually 37.5 or 40 hours on paper, and the shift shape is what changes the answer. A nurse is contracted to 37.5 hours, worked as three 12-hour shifts a week plus the odd fourth, and a care worker often has the same 12-hour pattern.

instruction: I'm looking for a full-body workout routine to do at home. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Two or three sessions a week of five moves covers the whole body at home: squats or sit-to-stands for legs, press-ups (hands on a worktop if needed) for chest and arms, a row pulling a loaded bag or a band towards you for the back, glute bridges for hips, and a plank for the middle. Do two or three sets of eight to twelve, and add a little each week - more reps, a slower lower, a heavier bag - because muscle only grows when the last rep is hard.

instruction: I'm learning about food chains in school. What's a food chain?
reply: A food chain is the line of who eats whom, starting with a plant that makes its own food and ending with a predator. Energy is lost at every step, which is why top predators are few and a chain rarely has more than four or five links.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to, do you know anything about hip-hop?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm doing some home maintenance this weekend and I was wondering what I should check for in terms of home safety.
reply: Do the safety things this week, not later: a lockable back gate, an alarm on the door, a card in a pocket with your number, and tell the neighbours and the local police what to do if they see them out alone. Ring the council's adult social care line and ask for a carer's assessment and a telecare alarm; wandering usually needs a person checking in during the day, and that is arranged, not improvised.

instruction: I'm planning my sister's birthday party and I was wondering about some family traditions for birthdays.
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan and I'm interested in learning about rail passes.
reply: *Codenames* (2 minutes to learn, works with any group), *Ticket to Ride* (simple, satisfying trains) and *Sushi Go!* (fast, small, cheap) are the three to start with. All are done in under an hour.

instruction: I'm learning about ecosystems in school. What are some types of ecosystems?
reply: An ecosystem is a community of living things plus the non-living parts they depend on - soil, water, air and sunlight - interacting in one place. A pond, a woodland and a garden are ecosystems, and they work because energy flows through them and materials are recycled.

instruction: I'm planning to use video calls for my work meetings. Are video calls secure?
reply: It isn't dangerous, but the light and the story keep your brain alert, so you fall asleep later and wake more in the night. If you need something playing, a podcast or radio set to sleep is easier on sleep than a screen.

instruction: I'm planning a weekend trip to the beach. What are some must-try foods when I'm there?
reply: Cheese, chutney and an apple; cream cheese with smoked salmon or cucumber; hummus and something crunchy; butter and a sliced boiled egg with salt and pepper. Anything soft wants something crisp on it, and anything dry wants something wet.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed lately. Can you tell me what emotional intelligence is?
reply: Anger is the body's alarm at a threat or at a goal being blocked: adrenaline speeds your heart and tenses your muscles, and the emotional part of the brain reacts before the thinking part has caught up. It usually passes in minutes; slow breathing and naming what set it off help it pass sooner.

instruction: I'm hungry, what's a good breakfast food?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I love sunny days, is sunshine good for my health?
reply: Take 10 micrograms (400 IU) of vitamin D every day through autumn and winter, roughly October to March: the sun is too low in the sky here for your skin to make it, however grey or bright the day is. From April to September, short spells outside with hands and face uncovered is enough for most people, and oily fish, eggs and fortified cereal help the rest of the year.

instruction: I'm hungry, what are some common lunch options?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm looking for a new cutting board. What are the different types?
reply: A board slides because nothing is gripping the worktop, and the fix is a tea towel: wet it, wring it out and spread it flat underneath, and the board will not move - that is what kitchens do rather than anything you buy. A non-slip mat cut to size or a rubber band round each end does the same.

instruction: I'm looking for some vegetarian main course ideas. What are some popular options?
reply: Pick a dish that is good on its own rather than meat with the meat left out: a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, a mushroom and lentil lasagne, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. One proper veggie main plus the usual sides is plenty, and it is worth asking what they actually eat, because vegetarian covers a wide range.

instruction: I'm going on a beach vacation next week and I'm not sure what to pack.
reply: A rug, a cool bag with a freezer block, plates and cups you do not mind losing, a bottle opener, napkins, a bin bag and water. Skip anything heavy with mayonnaise unless it is eaten within the hour: sausage rolls, cheese, fruit and a flask keep for hours.

instruction: What's the difference between a physical change and a chemical change?
reply: A chemical reaction is when substances rearrange their atoms to make new ones: bonds break, new bonds form, and the starting materials are used up. Burning, rusting, baking and digestion are all reactions, and they usually give out or take in heat.

instruction: I'm looking for some information about video game storytelling. What makes a good video game story?
reply: *Wow in the World* is the best one to start with: science stories with two silly hosts, made for 5 to 8 year olds. *Story Pirates* turns stories children send in into sketches and songs, and *Circle Round* tells a folk tale in fifteen minutes with a proper cast.

instruction: I'm planning a road trip to the beach this weekend and I was wondering about the traffic laws in that area.
reply: Most beaches allow dogs, but plenty of councils ban them on the main stretch from about May to September, so read the sign where you walk on: it names the beach and the months, and the council's own page lists the rest. Take fresh water, because sea water gives a dog the runs, and go early or late on a hot day as sand and pebbles burn pads.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about different languages and cultures. What's the most widely spoken language in the world?
reply: Pick by what you will actually use it for, not by which is easiest on paper: the language of the country you visit, or of the family you are marrying into, beats any ranking. With no reason to choose, Spanish is the usual bet - about 500 million speakers, spelling that matches the sound, and a lot of cheap material - and if you already have French or Italian, the other one of the pair is the cheapest start of all.

instruction: I'm trying to reduce my carbon footprint. What's a simple way to start?
reply: A carbon footprint is the total greenhouse gas your choices add up to in a year, counted as carbon dioxide: heating, electricity, flights, car trips, the food and things you buy. A typical UK footprint is around 10 tonnes a year, and flying and meat are usually the biggest single items.

instruction: I'm going to a meeting in the city center, but I'm worried about traffic congestion. What's the current traffic situation like?
reply: Nobody can tell you before you go: a walk-in centre sees people in the order they need seeing rather than the order they arrived, so a queue of two hours can move in twenty minutes when something urgent comes in, and a quiet room can still mean a long wait. Ring the centre or look at its own site on the day for the wait it is running, and go early rather than late in the evening.

instruction: I'm looking for information about baseball bats. What materials are they made of?
reply: Bats are not blind: they see about as well as a cat in dim light. What makes them special is echolocation, squeaks too high to hear that bounce back and tell them where things are in the dark.

instruction: I have a cat and I'm worried she's getting bored. What can I do to keep her entertained?
reply: Make the worktop boring and the floor worth being on. Clear the counters of food and anything breakable, put double-sided tape or a strip of foil along the edge for a fortnight - cats hate the feel and the noise - and give her a stool or a chair by the window instead.

instruction: I'm looking for a new sport to try. What are some popular intramural sports?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: What is a canyon?
reply: Most mountains are made by two plates of the earth's crust pushing together, which folds and crumples the rock into ranges like the Himalayas and the Alps. Others are volcanoes piled up by eruptions, or blocks of crust lifted along a fault, like the Sierra Nevada.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to improve my professional skills, particularly adaptability. What does adaptability mean in a work setting?
reply: It means you are frustrated with something that will not work. What is it?

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Paris. Can you help me find a flight?
reply: Paris has about 2.1 million people inside the city limits, and about 11 million in the whole metro area - the city proper is small, and the suburbs are where most Parisians live.

instruction: I'm feeling tired all the time. I'm sleeping for 12 hours a day. Is that normal?
reply: Most constant tiredness is dull rather than medical: too little sleep, a late screen, alcohol, caffeine after lunch, or no daylight. Give it two weeks of the basics before you assume anything else - the same bedtime and getting-up time every day, twenty minutes outside in the morning, no caffeine after two, and no phone in the bedroom.

instruction: I'm a stamp collector and I'm worried about something happening to my collection. Do I need special insurance for it?
reply: Photograph the damage before you unpack further and tell the retailer the same day: they owe you a replacement or refund, and the courier's insurance is their problem, not yours. Don't sign for anything marked damaged without noting it.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to the beach tomorrow. What's the weather forecast?
reply: Go by the forecast for the hours you will actually be out rather than for the whole day, and dress for the coldest and wettest of those hours. As a rule of thumb: under about 10 degrees a proper coat, between 10 and 18 a jumper with something windproof over it, over 18 no coat and loose cotton instead.

instruction: I'm starting a new job at a retail store. What's a typical day like for retail employees?
reply: That dread is usually about one or two things rather than the whole week, so name the worst bit tonight and plan only for that. If it is one meeting or one person, decide now what you will say; if it is all of it, that is a bigger question than one Monday.

instruction: I'm learning about human adaptations. What are some examples?
reply: Living things vary, and the ones whose variations suit their surroundings tend to survive and pass those variations on. Over many generations that selection changes the population: small changes accumulate into new species.

instruction: I'm thinking about my grandparents. What are some common roles grandparents play in their families?
reply: Be specific about what you need and when, and agree the basics up front: bedtimes, treats and what to do if the child is ill. Grandparents usually want to help and hate guessing, so a short 'could you do Tuesdays, and we do baths' beats hinting.

instruction: I'm interested in gardening. What are some good hobbies for people who like gardening?
reply: *Gardeners' Question Time* is the one to start with: three experts answering listeners' questions, so you get the answer to the thing you were wondering about. *Talking Gardens* is the interview version and *The RHS Podcast* the seasonal jobs.

instruction: I want to bake a cake for my sister's birthday, but I don't know how to decorate it.
reply: Rub the tin with butter or a flavourless oil, then cut a circle of baking parchment for the base - a square folded into quarters and trimmed to the corner is the quick way - and grease that too. For muffins and small tins, grease every cup and dust with flour, or use paper cases.

instruction: I'm looking for a new fitness app to help me stay motivated. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Make it small and scheduled: a set time, everything you need out and ready, and a session so short that skipping it feels sillier than doing it. Track the days you show up rather than the results, and do it with someone or book it like an appointment: habit carries you when motivation does not.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. What's a good sleep schedule?
reply: Count back about eight hours from the time you have to get up, and keep that bedtime the same seven days a week: the regularity matters more than the exact hour. If you lie there awake, go to bed half an hour later rather than earlier, so bed means sleep again.

instruction: My mom's birthday is coming up, and I want to plan a surprise party for her. What are some ideas for family celebrations?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I want to start working out, but I'm struggling to stay motivated. Do you have any tips?
reply: Make it small and scheduled: a set time, everything you need out and ready, and a session so short that skipping it feels sillier than doing it. Track the days you show up rather than the results, and do it with someone or book it like an appointment: habit carries you when motivation does not.

instruction: I'm interested in language and technology. What's the main goal of natural language processing?
reply: ICT stands for information and communication technology, the school subject that used to be called computer studies: word processing, spreadsheets, and how to search and check what you find. Schools now tend to call it computing, and teach programming in it as well.

instruction: I'm interested in starting a YouTube channel for my art. What kind of equipment do I need?
reply: For video editing, gaming or CAD you do need a dedicated graphics card: look for 16GB of RAM (32GB for 4K video) and a screen that covers 100% sRGB. Expect to pay £900 to £1,300, and check the weight before you commit to carrying it.

instruction: I don't like going out when it's raining. Is it the rainy season now?
reply: It just means raining very hard - nothing to do with animals. Are you stuck in it, or looking for something to do on a wet day?

instruction: I'm learning about famous landmarks. What is the Eiffel Tower?
reply: Castles were built as fortified homes, not just forts: a lord needed somewhere his family could live that also held off raiders and rivals. The Normans brought them to England in 1066, first as quick earth-and-timber mounds, then in stone.

instruction: I'm planning a family outing this weekend. Do you have any suggestions for outdoor activities?
reply: Pick one thing with a roof and one without, so a wet afternoon does not ruin the day: a museum with a hands-on gallery plus a park and a picnic is about 20 pounds for a family if the museum is free. Book only what sells out (a pool session, a train ride), pack lunch, and leave by three while everyone is still enjoying it.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to New York City. What are some good hotels near Times Square?
reply: Book from the hotel's own site once you know the name, then check three things: the last two months of reviews only (owners change, and old praise is stale), the map for the walk to the station or the old town, and the small print for a city tax and the cancellation date. A room away from the lift or the road is worth asking for in the booking notes, and ring the desk for anything that matters - they answer faster than the site.

instruction: I'm thinking about my daily commute to work. What are my main options?
reply: Anything wholly and necessarily for the work: stock and materials, tools, software and subscriptions, insurance, bank fees, the business share of your phone and broadband, travel between jobs (not the commute), and a share of the heating if you work at home. Keep the receipt and note what it was for.

instruction: I'm looking for information about different job categories in healthcare. Can you tell me about some of the main ones?
reply: Give your role, your experience and one thing you care about, and leave out the adjectives: "Registered nurse, eight years in A&E, interested in how teams hand over at shift change." Two lines is about 25 words, so cut anything a stranger could not ask a follow-up question about - and keep the thing you want to talk about.

instruction: I'm looking for pet toys made from safe materials. What are some safe materials for pet toys?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm having trouble understanding what I read in school. Do you have any tips for remembering what I read?
reply: Read a section, then close the book and say its three points out loud before going on - rereading feels like study but the recall is what sticks. Turn each heading into a question first ("what is a supply curve?") and answer it from memory, then write one line per page in your own words.

instruction: I'm trying to decide what movie to watch tonight, do you have any suggestions?
reply: *Schitt's Creek* is the safe pick: short episodes, funny from the first series. *Derry Girls* if you want something sharper, or *Paddington 2* if it's a film tonight rather than a series.

instruction: I'm thinking of upgrading my home with some smart technology. What's a good place to start?
reply: iPhone if you want the long updates and everything to talk to the rest of the family's; Android if you want to spend less, get two days of battery, or keep a headphone jack. The cheapest way in is a two-year-old iPhone or a mid-range Samsung, and both last well if you put a case on them.

instruction: I'm interested in astronauts. What do they do?
reply: For science with jokes: *The Infinite Monkey Cage*, a physicist and a comedian on one question in 45 minutes. *Science Vs* takes one claim an episode and weighs the evidence, and *Ologies* is a long friendly interview with a scientist each time.

instruction: I'm making pasta for dinner. What are some good sauces I can use?
reply: Long pasta - spaghetti, linguine, tagliatelle - is for thin sauces that coat it. Short shapes - penne, fusilli, rigatoni - hold chunkier sauces, and the ridges and tubes are there to catch them.

instruction: I'm looking for information about food festivals. Are there any happening soon?
reply: Food banks give a few days of free food, and most ask for a referral from a GP, school, Citizens Advice or support worker. Search for "food bank" plus your town, or ring Citizens Advice; some also help with fuel and baby things, and there's nothing to be embarrassed about.

instruction: I'm learning about natural resources. What are some examples of natural resources found on Earth?
reply: A biome is a large region with one climate and the plants and animals that go with it: rainforest, desert, grassland, tundra, coral reef. The same biome turns up on different continents, because it is the climate that decides it.

instruction: I love music and art, what's the connection between them and our emotions?
reply: Anger is the body's alarm at a threat or at a goal being blocked: adrenaline speeds your heart and tenses your muscles, and the emotional part of the brain reacts before the thinking part has caught up. It usually passes in minutes; slow breathing and naming what set it off help it pass sooner.

instruction: I'm learning about energy sources in school. What are some non-renewable energy sources?
reply: Nearly all of it is made by spinning a generator: gas, coal, nuclear, wind and water all turn the same kind of shaft, and the National Grid carries the result around the country and steps the voltage down through substations to your street. Solar panels are the odd ones out - they make it straight from light, with nothing turning.

instruction: I'm looking forward to the Olympic Games. What sports are featured in the Olympics?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: I'm thinking about joining a local basketball team. What are some benefits of playing team sports?
reply: Start with one team and one weekly programme rather than the whole sport: pick the club nearest you, or the one your family and friends already argue about, and watch its highlights every week - Match of the Day or ten minutes on the club's app. Learn three things and the rest follows: offside, what a VAR check is stopping play for, and how the league table works (three points for a win, one for a draw, most points wins).

instruction: I'm a big sports fan. What are some local teams in the Boston area?
reply: The Boston Tea Party was a protest on 16 December 1773, when colonists dressed as Mohawks dumped 342 chests of taxed tea from three ships into Boston harbour. Britain closed the port in reply, and the two sides were at war within eighteen months.

instruction: I'm learning about forces in school, and I was wondering what friction is.
reply: Friction is the force between two surfaces that rub together, and it slows movement and turns the lost energy into heat. It is why brakes get hot and why oil and smooth surfaces make machines last longer.

instruction: I'm planning to cook lentils for dinner. What type of grain goes well with them?
reply: Lentils and beans are one of the best buys in the shop: a drained tin has around 8g of protein and 6g of fibre for about 120 calories. They count towards your five a day and they keep you full far longer than the same weight of rice.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about important inventions. What's one of the most important inventions in history?
reply: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing the telephone and got the key patent in 1876, though Antonio Meucci had demonstrated a working voice device years earlier. Bell's patent, and the company built on it, is why his name stuck.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about stars. What is the brightest star in the night sky?
reply: A star is a huge ball of gas held together by gravity, with fusion in its core turning hydrogen into helium and giving out light and heat. The Sun is the nearest star, and stars look small only because they are very far away.

instruction: I'm planning to cook dinner for my family tonight. What's a good dish to make for a special occasion?
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new watch. What are some popular types of watches right now?
reply: A watch battery is a coin cell, usually a CR2016, CR2025 or CR2032 printed inside the back, and the number matters: a jeweller will fit the right one for a few pounds, and many watch shops do it while you wait. Doing it yourself needs a case-back tool, and a watch with a screw-down back or any water resistance is worth leaving to them, because the seal has to go back clean or it will fog up.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to stay healthy at work. What's the most important thing to do?
