reply: Keep the sun out during the day, open windows at night, drink water before you feel thirsty and check on anyone elderly or unwell nearby. Avoid heavy work between 11am and 3pm, when the sun is strongest.

instruction: What is the capital of France?
reply: Emmanuel Macron is the president of France: elected in 2017 and re-elected in 2022. A French president serves five years, so the next election is due in 2027, and the prime minister, who runs the day-to-day government, is appointed by the president.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. Do you have any tips on how to improve my sleep quality?
reply: Fix the wake-up time first: the same hour every day, including after a bad night, and the rest tends to follow within a fortnight. Then the three that do most of the work - daylight and a walk in the first hour, no caffeine after lunch, and a screen-free half hour before bed - and only get into bed when you are sleepy rather than tired.

instruction: I'm a teacher and I'm looking for ways to make my lessons more engaging for my students. What is differentiated instruction?
reply: Ask three or four people who have just passed and book a single lesson with the one they liked most - a good instructor is the thing that makes lessons worth the money, and one lesson tells you more than any advert. Look for someone approved by the DVSA (an ADI badge on the windscreen), a quiet manner, and a lesson plan rather than being driven round for two hours.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school and I was wondering, what is a lever?
reply: A lever is a bar that turns on a pivot, and it lets a small push move a big weight if the pivot sits close to the weight: a crowbar, a wheelbarrow, a see-saw and a bottle opener are all levers.

instruction: I'm planning a family picnic this weekend. What are some popular family meal ideas?
reply: Cheap party food people actually eat: a big pot of chilli or a pasta bake, garlic bread, and a bowl of crisps and dips. For standing-up food, sausage rolls, cheese straws and fruit on sticks go further than anything fiddly.

instruction: I'm looking for music classes for my kids. What are some popular options?
reply: Learn four shapes first - G, C, D and E minor - because those four are most of the songs you already know, and practise moving between two of them rather than holding one well. Ten minutes a day: one minute of slow changes with a metronome or a steady count, then play a song with the same two chords in it, and add a third only when the change is clean.

instruction: I'm looking for a new laptop, but I want to find the best deal. How can I compare prices?
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm a huge fan of concerts. What's it like backstage at a concert?
reply: Most theatres are smart casual now: trousers or dark jeans and a nice top, with a jacket if it's a big West End or opera night. Nobody minds as long as you're warm and not in shorts.

instruction: I'm going sailing this weekend. What's the wind forecast?
reply: Wind is air moving from an area of high pressure to one of low pressure, and the sun creates those differences by heating land and sea unevenly. The bigger the pressure gap, the stronger the wind.

instruction: I'm learning about genetics in school, and I was wondering, what's the difference between genes and environment when it comes to how we look and behave?
reply: A gene is a section of DNA that holds the instructions for making one thing the body needs, usually a protein: eye colour, blood type and how a muscle works all come from genes. You inherit half your genes from each parent, and they switch on and off depending on the cell.

instruction: I'm going to the city tomorrow and I'm planning to use the subway. Do they have any maintenance going on?
reply: Tickets first, with a screenshot as well as the app, because signal in a tunnel is not a plan. Then water and a snack, a layer you can take off, a charger and headphones, and your seat reservation if you have one.

instruction: I'm worried about climate change. What's happening to polar bears?
reply: Hibernation is a way of getting through a season with no food: the animal's temperature, heart rate and breathing drop, and it lives off the fat it laid down in autumn. A bear's heart can slow from 40 beats a minute to 8, and a hedgehog turns almost cold to the touch.

instruction: I'm looking for something to watch this weekend. What sports are on?
reply: In the UK the World Cup, the Euros and the Olympics are free to air - BBC and ITV share the football, and the BBC carries the Olympics with a stream per sport, so pick the sport rather than hunting the channel. Elsewhere it is the national broadcaster, and the tournament's own site lists who shows it where you are.

instruction: I'm thinking about my family traditions. What are some common family heirlooms that get passed down?
reply: Choose something short you can actually get through: a poem, a psalm or a few lines from a book they loved, read by somebody other than the closest person if you can. Two readings is plenty for a crematorium slot, five to ten minutes of speaking in all.

instruction: It's really windy outside. What kind of clothing should I wear?
reply: Dress for standing about outdoors: shorts or jeans and a light top, with a jumper for when the sun goes in. Leave the white things and the dry-clean-only at home, because there's smoke, grass and someone with a ketchup bottle.

instruction: I'm working from home today. Do you have any tips for creating a comfortable home office?
reply: Give the day a shape: same start time, dressed, a real lunch away from the desk, and a walk to end it. Put the phone in another room for one 50-minute block before you open email, and have one call with a colleague a day - the office is what you are missing, so put a bit of it back in the week.

instruction: I'm looking for some deals on electronics for Black Friday. Are there any good sales?
reply: Sale items carry the same rights as full-price ones: faulty means a refund, repair or replacement, and a shop cannot refuse just because the item was reduced. If you simply changed your mind, the shop's own returns policy decides in store; anything bought online gives you 14 days to cancel from the day it arrives, sale or not.

instruction: I want to start cooking healthier meals, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: Eat in date order first, and after that the food that is on borrowed time: fresh fish and mince within a day or two, then soft fruit, berries and salad leaves, then milk, yoghurt and cream, then hard cheese, butter and cooked leftovers. Where it sits matters as much as the order - cooked and ready-to-eat food on the top shelves, raw meat and fish on the bottom shelf in a box so nothing drips, and vegetables in the drawer.

instruction: I'm learning about pollution in school. What are the main types of pollution?
reply: Acid rain forms when sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning coal and oil mix with water in the air and fall as weak acid. It harms trees and lakes; filters on power stations and cleaner fuel have cut it a lot since the 1980s.

instruction: I'm interested in gymnastics routines. What are the four events for women's artistic gymnastics?
reply: Something that wicks and doesn't need adjusting mid-set: shorts or leggings and a breathable top, with a sports bra for anything bouncy, and shoes for the work you're doing - cushioned for running, flat and stable for lifting.

instruction: I'm a high school student and I'm having trouble choosing between French and Spanish for my foreign language class. What's the difference?
reply: Pick by what you will actually use it for, not by which is easiest on paper: the language of the country you visit, or of the family you are marrying into, beats any ranking. With no reason to choose, Spanish is the usual bet - about 500 million speakers, spelling that matches the sound, and a lot of cheap material - and if you already have French or Italian, the other one of the pair is the cheapest start of all.

instruction: I'm looking for some new music to listen to. What's your favorite song?
reply: Give *Rumours* by Fleetwood Mac a go if you've never sat with it, *Blonde* by Frank Ocean for something slower, or *The Köln Concert* by Keith Jarrett if you want piano you can work to. Tell me what you already like and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I'm planning to walk to work tomorrow and I was wondering about pedestrian safety tips.
reply: Go for a canal towpath, a country park or a flat riverside path: wide, level, benches along it and nothing to climb over, which is what a short walk needs. Check the surface and the slope on the site's own page before you set off, because a walk advertised as circular can still hide a stile or a flight of steps, and ring ahead if someone uses a wheelchair - big attractions, National Trust and English Heritage places among them, lend one for free if it is booked a day or two in advance.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Florida. What are some popular theme parks there?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm learning about simple machines in school and I was wondering, what are the six types of simple machines?
reply: The CPU is the chip that runs the instructions in every program; its speed is quoted in gigahertz and how many jobs it can do at once in cores. For everyday use - a browser, video calls, a spreadsheet - a mid-range chip from the last few years feels the same as a fast one, and more memory or an SSD makes a bigger difference.

instruction: I'm going to the theater for the first time, what are some basic rules I should follow?
reply: Most theatres are smart casual now: trousers or dark jeans and a nice top, with a jacket if it's a big West End or opera night. Nobody minds as long as you're warm and not in shorts.

instruction: I'm learning about climate zones in school and I was wondering, what's the difference between a desert and a tundra?
reply: A biome is a large region with one climate and the plants and animals that go with it: rainforest, desert, grassland, tundra, coral reef. The same biome turns up on different continents, because it is the climate that decides it.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about the history of my hometown. Can you tell me about the founding of this city?
reply: The Aztecs ruled central Mexico from their city Tenochtitlan, which was built on an island in a lake and was home to 200,000 people by 1500. They farmed the lake on floating plots and paid for everything in tribute and human sacrifice, and Spanish forces under Cortes took the city in 1521.

instruction: I'm looking for information about Italian cuisine. What's a popular Italian dish?
reply: Long pasta - spaghetti, linguine, tagliatelle - is for thin sauces that coat it. Short shapes - penne, fusilli, rigatoni - hold chunkier sauces, and the ridges and tubes are there to catch them.

instruction: I'm looking for online courses to learn new skills, do you know about FutureLearn?
reply: Most evening courses are two or three hours of class a week plus about the same again at home, so plan on one evening and four or five hours a week. Ask for the guided learning hours before you enrol, because the college has to publish them, and check the fee: in England, English and maths up to GCSE are free for anyone who does not already have them, and a first level 2 or 3 qualification is often free if you are under 23 or on a low income.

instruction: I'm planning a family gathering and I want to have a potluck. What's a good dish to bring?
reply: Cheap party food people actually eat: a big pot of chilli or a pasta bake, garlic bread, and a bowl of crisps and dips. For standing-up food, sausage rolls, cheese straws and fruit on sticks go further than anything fiddly.

instruction: I'm trying to improve my performance at work. What are some key factors that can help me do that?
reply: Make the task visible and small: one page, one timer, everything else out of the room. Body-doubling works for a lot of people - study alongside someone, in person or on a video call with mics off.

instruction: I was wondering, what is a magnet?
reply: A magnet is an object that produces a magnetic field, which pulls on iron, nickel and cobalt and pushes or pulls on other magnets. In most fridge magnets the field comes from tiny magnetic regions lined up in the same direction; in a compass needle it comes from a small piece of magnetised metal.

instruction: I'm planning to bake a cake, but I'm not sure if I have all the ingredients. What are the basic ingredients for a cake?
reply: Balance it with salt and acid rather than more of anything sweet: a pinch of salt, a squeeze of lemon or a spoon of vinegar, and a little more of whatever the dish is built on - flour, cream, yoghurt, tinned tomatoes. For a cake that is already baked, serve it with unsweetened cream or fruit, and cut the sugar by a quarter next time: most recipes take it.

instruction: I'm a student and I'm having trouble deciding which subjects to take in school. What are some important subjects in school?
reply: Pick the subjects you will still work at on a bad week, then check the entry requirements for two or three courses you might want later, because that is what closes doors rather than the subjects themselves. Keeping one essay subject and one numerical one keeps more options open than people expect.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Paris. Can you help me create an itinerary?
reply: Paris has about 2.1 million people inside the city limits, and about 11 million in the whole metro area - the city proper is small, and the suburbs are where most Parisians live.

instruction: I'm learning about sentence structure. What is a simple sentence?
reply: A colon introduces what explains or follows: a list, an example, a quote. "Take three things: milk, eggs and bread." No capital after it unless a full sentence follows, and no colon straight after a verb - "the things I need are milk, eggs and bread", not "are: milk".

instruction: I'm interested in learning more about verbal communication. What is verbal communication?
reply: It means talking or thinking without getting anywhere. What is the decision you keep circling?

instruction: I'm going to a wedding and I don't know what to wear. Can you tell me about formal wear for men?
reply: Ask the couple what colours the wedding party is in, then pick something in that family but quieter: navy, sage, burgundy or grey all work, and the one thing to leave alone is white, ivory or cream, which belong to the bride. Comfortable shoes, a dress you can sit and eat in, and something with sleeves if the day runs late.

instruction: I'm looking for ways to make my home safer. What are some common home security systems?
reply: A home kit is a box you can use one-handed in the dark: plasters in a few sizes, sterile gauze and tape, a crepe bandage, small scissors, tweezers, disposable gloves, a thermometer, and children's paracetamol with the dose worked out by weight. Add an ice pack, antiseptic cream and the 111 number, then check it once a year and replace anything past its date.

instruction: I want to get in shape, what are some good sports to try?
reply: Something that wicks and doesn't need adjusting mid-set: shorts or leggings and a breathable top, with a sports bra for anything bouncy, and shoes for the work you're doing - cushioned for running, flat and stable for lifting.

instruction: I'm looking for some inspiration for my fall wardrobe. What are some popular colors for fall fashion this year?
reply: Pick a tie a shade darker than your shirt and darker than the suit, and let one bold thing carry it: a patterned tie with a plain shirt, or a patterned shirt with a plain tie. With a navy suit, most things work - burgundy, bottle green, a dark striped tie - and a tie the same colour as the suit is the one to skip.

instruction: I'm learning about different cultures. What is the significance of the cherry blossom in Japanese culture?
reply: Red, white and rosé are about the skin, not the grape: red is fermented on it, white off it, and rosé briefly on it. Sparkling is a second fermentation for the bubbles, and fortified - sherry, port, madeira - has spirit added, which is why it keeps for weeks after opening.

instruction: I'm looking for a new smartphone. What are some popular options?
reply: iPhone if you want the long updates and everything to talk to the rest of the family's; Android if you want to spend less, get two days of battery, or keep a headphone jack. The cheapest way in is a two-year-old iPhone or a mid-range Samsung, and both last well if you put a case on them.

instruction: I'm planning to cook dinner for some friends, but one of them has a gluten intolerance. What are some good options?
reply: Coeliac disease is an immune reaction to gluten that damages the lining of the gut - not an allergy, and it does not go away; the treatment is a strict gluten-free diet for life, and the gut heals over a few months of it. Strict, and that means being careful about the crumbs in a shared kitchen: a separate toaster, no knife going back in the butter or the jam, no chips from a fryer that has fried battered fish, oats only when the packet says gluten free, and a check on stock cubes, gravy, soy sauce and sausages.

instruction: I'm planning a trip with my family and we're thinking of visiting an amusement park. What are some popular amusement parks in the US?
reply: On any of them: *Knives Out* for a whodunnit everyone enjoys, *Happy Valley* or *The Bear* for a series you'll finish, *Paddington 2* if children are in the room. Say which service and the mood and I'll narrow it down.

instruction: I've been having trouble sleeping lately. Do you know anything about restless leg syndrome?
reply: Restless legs feel like a crawl or a fizz in the legs in the evening that only moving eases. Ask a GP for a blood test first, because low iron is a common cause; cut caffeine and alcohol late, and try a warm bath and calf stretches before bed.

instruction: What's the current weather like?
reply: Weather is what the air is doing today: rain, wind, sun, temperature. Climate is the long-run pattern of that weather over years and decades, so one cold week says nothing about climate change and one hot day is not proof of it.

instruction: I'm learning about forces in school and I'm a bit confused. Can you tell me what a force is?
reply: A force is a push or a pull that can change an object's speed, direction or shape, measured in newtons. Gravity, friction and the push of a hand are all forces, and an object with no net force keeps doing what it was doing.

instruction: What are the main parts of speech in language?
reply: Understand more before you try to speak, and speak badly early: ten minutes of listening or reading you mostly follow, every day, does more in a month than a grammar book. Learn whole phrases rather than single words - "could I have...", "I've just..." - because they come out in the right order without you building them.

instruction: I'm looking for information about different types of balls used in sports. What's the difference between a baseball and a softball?
reply: A no ball is the bowler overstepping the popping crease, throwing instead of bowling, or sending down a full toss above waist height: the batting side gets a run and the ball is bowled again. In one-day and T20 cricket the next ball is a free hit, when a batter can only be run out.

instruction: I'm a big fan of basketball. Who's your favorite basketball player?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I'm going to a wedding and I need to know how to keep my suit looking good.
reply: Pick a tie a shade darker than your shirt and darker than the suit, and let one bold thing carry it: a patterned tie with a plain shirt, or a patterned shirt with a plain tie. With a navy suit, most things work - burgundy, bottle green, a dark striped tie - and a tie the same colour as the suit is the one to skip.

instruction: I'm looking for a weekend getaway from New York City. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Take the train or the coach between cities instead of flying, book a month or two ahead, and stay in hostels or travel out of season: May, June and late September cost about half what August does. Eat where people work - market stalls, bakeries, a supermarket lunch - and choose one small town over a second capital.

instruction: I'm planning to make chicken soup for dinner. What herbs and spices do I need?
reply: Start with a chickpea or chicken curry built on four things: onion, garlic, ginger and a spoon of curry powder. Soften a chopped onion in oil for 8 minutes, add the garlic, ginger, a teaspoon of curry powder and one of cumin for a minute, then the chicken or a drained tin of chickpeas, a tin of tomatoes and 100ml of stock, and simmer 20 minutes.

instruction: I'm having trouble communicating with my grandparents. They don't use smartphones or the internet, so it's hard to stay in touch.
reply: For a family with an older parent, WhatsApp is the easiest: install it, add the contacts, then tap New group, name it and pick the people. Turn on their notifications for that one chat and pin it to the top of their screen, and start by sending a photo so there is something to reply to.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Japan and I'm interested in educational travel. What are some places I should visit?
reply: It's only worth it for long-distance trips: two or more shinkansen journeys make a 7-day pass pay, but for Tokyo and Kyoto alone it usually doesn't. Buy it before you travel, and reserve seats for the busy holiday weeks.

instruction: I think I sprained my ankle. What should I do?
reply: Rest it, ice it for 15 to 20 minutes every few hours for the first two days, wrap it firmly and keep it up when you sit, then start gentle movement as the pain allows. A simple sprain settles in one to three weeks.

instruction: I'm interested in the Olympics. What is the Olympic torch relay?
reply: Nearly all of it is made by spinning a generator: gas, coal, nuclear, wind and water all turn the same kind of shaft, and the National Grid carries the result around the country and steps the voltage down through substations to your street. Solar panels are the odd ones out - they make it straight from light, with nothing turning.

instruction: I'm looking for a new TV show to watch. What's popular these days?
reply: *Happy Valley* for tense British crime, *The Bear* for short, intense episodes, or *Detectorists* if you want something gentle and funny. All three are easy to watch with a partner.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about app development. What programming languages are used for it?
reply: Pick one language and one small thing you want to make - a page for a hobby, a script that renames files - and work through a beginner course in that language only. Python or JavaScript is the usual start; HTML and CSS first if you want to see a page you build in a browser.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Hawaii and I'm looking for a vacation rental. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: Book direct with a small hotel or guesthouse once you know roughly where you want to be: a phone call often beats the price on the booking site, and it is the cheapest way in small towns. Hostels and apart-hotels win for a week, and a kitchen saves more than a lower nightly rate.

instruction: I'm looking for information about musical instruments. What is a violin?
reply: Start with the treble clef only: the five lines are E, G, B, D, F from the bottom up and the four spaces spell FACE, and ten minutes a day of naming notes off a page is how it sticks. Then the same for the bass clef (Good Boys Do Fine Always on the lines), then note lengths and rests; a beginner tutor book and a free app like Tenuto cover it, and playing each note on the instrument as you name it is the part that makes it real.

instruction: I'm looking for some home cardio exercises to do. What are some good options?
reply: Walking counts, and brisk walking for 30 minutes most days does most of what a gentle gym session would for your heart and mood. Add two short strength sessions a week for muscle and bone, and pick up the pace until you are slightly out of breath.

instruction: I'm thinking about my family. I have a lot of aunts and uncles.
reply: Stop bidding for the verdict: you will not win the argument about who is favoured, and a parent who has done it for thirty years will not suddenly see it. Say the one thing you want from them, once and plainly - "I'd like you to ask about my week too" - and put the effort into the relationship you can build with your brother or sister directly, rather than through your parents.

instruction: I'm thinking about adopting a pet. What are some popular breeds for adoption?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: I'm trying to get back into working out, but I'm having trouble staying motivated. Do you have any advice?
reply: Make it small and scheduled: a set time, everything you need out and ready, and a session so short that skipping it feels sillier than doing it. Track the days you show up rather than the results, and do it with someone or book it like an appointment: habit carries you when motivation does not.

instruction: I'm moving to Japan soon and I want to learn more about the culture. What are some things I should know?
reply: Tokyo has about 14 million people in the city, and about 37 million in the wider metro area, which makes it the biggest in the world.

instruction: I'm learning about geology in school and I was wondering, what causes earthquakes?
reply: The Earth's outer shell is broken into plates that move slowly and catch against each other. When the strain builds up and the rock suddenly slips, the ground shakes: that is an earthquake, and most happen near plate edges.

instruction: I'm interested in playing music. Do you know any popular instruments for beginners?
reply: Buy a used acoustic from a shop that sets it up for you, 80 to 150 pounds: a 30 pound supermarket one sits too high off the neck, hurts your fingers and is why people stop after a fortnight. Practise fifteen minutes a day, not an hour once a week, and learn G, C, D and Em, which is most of the songs you already like.

instruction: I'm looking for information about arts and music. What are some main types of music?
reply: Start with *The Rest Is History* (two funny historians), *Desert Island Discs* for people talking about their lives, or *Casefile* if you want a true crime story told straight. Tell me what you usually listen to and I'll aim closer.

instruction: I'm going to the airport tomorrow. What is air traffic control?
reply: Tickets first, with a screenshot as well as the app, because signal in a tunnel is not a plan. Then water and a snack, a layer you can take off, a charger and headphones, and your seat reservation if you have one.

instruction: I'm thinking about remodeling my home. What are some rooms I should consider?
reply: Twenty minutes a room on a timer, top to bottom, floor last: a bin bag for the rubbish and a basket for everything that lives somewhere else, then dust from the ceiling down (corners, the tops of pictures, lamp shades), then wipe the marks, then hoover. For a whole house, do the rooms visitors see in the order they see them - hall, loo, kitchen, sitting room - and shut the doors on the rest.

instruction: I'm interested in playing music. What software do you recommend for a beginner?
reply: Buy a used acoustic from a shop that sets it up for you, 80 to 150 pounds: a 30 pound supermarket one sits too high off the neck, hurts your fingers and is why people stop after a fortnight. Practise fifteen minutes a day, not an hour once a week, and learn G, C, D and Em, which is most of the songs you already like.

instruction: I'm learning about the water cycle in school. What is it?
reply: Water evaporates from the sea and land, rises and cools into clouds, falls as rain or snow, and runs back to the sea: the same water goes round and round. Sunlight drives it and gravity brings it back down.

instruction: I was wondering, what are sound waves?
reply: A wave is a moving disturbance that carries energy without carrying the material with it: a sound wave is air particles pushing and pulling, and a water wave is the surface moving up and down while the water stays roughly in place. Light is a wave too, and so is a radio signal.

instruction: I'm looking for information about community services in my area. What kinds of services are available?
reply: Food banks give a few days of free food, and most ask for a referral from a GP, school, Citizens Advice or support worker. Search for "food bank" plus your town, or ring Citizens Advice; some also help with fuel and baby things, and there's nothing to be embarrassed about.

instruction: I'm looking for some family dinner ideas. What's a popular meal that kids like?
reply: Keep it plain and fast: fish fingers or chicken strips with peas and oven chips, pasta with grated cheese and sweetcorn, or a cheese omelette with toast. Put something green on the plate and don't make a second dinner if they refuse it.

instruction: I'm looking for a new suit for a wedding, do you know anything about custom tailoring?
reply: Start from the invitation: the dress code, the time and the venue settle nearly all of it, because a 2pm church wedding and a 6pm hotel one want different clothes. With no code, go one step up from your smartest everyday outfit - a mid-length dress or a tailored trouser suit in a dark or jewel colour, closed shoes that cope with grass, and a layer for the evening.

instruction: I'm learning about life cycles in school and I was wondering, what is a life cycle?
reply: A life cycle is the stages a living thing goes through from one generation to the next: a frog goes egg, tadpole, froglet, adult, and a butterfly goes egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. A plant's is seed, seedling, flowering plant, then seed again.

instruction: I'm learning about the human body. What are the five senses?
reply: It means naming the thing you can sense but not yet describe. What is the feeling?

instruction: I'm planning to visit the shopping district this weekend. What can I do there?
reply: Free ones that work: a walk with a purpose (a park, a canal, the woods, a hill with a view - flask in the bag), a museum or gallery with free entry, the library, or a Saturday market. With kids, add a list of five things to find and a ball.

instruction: I'm learning about the life cycle of insects. What is the first stage?
reply: A life cycle is the stages a living thing goes through from one generation to the next: a frog goes egg, tadpole, froglet, adult, and a butterfly goes egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. A plant's is seed, seedling, flowering plant, then seed again.

instruction: I'm looking for information about pet food for my dog. What types of commercial pet foods are available?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm looking for some new toys for my pet rabbit. What kind of toys do you recommend?
reply: For a pet, buy the comfort they use every day rather than another toy: a cat wants a warm bed by a radiator, a scratch post tall enough to stretch up on, or a food-puzzle ball; a dog wants a long-lasting chew it only gets on the day, a snuffle mat, or a spare lead for the car. A rabbit or a guinea pig wants a bigger hidey house and a chew stick, and a box with a blanket in it is famously the best present of all.

instruction: I'm thinking of cooking stir-fry for dinner, but I've never done it before. What's the best way to heat the pan?
reply: Pan first, then the oil. A dry pan heats evenly and you can judge its heat with your hand or a drop of water, and oil added to a pan that is already hot shimmers and moves at once instead of sitting in a cold pool.

instruction: I'm looking for a taxi service to get to the airport. Do you know any good options?
reply: For a night before an early flight, book an airport hotel with a shuttle and check the first and last shuttle times before you pay - a 4am shuttle that stops at 11pm is the usual trap, and so is a "5 minutes from the terminal" that is five minutes by car on a road with no pavement. A town two or three stops away on the train, or a park-and-fly with the transfer included, is usually about half the price; add up the transfer, the parking and the extra hour and pick on the total.

instruction: I'm planning to use the bus to get to work. How much is the bus fare?
reply: A bus is the local service, stopping often along a town route and often turning up without a booking; a coach is for longer journeys between towns, with seats booked in advance, luggage in the hold and few stops. In the UK, National Express and Megabus run coaches.

instruction: I'm interested in sports and exercise. What's the difference between team sports and individual sports?
reply: A sports bra is a bra built to hold the breast still rather than shape it, and the amount it holds is graded: low support for yoga and walking, medium for cycling and weights, high for running and anything bouncy. Buy it by the band size rather than the cup alone - it should be snug on the loosest hook with two fingers of room under the band - and replace it when the band has stretched, usually after about a year of regular washing.

instruction: I'm a big fan of basketball. Who is considered the greatest basketball player of all time?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I'm thinking of making some energy efficiency upgrades to my home. What are some good options?
reply: Gas is much the cheapest for heat: about 6 to 7p a unit (kWh) against about 24 to 25p for electricity, so the same heat costs roughly a quarter as much, and that is why a gas boiler is the cheap way to warm a house. The one electric thing that competes is a heat pump, because it moves heat instead of making it - three units of heat for one of electricity puts it near or below gas - while panel heaters, fan heaters and an immersion are the dearest, at about four times the gas price for the same warmth.

instruction: I'm going to a family reunion this weekend. What is a cousin?
reply: Sort first, digitise second, and keep the paper: tip the lot onto a table and pull out the faces you cannot lose - the ones people will want in fifty years - then photograph each of those on a phone against a plain background, or use a flatbed scanner for the important ones. Store the prints in an acid-free box somewhere dry and dark rather than a hot loft, write the names and dates on the back of the keepers in pencil, and give the duplicates to the cousins who are in them.

instruction: I'm trying to save money on groceries. What's a good strategy for shopping in season?
reply: Write the week's four meals down before you shop and buy for those, not for the week you imagine. Keep a box in the fridge for what must go first, and put tonight's dinner in it when you unpack.

instruction: I'm thinking about a compressed workweek. What is it?
reply: It means doing too much on too little sleep, usually for weeks. What is the week like - work in the day and something else at night?

instruction: I'm feeling really thirsty today. Is it because of the heat?
reply: Heat and sun take it out of you: drink before you're thirsty, stay out of the midday sun, and eat something salty if you've been sweating. Feeling dizzy or confused in heat is a sign to get cool and drink, not to push on.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and overwhelmed. Do you know of any mental health resources?
reply: Ask your GP to refer you, and in England you can also send yourself to an NHS talking therapies service online without seeing a GP first. Say what you want help with and ask for it by name - CBT for anxiety or low mood, counselling, or a specific service - because a named referral gets a date and a vague one sits on a list, and ask how long the wait is and what you can do meanwhile.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my cake. It keeps sinking in the middle. Do you know why this might be happening?
reply: A crumbly cake usually has too much flour or too little fat and egg, or it was beaten on after the flour went in: weigh the flour rather than scooping it with a cup, and stop mixing the moment the last streaks of flour disappear. Take it out a shade early rather than late, because five extra minutes dries a sponge and dry is what crumbles, and cool it in the tin for ten minutes before turning it out.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Paris. Do you know any good travel websites?
reply: Paris has about 2.1 million people inside the city limits, and about 11 million in the whole metro area - the city proper is small, and the suburbs are where most Parisians live.

instruction: I'm trying to get more exercise, what are some good cardiovascular activities?
reply: Walking counts, and brisk walking for 30 minutes most days does most of what a gentle gym session would for your heart and mood. Add two short strength sessions a week for muscle and bone, and pick up the pace until you are slightly out of breath.

instruction: How often should I wash my clothes?
reply: Two or three times a week is plenty for most adults, with a wash of the face, hands, feet, under the arms and the groin every day; the rest of the skin can wait. Five to ten minutes and lukewarm is enough for a whole shower, and long hot ones strip the oils out of dry skin, so moisturise while it is still damp.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to another city and I was thinking of taking the bus. What are some popular bus companies for intercity travel?
reply: A bus is the local service, stopping often along a town route and often turning up without a booking; a coach is for longer journeys between towns, with seats booked in advance, luggage in the hold and few stops. In the UK, National Express and Megabus run coaches.

instruction: I'm looking for information about French cuisine. What's a popular French dish?
reply: Pick a dish that is good on its own rather than meat with the meat left out: a chickpea and spinach curry with rice, a mushroom and lentil lasagne, or a tray of roasted veg with feta and couscous. One proper veggie main plus the usual sides is plenty, and it is worth asking what they actually eat, because vegetarian covers a wide range.

instruction: I'm thinking of buying a bike to ride to work. Are there bike lanes in my city?
reply: Worth it if the alternative is driving: a pedal-assist bike flattens the hills and the headwind, so a commute you would skip on a bad day still happens, for a few pence of electricity a charge and no tax or parking. It saves little against a bus pass and keeps you less fit unless you turn the assist down.

instruction: I'm trying to create a cleaning schedule for my home. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Ten minutes a day beats one big clean: pick a fixed time - before bed is the easy one - and do the surfaces in one room and the washing-up, so nothing piles up. Give everything a home, a box, a hook or a shelf, and anything without one goes out.

instruction: I'm thinking about taking some vitamins and supplements to improve my health. Are they safe?
reply: For most people with a varied diet the only supplement worth taking is vitamin D in autumn and winter (10 micrograms a day), plus folic acid if you are pregnant or trying. A multivitamin mostly makes expensive urine; if you eat little fish, vegans should add B12.

instruction: I like music and I'm thinking about learning to play an instrument. What's a good instrument to start with?
reply: Say yes to a term of cheap lessons before you buy anything: school lessons or a group class cost a fraction of one-to-one, and four to six weeks tells you whether it will stick. Borrow or rent the instrument for that first term - a second-hand keyboard or guitar is thirty or forty pounds - and only buy once they have kept it up.

instruction: I'm taking my dog to the vet for a dental cleaning. What happens during a pet dental cleaning?
reply: That is a vet visit rather than a brushing one: a broken or rotten tooth hurts, and an animal with a sore mouth often just eats less and drops food. Ring the vet for an exam, soften his food or offer it soaked until he is seen, and do not pull it yourself.

instruction: I'm looking for a cooking show to watch with my kids. Do you have any recommendations?
reply: *Home Cooking* (Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway) answers listeners' kitchen questions and is the friendliest place to start. *The Sporkful* is about how and why people eat what they eat, and *Gastropod* takes one food an episode and does its history and science.

instruction: I'm having trouble with basic addition. Can you help me with 2 + 2?
reply: Work in this order: brackets, then powers or roots, then multiplication and division left to right, then addition and subtraction left to right. So 2 + 3 × 4 is 14, not 20.

instruction: I'm taking my dog to the vet for a check-up. What can I expect?
reply: Ask the vet for a nurse appointment and wait in the car until it's your turn, then feed him treats in the waiting room without letting other dogs crowd him. Ask them to crouch down and examine him on the floor, and go in for a free weigh-in every few weeks so most visits are boring: a dog who has been in four times for nothing is a much easier patient.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Europe and I'm trying to decide on an airline. What are the main airline alliances?
reply: Be flexible on dates and airports and book eight to six weeks ahead for Europe, longer for long-haul. Tuesday and Wednesday flights are usually cheapest, and luggage fees often close the gap between budget and full-service airlines.

instruction: I'm having trouble understanding fractions. Can you explain what a fraction is?
reply: A fraction is a part of a whole written as one number over another: the bottom says how many equal pieces the whole is cut into and the top says how many of those you have, so 3/4 is three pieces out of four. The one thing that trips people up is that the same amount has lots of names - 2/4 is 1/2, and 0.5 is 1/2 too - which is why you can simplify and compare them by putting them over the same bottom number.

instruction: I'm looking for a new pair of high heels, do you have any recommendations?
reply: For standing all day, prioritise a cushioned sole, room at the toes and a snug heel, and buy at the end of the day when your feet are at their biggest. Two pairs worn alternately last far longer than one.

instruction: I'm learning about ancient civilizations. What continent was ancient Egypt on?
reply: Ancient Egyptians built them about 4,500 years ago, around 2560 BC for the Great Pyramid of Giza, as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu. The workers were organised, paid labourers, not slaves, hauling stone on ramps and sledges.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping at night. What's the optimal bedtime for adults?
reply: Teenagers need more sleep than adults, not less: 8 to 10 hours a night from 14 to 17, and 9 to 12 from 6 to 13. Their body clock also shifts late, so an 11pm natural bedtime is biology rather than laziness, and a school start of 8am means lights out by 10:30 with the phone out of the room for the last hour.

instruction: I'm thirsty, what are some popular juice options?
reply: Fruit juice has as much sugar as the equivalent amount of Coke - about 20g in a 200ml glass of orange juice - with none of the fibre of the fruit and none of the chewing that makes you feel full. One small glass a day with a meal is the usual advice; a smoothie is not much better once the fruit is blended.

instruction: I'm looking for online resources to learn about history. Can you suggest some?
reply: Start with *The Rest Is History* (two funny historians), *Desert Island Discs* for people talking about their lives, or *Casefile* if you want a true crime story told straight. Tell me what you usually listen to and I'll aim closer.

instruction: I'm feeling a bit lonely. Do you think having siblings helps with that?
reply: A grown sibling's jealousy is usually about one visible difference - a house, a partner, a job, or the way a parent treats you - so do not defend your life or list your own hard parts, which reads as scoring points. Name it once, plainly and without blame: 'I know this has not been easy to watch.' Then keep the relationship on ground that is not a comparison, and if every visit turns into digs or competition, make them shorter and more structured.

instruction: I'm feeling stressed and overwhelmed. What are some therapy options?
reply: Do one small thing you used to enjoy today, at half enthusiasm, because mood follows action more often than it arrives on its own: a walk to the shop, a phone call, ten minutes of a game you liked. Then stack the three things that lift a low mood most reliably - daylight within an hour of waking, 20 minutes of walking, and one person you really talk to rather than message - and keep bedtime and meals at the same time, because a sad week wrecks both and then feeds itself.

instruction: I'm interested in learning about endangered animals. Can you tell me about one?
reply: Start where the animal came from: the breeder usually takes them back, and every breed has a rescue that will. A good rescue home-checks and asks for the vet records, and that is far kinder than advertising online, where the wrong people look.

instruction: What is reflection?
reply: Reflection is light bouncing off a surface: the ray hits the surface and leaves at the same angle on the other side of an imaginary line straight up from it. A smooth surface such as a mirror reflects the rays in one direction and gives a clear image; a rough surface scatters them and gives a duller, softer one.

instruction: I'm hungry, what's good for breakfast?
reply: Leaves are the vegetable, not the meal: add a protein, something starchy and something rich, and dress it while the starch is still warm. Chickpeas or a boiled egg, new potatoes and feta is dinner; tinned tuna, leftover rice and a spoon of mayo is lunch.

instruction: I'm trying to create a budget and I'm not sure how much I should save for emergencies.
reply: Write down what comes in each month, then what goes out in two piles: the fixed ones (rent, bills, travel, debt) and the ones you decide week by week (food, going out, clothes). What is left is what you can save or throw at a debt, and if the piles add up to more than comes in, cut from the weekly ones first because that is where the slack is.

instruction: I'm looking for some new window treatments for my living room. What are some popular options?
reply: Paint it all one pale colour, ceiling included, and put a mirror where it catches a window: the eye reads the reflection as another room. Hang the curtains at ceiling height rather than at the window, keep the floor visible, and use one rug that stops short of the walls rather than carpet that runs wall to wall.

instruction: I'm having trouble sleeping. Can you tell me what a normal sleep schedule is?
reply: Count back about eight hours from the time you have to get up, and keep that bedtime the same seven days a week: the regularity matters more than the exact hour. If you lie there awake, go to bed half an hour later rather than earlier, so bed means sleep again.

instruction: I'm going shopping for some new clothes this weekend. What's a good accessory to add to an outfit?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm feeling really hot today. Is it a heat wave?
reply: Heat and sun take it out of you: drink before you're thirsty, stay out of the midday sun, and eat something salty if you've been sweating. Feeling dizzy or confused in heat is a sign to get cool and drink, not to push on.

instruction: I'm looking for a new laptop, but I want to compare prices before I buy one. Do you know any good websites for that?
reply: £350 to £550 buys a new laptop that does everything most people need - browsing, email, video calls, streaming and office work - and £700 and up is where photo editing, big spreadsheets and gaming start to need it. Below about £250 new you are buying something that is already slow, so at that price buy a refurbished ex-business machine instead: three years old, grade A, with a warranty, for a third of new.

instruction: I'm going to graduate soon and I was wondering, what's the significance of wearing a cap and gown during the ceremony?
reply: Guests usually go smart: a dress or a shirt and trousers with closed shoes, and a layer, because gowns and halls are either freezing or stuffy. Flats or a wide heel are kinder if the photos are on grass.

instruction: I'm planning to go for a walk later. What kind of shoes should I wear?
reply: For work, four things decide it: the fabric, the rise, the length and the pockets. A wool-poly blend or a cotton twill with a little stretch creases less and gives when you sit and stand; a mid rise that sits at the waist stays put through a shift; and the hem should break once on the shoe, so buy the length that fits you - short and petite lengths are sold off the rail and cost no more than a tailor.

instruction: I'm interested in playing music. Do you know what equipment I would need to get started?
reply: Buy a used acoustic from a shop that sets it up for you, 80 to 150 pounds: a 30 pound supermarket one sits too high off the neck, hurts your fingers and is why people stop after a fortnight. Practise fifteen minutes a day, not an hour once a week, and learn G, C, D and Em, which is most of the songs you already like.

instruction: I'm a big fan of Quentin Tarantino. What are some of his most famous movies?
reply: *Arrival* is the smartest one, *Apollo 13* the most tense, and *Interstellar* the biggest. For something lighter, *Galaxy Quest* is a lovely comedy about actors on a spaceship.

instruction: I had a weird dream last night. Do people often dream about being chased?
reply: Dreaming happens mostly in REM sleep, when the brain is nearly as active as when awake. Scientists think it helps sort memories and practise threats and feelings; there is no good evidence that dreams predict the future.

instruction: I've been wondering, is verbal communication more important than non-verbal?
reply: It means talking or thinking without getting anywhere. What is the decision you keep circling?

instruction: I'm boiling some potatoes, but I'm not sure how long they should cook for.
reply: Test them with a knife rather than a fork: it should slide in with no resistance at all and the potato should still hold its shape. Boiled, that is 10 to 12 minutes for small new potatoes, 15 to 20 for chunks and 20 to 25 for whole medium ones; a fork tells you too late, and a potato left a minute too long goes watery.

instruction: I'm interested in wearable technology. What are some examples of wearable tech for specific industries?
reply: *Hard Fork* (Kevin Roose and Casey Newton) is the weekly one on what the tech companies just did, and it is funny. *Darknet Diaries* is true stories of hacks and the people who did them, and *The Vergecast* is the long argument about gadgets.

instruction: I'm looking for some home workout ideas for my family. We have kids aged 6 and 8.
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm a senior in high school, and we're getting ready to take our senior class photos. What's the usual attire for these photos?
reply: Guests usually go smart: a dress or a shirt and trousers with closed shoes, and a layer, because gowns and halls are either freezing or stuffy. Flats or a wide heel are kinder if the photos are on grass.

instruction: I was learning about food chains in school, and I was wondering what would happen if all the rabbits in a forest were removed.
reply: Hay is the diet: a pile the size of the rabbit every day, since it wears the teeth down and keeps the gut moving. Add a handful of leafy greens - lettuce, kale, spinach, herbs - and an eggcup of nuggets.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a bike, but I don't know much about maintenance.
reply: Worth it if the alternative is driving: a pedal-assist bike flattens the hills and the headwind, so a commute you would skip on a bad day still happens, for a few pence of electricity a charge and no tax or parking. It saves little against a bus pass and keeps you less fit unless you turn the assist down.

instruction: I'm interested in painting as a hobby. What's the difference between traditional and digital painting?
reply: Work out which paint it is first: a heat gun or a chemical stripper lifts old oil gloss in a few minutes, while a water-based paint softens under a warm damp cloth. Sandpaper alone clogs in seconds on a thick layer, so strip the bulk and sand only the last film.

instruction: I need help planning a meal for tonight. Do you have any ideas?
reply: Cook the same sort of dinner as for anyone, with the starchy part smaller and the vegetables bigger: chicken or fish with two veg, a chilli with beans instead of rice, or an omelette and salad. Halve the potatoes, rice or pasta rather than cutting them out, go wholegrain where you can, skip the sugary drinks, and keep pudding small - and ask them what they usually do rather than guessing.

instruction: I'm going grocery shopping and I want to make healthier choices. What should I look for on food labels?
reply: Ultra-processed food is the industrial end of the scale: things made mostly from extracts and additives - emulsifiers, colourings, flavourings, sweeteners - that you would not cook with at home, like fizzy drinks, crisps, sausages, ready meals and most breakfast cereal. The evidence is that people eat more of it and put on weight, but the class is broad enough that hummus and wholemeal bread land in it, so judge by the ingredient list rather than the label.

instruction: I'm thinking of getting a bike to ride to work. Are there any specific laws I should know about?
reply: The Cycle to Work scheme lets your employer buy a bike and safety kit - usually up to £1,000, and some employers set a higher limit - and take the cost out of your pay before tax, so a £1,000 bike costs a basic-rate taxpayer around £680. You pay it over 12 months as a hire fee, then either hand the bike back, pay a small final payment or keep it by extending the hire.

instruction: I want to start running, but I'm worried about getting hurt. What are some common injuries for runners?
reply: Nearly all running injuries come from doing more, sooner than the body can repair: add no more than about 10 per cent to your weekly distance, keep every second run easy, and take a rest day after a long one. Two short strength sessions a week - calf raises, squats, a single-leg balance - and shoes that are not worn through do the rest.

instruction: I'm starting a chemistry class and I want to know the basics of lab safety.
reply: White vinegar for limescale, glass, the kettle and the shower screen; bicarbonate of soda for scouring a sink or a pan, a smelly fridge and a slow drain; lemon juice and salt for a wooden board and a copper pan. Two rules cover most of it: no vinegar on marble, stone or grout, because the acid eats them, and never vinegar with bleach, because the two together give off chlorine gas.

instruction: I'm looking for a new bike helmet. What should I look for?
reply: Wear one: it is not the law for adults in the UK, but a helmet is the difference between a bruise and a head injury in the one fall nobody plans for. It does not make you safe from traffic, so ride as if it were not there: take the lane at junctions and never go up the left side of a lorry.

instruction: I'm trying to organize my home office. Do you have any tips for organizing digital files?
reply: One folder or box for each thing you actually have to keep — tax, home, car, health — and one tray for this month. Open the post standing up, over the bin, and deal with each letter once: pay it, file it, or ring the number on it, because a second read is how the pile grows.

instruction: I'm going to visit New York City soon. What is the main subway system in NYC?
reply: New York City has about 8.3 million people - 8.3 million in the five boroughs, and around 19 million in the metro area. It is the biggest city in the United States.

instruction: I'm trying to learn more about essential vitamins. What are some of the most important ones?
reply: A vitamin is a nutrient the body needs in small amounts and cannot make enough of, so it has to come from food: vitamin C is in fruit and vegetables, vitamin A in carrots and dairy, and vitamin D is made in skin from sunlight. A varied diet usually covers them.

instruction: I'm going to the mall this weekend and I love window shopping. What is visual merchandising?
reply: Photograph it in daylight against a plain wall, and price it against what the same thing actually sold for, not what people are asking. Clothes go on Vinted, furniture and anything heavy on Facebook Marketplace, an odd one-off on eBay as an auction with a low start.

instruction: I'm looking for online resources to help my child with math homework. Do you know of any good websites?
reply: Put the child's name and class in the subject, say what you have noticed and what you would like: "Sam (5B) has been anxious about maths homework — could we talk for ten minutes this week?" Keep it to a few lines and ask for a specific next step.

instruction: I'm feeling really burned out from work and I was wondering if you had any strategies for achieving a better work-life balance.
reply: Ask for a private twenty minutes and say it plainly in the first sentence: "I'm not coping with the current load and I want to sort it out before it shows in the work." Then bring two or three specifics - the tasks, the hours, what has slipped - and two things you want changed, because a manager can act on a proposal and rarely on a feeling. Ask what support exists: an employee assistance line, occupational health, flexible hours or a temporary reallocation.

instruction: I'm looking for a new herbal tea to try. What are some popular options?
reply: Nearly all of it is the same leaf at different levels of oxidation: green tea is dried before it can darken and tastes grassy, black tea is fully oxidised and malty, and oolong sits between them, roasted and floral. White tea is the young leaf barely processed, light and sweet, and pu-erh is aged and earthy, an acquired taste.

instruction: I'm going shopping and I need to make a list. What are some things I should have on my shopping list?
reply: A rug, a cool bag with a freezer block, plates and cups you do not mind losing, a bottle opener, napkins, a bin bag and water. Skip anything heavy with mayonnaise unless it is eaten within the hour: sausage rolls, cheese, fruit and a flask keep for hours.

instruction: I'm going to the mall this weekend and I'm worried about parking. Do you have any tips?
reply: Take the train into the centre: parking runs twenty to thirty pounds for a day, the congestion charge is on top of that, and then you are still looking for a space. Drive only if you are heading somewhere outside the centre or carrying things - and then park at a Tube or rail station on the edge and finish by train.

instruction: I'm looking for some home workout videos to help me get started with my fitness routine.
reply: Anything that gets you warm and out of breath counts, so pick the kind you will actually turn up for three times a week: brisk walking, cycling, swimming, stairs, dancing or a run-walk. Add two short strength sessions - squats or sit-to-stands, press-ups on the stairs or against the worktop, a row with a band or a loaded bag - because muscle is what keeps carrying and climbing easy.

instruction: I'm planning a ski trip and I'm worried there won't be enough snow. Do ski resorts make their own snow?
reply: Snow forms when water vapour freezes straight into ice crystals high in a cloud, and the crystals stick together as they fall. It only reaches the ground as snow if the air stays cold all the way down, which is why a cold snap often brings sleet instead.

instruction: I'm looking for a healthy snack option. What do you recommend?
reply: One moist thing and one with a bit of crunch or sharpness, and it stops being a sad sandwich: cheddar with apple and pickle, tuna with celery and a little mayo (drained, or the bread goes), hummus with grated carrot and cucumber, or leftover roast chicken with lettuce and mustard. Butter both slices to the edges first so the bread does not go soggy, and keep tomato or cucumber in the middle.

instruction: I'm a big fan of basketball. Who's the best basketball player of all time?
reply: Basketball is five a side over four quarters, and you score 2 points in the basket, 3 from behind the arc, and 1 from the free-throw line. You have to keep dribbling or pass — picking the ball up and walking with it is a travel.

instruction: I'm looking for ideas to create a family recipe book. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Three that work with children, easiest first: flapjack (no oven hands, just stirring and a flat tin), fairy cakes (they can fill the cases and ice them once cool) and shortbread (three ingredients, and cutting shapes is the fun part). Give the little ones the measuring and the stirring and keep the oven and the hob to yourself, and expect it to take twice as long as it would alone.

instruction: I'm looking for a new desk lamp for my home office. What are some popular types?
reply: Old-style filament and halogen bulbs are just glass and wire, so they go in the bin. The coiled low-energy ones hold a little mercury: take those to the tip or to a shop that sells them.

instruction: I'm thinking of making some home improvements, but I'm not sure if I should do it myself or hire a professional.
reply: Start with a free needs assessment from the council - it opens the door to home help, grab rails and a care package without you paying privately first. Then take the falls out of the house: rugs taped down, a light by the bed, a shower seat, a keysafe so help can get in.

instruction: I'm having trouble with my Language Arts homework. What is a simile?
reply: Explain it out loud to someone who does not know it, without notes. Where you stumble or reach for jargon is exactly what you do not understand yet, so go back to that bit and try again.

instruction: I'm looking for grocery delivery services in my area. Do you know of any?
reply: Look for the places that sell a lot of one thing: a market hall or a food court, a bakery, a cafe at the back of a shop, a street food van in a regular spot, or the lunch board outside a restaurant that wants the office trade. Walk a street back from the station or the main road, where the rents are lower, and follow the queue of people who work nearby.

instruction: I'm looking for a new job, but I'm not sure where to start.
reply: Try the smallest real version first: an evening course, one freelance job, or a sideways move inside your current employer. Talk to three people doing the job now and ask what the bad days are like, not the good ones.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to Paris. What's the best way to get around the city?
reply: Paris has about 2.1 million people inside the city limits, and about 11 million in the whole metro area - the city proper is small, and the suburbs are where most Parisians live.

instruction: I need help organizing a carpool for my kids' school. Do you have any tips?
reply: Nothing fancy for the first day: a named bag with a pencil case (two pens, a pencil, a rubber, a ruler), a water bottle, a packed lunch or the money loaded on the dinner account, and the PE kit the school asked for, in a bag of its own if they can. Label everything, including the coat and the shoes, and put the timetable in the front pocket.

instruction: I'm looking for comfortable clothes to wear while exercising. What's a good option?
reply: Cotton rather than polyester, because it breathes and you wake up less clammy: a t-shirt and shorts or loose pyjama bottoms is plenty, and socks if your feet get cold. A pair of shorts you'd answer the door in is worth having in the summer.

instruction: I'm looking for some new clothes, but I want to support brands that are good for the environment. Can you tell me about some eco-friendly fashion brands?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm looking for some ideas for break activities at work. Do you have any suggestions?
reply: Take the smallest break that is really a break, and take it today: twenty minutes out of the house without your phone, or a bath with the door shut while someone else does bedtime. Then lower the bar for the rest of the day - one meal, one wash, no craft - because a worn-out parent does not need a plan, they need an hour.

instruction: I'm looking for a new pair of jeans. What are the current styles?
reply: Smart jeans or trousers with a top you like is right for nearly any evening out, and a jacket you can take off covers a cold walk home and an over-hot bar. Wear shoes you can walk and stand in, and check the place's own rules if it's somewhere new, because plenty still say no trainers or sportswear.

instruction: I'm planning a trip to the Great Barrier Reef and I want to take some amazing underwater photos. What kind of camera do I need?
reply: Spend on the battery and the update years, not the camera: a mid-range phone at £250 to £400 lasts as long as a flagship if the maker promises four or five years of security updates (Samsung, Google and Apple do; many cheap brands promise two). Get at least 128GB, check the battery is 5,000mAh or more, and make sure it takes a physical SIM as well as an eSIM if you travel.
